SUMMARY: httpjet is a from-scratch Rust web server and drop-in LiteSpeed replacement: the same XML configuration, native HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, LSAPI PHP, .htaccess rewriting, reverse proxy and FastCGI gateways, and an opt-in origin page cache.

httpjet · documentation · v0.1.5

# httpjet

A from-scratch **Rust web server** that is a **drop-in LiteSpeed replacement**: it reads the same `conf/httpd_config.xml` tree, speaks native LSAPI to `lsphp`, evaluates the same `.htaccess` files, and adds native HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, reverse-proxy and FastCGI gateways, an opt-in LSCache-protocol page cache, optional ACME and OCSP, and a loopback admin API — all on one io_uring transport.

            resolve  SNI / Host → vhost
            acl  identity · throttle · geo · WAF
            rewrite  .htaccess · auth
            cache  lookup → hit?
            dispatch  ws · proxy · php · fcgi · static
            finalize  headers · compress
            store  cache write

       one pipeline per request, whatever the wire protocol — every page tells you where it sits on this rail

           Drop-in LiteSpeed XML config
           HTTP/1.1 · native HTTP/2 · HTTP/3
           Native LSAPI → lsphp · FastCGI
           Apache .htaccess · Basic auth
           Opt-in origin page cache
           ACME · OCSP · OTel (build features)

## What httpjet is

httpjet is a complete origin server on a memory-safe Rust core, built so that an existing LiteSpeed Web Server (LSWS 6.3.5 compatibility target) or OpenLiteSpeed deployment becomes an httpjet deployment by pointing `--root` at the tree it already has. Compatibility is the feature; everything httpjet adds on top is an explicit opt-in that LiteSpeed simply ignores.

#### Compatible surface

- LiteSpeed XML: server, tuning, listeners, vhosts, contexts, `mime.properties`

- Native LSAPI wire protocol to any LSAPI-capable `lsphp`

- mod_rewrite , access control, Basic auth, `Header`, `ErrorDocument`, LSCache directives

- LSCache protocol (`X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control` / `-Tag` / `-Vary` / `-Purge`)

- LiteSpeed `fileETag=28` ETags, `.html`→PHP dispatch order

#### httpjet-native (opt-in)

- Per-client throttle, GeoIP/ASN rules, PROXY protocol , Unix-socket listeners

- Weighted upstream groups with active health checks; `h2://` / `h2s://` upstreams; FastCGI

- Per-context body/timeout/bandwidth overrides, `sub_filter`, request decompression

- ACME HTTP-01/DNS-01, OCSP stapling , kTLS/sendfile, OpenTelemetry

- Loopback status + transactional config API , WAF sidecar , compile-time extensions

        i   Where it runs
httpjet serves WindowsForum.com on an x86_64 origin and MoonTimeNow.com + ThisDayInHistory.ai on an active ARM64 origin behind Cloudflare, over the pure io_uring transport with the page cache's file tier live. It is early-stage software (semantic version **0.1.5**, Rust 1.99.1+, edition 2024, GPL-3.0-only) built around these production deployments — test on alternate ports before trusting it elsewhere. See Capabilities & limits for the honest matrix.

## How the pieces fit

Every wire protocol lands in the same request pipeline. Click a node to jump to its page.

> [Diagram: pipeline] The request pipeline. pipeline::handle() resolves the vhost and the client's identity, then dispatch() mirrors OpenLiteSpeed's ordering with the WAF, extension, page-cache lookup and store seams inserted at fixed points. Each terminal finishes through finalize_response before the transforms run.

## By the numbers

Headline figures from the checked-in benchmark record — every number names its regime (see Performance for methodology and the raw CSVs).

          ~908 k rps   h2 static, dedicated-host loopback — vs OpenLiteSpeed's ~793k (2026-08-27)
          44.8 k rps   PHP/LSAPI over h1, PGO loopback — vs LiteSpeed's ~38.5k (2026-06)
          101 ×   cache hit vs full PHP render of the same page (19,912 vs 196 rps)
          146 /146   h2spec conformance on the native HTTP/2 stack, over TLS, three consecutive runs
          0.2 %   httpjet's share of production request latency — ~138 µs/req; PHP owns the rest
          3,000 +   test functions across 20 crates; full workspace suite green at v0.1.5

## Project status

| Aspect | State (2026-10-24) |

| Version | **0.1.5** — semantic versioning adopted 2026-09-17; MSRV Rust 1.99.1, edition 2024; dependencies current (0.1.x sweep: tokio 1.54, rustls 0.23.46, rustls-webpki 0.103.16 + webpki-roots 1.0.10, fancy-regex 0.20, parking_lot 0.13, zstd 0.14.3). |

| Configuration | LiteSpeed-compatible XML is the authority; httpjet-native directives are opt-in add-ons. `check --strict` is the deploy gate. |

| Transport | Pure io_uring (monoio) for H1/H2/H3 — the *only* transport; there is no epoll fallback and no Windows/macOS port. |

| PHP | Native LSAPI; the operator supplies `lsphp`. Production runs the persistent external pool with zero-downtime generation reloads. |

| Page cache | Off by default; LSCache-protocol opt-in, private tier, per-URL cookie vary, tmpfs file tier, per-vhost dictionaries, generation-scoped namespaces. Live in production. |

| Optional features | `acme`, `ocsp`, `otel`, `ktls`, `profiling` — build features that still need explicit runtime opt-in. |

| Security posture | Whole-codebase review rounds through 2026-10-23 landed, plus the October bug-bash campaign (rounds 1–16 across 0.0.6–0.1.1; see audit posture ); fail-closed defaults throughout. |

| Release | Source builds, generic systemd units, and a hardened OCI example. Signed public packages and a supported-platform matrix are still release work. |

==============================================================================
PAGE: Quickstart (https://httpjet.net/docs/quickstart)
SUMMARY: Build httpjet from source, validate a LiteSpeed-compatible configuration tree with check --strict, and serve it on loopback in ten minutes.
==============================================================================

# Quickstart

From a source checkout to a running origin in a few minutes: build the binary, validate a LiteSpeed-compatible tree with `check --strict`, serve it on loopback, and verify. httpjet reads the same `conf/httpd_config.xml` layout LiteSpeed uses, so an existing tree needs no migration step — but validate it first.

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Why |

| Linux with **io_uring** | The monoio/io_uring transport is the only transport. Container runtimes must allow `io_uring_setup`/`io_uring_enter`/`io_uring_register` (see OCI ). |

| **Rust 1.99.1+**, edition 2024 | The workspace MSRV. A C toolchain is needed for the aws-lc-rs crypto backend and mimalloc. |

| OpenSSL 3.x headers + pkg-config | Only for `--features ocsp`. |

| An LSAPI-capable `lsphp` | Only for PHP. Static, proxy and FastCGI deployments need no PHP and no LiteSpeed installation. |

        i   Release status
No signed binary packages are published yet; the source build below is the install path. The repository's PGO and deploy scripts are tailored to one production deployment — do not treat them as a general installer.

## 1 · Build the binary

            **build** · cargo

```
git clone https://github.com/faratech/httpjet.git
cd httpjet

# release build of just the binary crate (the workspace is large — always scope with -p)
cargo build --release -p httpjet        # → target/release/httpjet

# optional build features (each still needs explicit runtime opt-in):
cargo build --release -p httpjet --features acme,ocsp,otel
```

A debug build (`cargo build -p httpjet`) compiles faster but runs ~5× slower — fine for iteration, meaningless for any measurement. For reproducible results use `--locked`.

## 2 · Validate a configuration tree

httpjet is configured by a *server root* containing `conf/httpd_config.xml`, optional `conf/mime.properties`, and the per-vhost XML files it references. The checked-in `examples/litespeed/` tree is a minimal working example: one plain listener on `127.0.0.1:8080` and one static vhost (`example.test`) with scripting and symlinks off.

            **check** · config lint

```
# parse the tree and print a summary (check is also the default subcommand)
target/release/httpjet --root "$PWD/examples/litespeed" check

# strict: lint topology and exit non-zero on findings — the deploy gate
target/release/httpjet --root "$PWD/examples/litespeed" check --strict
```

`check --strict` hard-errors on a docroot shared by two vhosts, a vhost whose docroot is missing, and a vhost with no exact `vhostMap` domain; it warns on an apex mapped without its `www.` twin, TLS over a Unix socket, PROXY protocol on a public bind, geo rules without a database, ignored LiteSpeed anti-abuse elements, generic CGI contexts, and every other directive that would parse but do nothing. It also prints each vhost's fast-memo verdict (`fast_memo: eligible [vary: …]`) and a `vhost-map-fingerprint` for comparing check output over time. Always use an absolute `--root`.

        !   Parsed ≠ equivalent
httpjet accepts LiteSpeed XML leniently so real trees load. A warning means the directive is *not* enforced — review every one before assuming parity. The capability matrix lists what is implemented.

## 3 · Serve on loopback

The XML holds persistent policy; `serve` flags hold operational overrides (addresses, workers, PHP wiring, cache budgets). The example is HTTP-only, PHP-off and cache-off, so it is safe next to an existing server.

            **serve** · development

```
target/release/httpjet --root "$PWD/examples/litespeed" serve \
  --http-addr 127.0.0.1:8080 --https-addr "" \
  --workers 1 --no-php
```

To try TLS and HTTP/3, add a secure listener with `keyFile`/`certFile` to the XML, set ` 1 `, and pass `--https-addr 127.0.0.1:8443`; the same port must be reachable over TCP (h1/h2) and UDP (h3). See TLS, ACME & OCSP .

        !   Keep test state isolated
Use alternate HTTP/HTTPS/metrics/admin ports, a separate `--php-socket` if PHP is on, low `--php-children`, and a separate `--page-cache-store-path`. Never point a test instance at a production LSAPI socket — two supervisors on one socket corrupt each other's worker accounting. Test pools default their control and generation files *beside* their own socket for exactly this reason.

## 4 · Verify

            **verify** · curl

```
printf 'hello from httpjet\n' > examples/litespeed/example/public/index.html
curl -i -H 'Host: example.test' http://127.0.0.1:8080/

# h2c prior knowledge on the same plain port
curl -i --http2-prior-knowledge -H 'Host: example.test' http://127.0.0.1:8080/

# Prometheus metrics (loopback-only by design)
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9090/metrics | grep -E '^httpjet_(requests_total|active_connections)'
```

Expect a LiteSpeed-style ETag (`"size-mtime-inode;;;"`), `Vary: Accept-Encoding` on compressible bodies, and — once a listener is secure and QUIC is on — an `Alt-Svc` header advertising h3.

## 5 · Add PHP (optional)

With an LSAPI-capable `lsphp` configured in the XML (` ` or an `lsapi` `extProcessor` plus a `scriptHandler`), drop `--no-php` and let httpjet spawn its own pool on a private socket. For zero-downtime deploys, run the pool as a separate process instead:

            **two processes** · external pool

```
# terminal 1 — the persistent PHP pool
httpjet --root /abs/root lsphp --php-socket /run/httpjet-test/php.sock --php-children 4

# terminal 2 — the web tier dials it and never spawns lsphp itself
httpjet --root /abs/root serve --http-addr 127.0.0.1:8080 --https-addr "" \
  --lsphp-external /run/httpjet-test/php.sock \
  --lsphp-generation-file /run/httpjet-test/php.sock.generation
```

How the pool, the generation file and `lsphp-reload` fit together is on LSAPI & PHP .

## Where to go next

- Configuration — the XML reference, including the httpjet-native directives.

- CLI reference — every `serve` flag, grouped and filterable.

- Operations — systemd socket activation, the PHP pool, deploy gates and rollback.

- Page cache — enabling `--page-cache` safely.

- Migrating from LiteSpeed — the validation-first path for a real tree.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Architecture (https://httpjet.net/docs/architecture)
SUMMARY: The httpjet workspace: 19 hj-* library crates under one binary, the frozen hj-core contract, the io_uring transport bridge, the request pipeline, and configuration generations.
==============================================================================

# Architecture

httpjet is a Cargo workspace: **one binary crate** (`httpjet`) over **nineteen `hj-*` library crates**. The graph is acyclic, `hj-config` is the root, and `hj-core` is the small frozen seam every handler programs against. Two crates (`hj-acme`, `hj-ocsp`) only link in behind build features. Roughly 3,000 test functions span the workspace (3,019 green at v0.1.5).

## Workspace shape

Responsibilities are split so the contract a handler depends on stays tiny while transports, protocols, gateways and the cache evolve behind it. Three libraries are completely isolated — `hj-log`, `hj-geo` and `hj-cache` take no `hj-*` dependency — while `hj-rewrite` depends only on `hj-compress` so `.htaccess` and XML expiry directives share one `A/M` time grammar. `hj-pagecache` is transport-agnostic and builds on `hj-cache`'s sharded LRU; its request-aware glue lives in the binary.

           1 binary + 19 libraries
           Rust 1.99.1 · edition 2024 · v0.1.5
           Acyclic; hj-config at the root
           ≈3,000 test functions
           Vendored forks: monoio, monoio-rustls (real writev), dashmap, pprof

## Crate dependency graph

`hj-config` parses the LiteSpeed XML tree into one normalized model; `hj-core` re-exports it so every downstream crate imports the configuration model *through* core — one import surface, never inverted. The binary is the only crate that sees everything.

- hj-config XML tree → model · parse_bundle hj-core the frozen contract · ReqCtx · Router · budgets handlers & transports (depend on hj-core) hj-tls hj-h2 hj-lsapi hj-fastcgi hj-static hj-compress hj-proxy hj-acl hj-extension hj-http (ServeConfig) hj-pagecache (uses hj-cache) hj-cache sharded byte-LRU hj-acme · hj-ocsp --features acme / ocsp isolated (no hj-* deps) hj-rewrite hj-log hj-geo hj-cache httpjet uring transport · pipeline · lscache glue · admin config_transaction · resource_generation · waf · otel hj-config → hj-core → handlers/transports → the httpjet binary. Isolated crates converge at the binary; `hj-geo` feeds `hj-acl`'s `GeoRules`; the two feature-gated crates hang off `hj-tls`'s resolver handles. ## Crate map Crate Role hj-core Protocol-agnostic `Request`/`Response`/`Body`, `ReqCtx`, the vhost `Router`, shared budgets (`BodyBufferBudget` leases, `BandwidthThrottle`, `ResponseCompletion`, `body_deadline`), and `recycle` (`TieredPool` transient buffer and task pooling) — the seam every handler programs against. hj-config LiteSpeed XML → one normalized model (`$VAR` substitution, OLS-faithful value semantics, fail-closed defaults). `parse_bundle` is the in-memory variant used by the transactional API . hj-tls One rustls `ServerConfig` for TCP + QUIC: SNI resolver (no cert-name-match, like OLS), dual ECDSA/RSA chains, mTLS verifier with CRLs, generation-bound staple slots, certificate reload handles. hj-acme feature RFC 8555 HTTP-01/DNS-01 issuance and renewal (instant-acme), the 0700 `PrivateStore` with atomic snapshots, challenge registry, DNS webhook adapter with durable cleanup journal. hj-ocsp feature Bounded OCSP fetch + OpenSSL 3.x signature/issuer/freshness validation; status lifecycle with revocation enforcement. hj-http The shared `ServeConfig` connection-tuning struct derived from ` `. Its old hyper-H1/quinn-H3 adapters were removed when io_uring became the only transport. hj-h2 The **native HTTP/2 server**: one task per connection, send flow control, streaming bodies, one vectored write per wake, RFC 9113 validation, and the zero-allocation HPACK codec (`hj_h2::hpack`). hj-lsapi Native LSAPI wire codec (vendored `lsapidef.h` constants), UDS client pool with generation epochs, the `lsphp` supervisor and subreaper, the CGI env builder, and the fail-closed jail. hj-fastcgi Bounded FastCGI record codec, connection pool (poison-by-default), strict CGI response parser and streaming handler for explicit `fcgi`/`fastcgi` processors. hj-static Static files: `openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH)` resolution, `fileETag` ETags, conditional requests, single + multipart ranges, precompressed `.br`/`.gz` siblings, `Body::File` with pinned inodes for sendfile. hj-cache The shared `ShardedCache` byte-weighted LRU primitive and `CacheCaps` sizing (the former mmap file cache was removed — it had no consumers). hj-pagecache The **origin page store**: sharded byte-LRU index with W-TinyLFU admission, keys + vary + tags + TTL/stale windows, the LSCache header classifier, the HJPC file tier with boot scan, dictionary recompression, single teardown path. hj-compress gzip/brotli/zstd response encoders, server-priority negotiation, streaming `CompressStream`, per-thread zstd contexts, and the per-vhost `PageDictRegistry` the page cache uses for internal dedup. hj-rewrite Apache mod_rewrite / `.htaccess`: dense-DFA prefilter, linear-first regex with `fancy-regex` fallback, access control, scoped Basic auth, header ops, LSCache directives, memo-eligibility classification. hj-proxy Reverse proxy (h1, `h2://`, `h2s://`), upstream groups with weighted selection and active health checks, passive circuit breaker, WebSocket relay, SSE streaming, upstream mTLS. hj-acl Allow/deny ACLs with trusted-proxy (`T`) marking, real-IP resolution and anti-spoofing, the sharded per-IP throttle, and `GeoRules` (geo/ASN resolved to CIDR sets at state build). hj-geo Offline GeoIP/ASN sources: the CidrList text format and binary-search interval sets. No runtime fetches. hj-log Non-blocking access + error logging: common/combined/JSON access lines, text or JSON error events with redaction, size rolling with day pruning, the syslog tap. hj-extension `ExtensionRegistry` for compile-time pre-handlers and response transforms (the shipped registry is empty). httpjet The binary: listener planning and adoption, the `uring/` transport, `pipeline/`, `lscache/` glue, the fast-path memo, metrics, admin listeners, config transactions and resource generations, WAF client, OTel, PHP slow log, memory trim. ## Transport paths The pure io_uring transport is the only serving transport. There is no runtime switch and no `URING=0` rollback build; reverting is a rebuild from an older revision. One monoio runtime runs per inherited or self-bound `SO_REUSEPORT` listener fd, pinned to its core when the worker count equals the CPU count (`--no-core-pinning` is the kill switch). > [Diagram: transport] One transport, three protocols, one pipeline. Cheap work stays on the monoio core: the H1 codec, the native h2 task, the QUIC driver, and the on-core fast path (finished-response memo, static files, page-cache hits). Anything else crosses uring::bridge into the tokio runtime that owns ServerState, the LSAPI pool, the page cache and reload state, then returns to the monoio core for framing and writes. Bodies ≤ 256 KiB are buffered; larger ones stream on H1, H2 and H3 alike. Ring setup is tunable but deliberately plain: `--uring-ring legacy` (default) uses flagless rings because the measured `coop` and `defer` variants were noise or a ~2% loss on the virtualized production guest; ring size stays at the default because ring memory is memlock-charged. Multishot accept is on by default (`--no-multishot-accept` reverts to one SQE per connection). ## The frozen contract — hj-core This is the seam that lets handlers compose without knowing the transport. Changing these signatures means updating every dependent, so they are treated as frozen: **hj-core** · the seam ``` enum Body { Empty, Full(Bytes), Stream(BoxBody), File(FileBody) } type Request = http::Request ; type Response = http::Response ; // every terminal handler (StaticFiles, Lsapi, FastCgi, ProxyHandler) trait Handler { async fn handle(&self, &mut ReqCtx, Request) -> Result ; } // every post-handler munger (promote → expires → sub_filter → compress → deny-CDN-cache → Alt-Svc) trait ResponseTransform { async fn transform(&self, &ReqCtx, &mut Response); } ``` `FileBody` may carry an open descriptor that pins the selected inode across a concurrent cache version swap, recompression or unlink — that is what lets sendfile and the file tier coexist safely. `ReqCtx` carries the per-request state: `server`/`vhost` (Arcs of the pinned generation), `peer_ip`/`client_ip` (post-forwarding, or `peer_unix`), `is_tls`, `protocol`, `trusted_proxy`, and an `env` vec that holds rewrite `[E=]` sets *and* CGI overrides. `Router::resolve(listener, key)` maps SNI/Host to a vhost. i Extending without touching handle() New terminal handlers `impl Handler` and register in `pipeline/mod.rs::dispatch()`; new response munging `impl ResponseTransform` and is pushed into `state.rs::build_transforms`. Out-of-tree code uses the same traits through the compile-time extension registry . ## The request pipeline `pipeline::handle()` is the integration point: vhost resolution → mTLS trust boundary → client-IP/ACL/geo/throttle → optional WAF inspection → extension pre-handlers → `dispatch()` → response transforms → access log, metrics and spans. `dispatch()` mirrors OpenLiteSpeed's ordering with the page-cache seams inserted once rewrite and access state are known: The terminals are intentionally *not* a uniform matcher registry. Their predicates differ (request headers for WebSocket, URI prefix for proxy contexts, script-path split for suffix routing), their fall-through rules differ, and their post-processing differs, so an explicit `if/return` chain keeps the security-relevant ordering legible. Two fall-throughs matter: a proxy context that cannot resolve its ext-processor falls through to static, while a script whose handler has no pool **hard-fails 503 and must never fall through** — falling through would serve the raw PHP source. ! Load-bearing detail A rewrite to `index.php` keeps the **original** `REQUEST_URI`: the resolved script is pinned separately via the `LsapiScript` request extension, with `SCRIPT_NAME`/`QUERY_STRING` pushed into `ctx.env`. That is what makes XenForo-style front-controller routing correct — and why the page cache must key by the *original* URI, never the rewrite-resolved path. The cache seams are inert unless `serve` runs with `--page-cache`: `lscache::cache_lookup` runs after rewrite/ACL but before any backend (a hit short-circuits dispatch), and `lscache::cache_store` runs after `finalize_response` at each terminal return. Both key off a single `CacheCtx` built once per dispatch. ## Module organization Path Contents `crates/httpjet/src/uring/` The transport: `mod.rs` (accept loops, sniff, TLS), `codec.rs` (H1), `h3.rs` (QUIC driver), `bridge.rs`, `ktls.rs` + `ktls_policy.rs`, `proxy_protocol.rs`, `request_body.rs` (decompression), `worker_group.rs` (listener generations). `crates/httpjet/src/pipeline/` `mod.rs` (`handle`/`dispatch`/`finalize_response`), `rewrite_glue`, `proxy_glue` (incl. `ProxyHandler`), `htaccess_apply`, `suffix_routing`, `scoped_auth`, `fast_memo`, `response_util`, and the in-file e2e/security regression tests. `crates/httpjet/src/lscache/` `mod.rs` (`CacheCtx`, `cache_lookup`/`cache_store`), `hit.rs` (hit-response construction + precompress), `singleflight.rs`. `crates/httpjet/src/{admin*,config_transaction,resource_generation,serving_generation,listener_plan,tcp_candidate}.rs` The read-only status API, the authenticated write API, the publication coordinator, and the listener/resource generation model behind SIGHUP and transactional reloads. `crates/httpjet/src/{acme_runtime,ocsp_runtime,otel,waf,extensions,metrics,telemetry,phpslow,memtrim}.rs` Feature runtimes and observability. `crates/hj-h2/src/server/` `state`/`recv`/`send` + `serve()`; HPACK is the `hpack` submodule. `crates/hj-rewrite/src/` `rules/{parse,eval}`, `htaccess/{parse,mod_access,auth_scope,cache,php,scope_index}`, `auth.rs` (htpasswd). `crates/hj-lsapi/src/` `proto/{frame,builder}`, `pool.rs`, `supervisor`, and the security-critical `jail`. ## Configuration generations Live state is published as immutable *generations* behind an `ArcSwap`. A SIGHUP or an API transaction builds a complete candidate (config, rewrite caches, health schedulers) with background work inactive, validates it, then publishes it atomically under one coordinator; requests already in flight finish on the generation they pinned at acceptance. > [Diagram: generations] Candidate → published → retired. A rejected candidate never touches the serving generation. Trust changes (TLS material, mTLS policy, PROXY protocol) retire the old listener group and drain its connections under their pinned policy; boot-owned resources (listener topology, PHP pools, cache stores, privileges) are restart_required. The full ownership inventory and the transactional replacement sequence are on Admin API & reload . ## Code conventions **Formatting:** rustfmt-clean (default settings, edition 2024); `cargo fmt --all --check` is a CI gate.

- **Errors:** `thiserror` types at system boundaries; internal invariant violations panic with a message rather than pretending to recover.

- **unsafe:** rare, and never in HPACK. The real sites are `hj-h2`'s pin projection and writev/iovec plumbing, the validated fixed-size mmaps in `hj-pagecache/diskstore.rs` and `hj-lsapi/pool.rs`, and small libc shims — each with its safety invariant documented above the block.

- **Async:** tokio tasks for independent work, `FuturesUnordered` for multiplexing with coordinated shutdown, no per-stream spawn on hot paths.

- **Hashing:** `rustc-hash` only for internal maps keyed by trusted values (h2 stream ids); anything keyed by untrusted input keeps SipHash.

- **Allocator & pooling:** mimalloc globally, with a background `mi_collect` trim that only runs above an RSS threshold (`--mimalloc-trim-*`). Because production sets `MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0` so freed pages return to the OS immediately, transient per-request buffers and task boxes are pooled in `hj_core::recycle` (`Recycled ` and `BODY_BUFS` `TieredPool >`) and per-core TLS write pools to keep steady-state page faults at zero.

> [Diagram: recycle-pools] Zero-fault buffer and task recycling (v0.1.2–v0.1.5). Under MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0, unpooled transient allocations in sparse size classes fault back in on every request. hj_core::recycle pools H2 stream futures, bridge futures, tiered body buffers (frozen into ref-counted Bytes via Bytes::from_owner and returned when the last slice drops), LSAPI read/BEGIN buffers, and per-core 64 KiB TLS record buffers.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Capabilities & limits (https://httpjet.net/docs/capabilities)
SUMMARY: What httpjet supports today, what is optional behind build features, what is deliberately unsupported, and the fixed operational bounds.
==============================================================================

# Capabilities & limits

What the current source tree does, what it does only behind a build feature, what is a tested subset, and what is deliberately unsupported. **Supported** means an implemented, tested code path — not directive-for-directive parity with LiteSpeed, NGINX, Apache or Caddy. Optional features stay off unless explicitly enabled at build *and* at runtime.

        supported  implemented + tested
        optional  build feature + runtime opt-in
        partial  tested subset — review the boundary
        unsupported  deliberate, documented

## Capability matrix

| Area | Status | Scope and important limits |

| HTTP/1.1 | supported | Keep-alive, pipelining, chunked bodies; strict framing; configured header/URL/body/timeout/request-count limits; 103 Early Hints; single + multipart ranges; `CONNECT` answered 405. → |

| HTTP/2 | supported | Native TLS h2 and h2c prior knowledge; flow-controlled buffered, file and streaming responses; h2spec 146/146. No server push; no `Upgrade: h2c`. → |

| HTTP/3 | supported | QUIC over UDP through the same pipeline; TCP *and* UDP HTTPS ports must both be published. Connection migration disabled. → |

| TLS | supported | rustls (aws-lc-rs) TLS 1.2/1.3, SNI, ALPN, dual ECDSA+RSA chains, certificate reload, optional/required client certificates, CRLs. → |

| Automatic certificates | optional | HTTP-01 and DNS-01 behind `--features acme` + CLI opt-in. One managed account/identifier set per process; DNS-01 needs an operator-supplied webhook controller. → |

| OCSP stapling | optional | `--features ocsp`, OpenSSL 3.x, an explicit responder that covers every issuer. Not for CAs that retired OCSP (Let's Encrypt). → |

| kTLS / sendfile | partial | Plain-TCP H1 file bodies use `sendfile(2)` always; a `--features ktls` build adds TLS 1.3 H1 sendfile only when `--ktls=auto` finds a physical NIC with active `tls-hw-tx-offload`. H2/H3/UDS/TLS 1.2 keep userspace paths. → |

| Virtual hosts | supported | Listener + exact Host/SNI maps, OLS wildcard domain patterns (`*.example.test` and `example.*` with exact > longest-match precedence), and a bare `*` fallback. |

| Static content | supported | Conditional requests, LiteSpeed ETags, ranges, in-memory small-file promotion, precompressed `.br`/`.gz` siblings, traversal-safe opens. → |

| Reverse proxy | supported | HTTP/1 upstreams plus explicit `h2://`/`h2s://`; request/response streaming, SSE; upstream mTLS. → |

| WebSocket | partial | HTTP/1 upgrade and raw relay. Relay does not support TLS, H2 or Unix-socket upstreams. → |

| Upstream groups | supported | Primary-first, smooth weighted round-robin, weighted least-active, passive breaker, optional connect/GET/HEAD probes. No automatic replay of unsafe requests. → |

| PHP / LSAPI | supported | Native LSAPI; owned pool or separately supervised external pool with generation tracking and candidate-first reload. → |

| FastCGI | supported opt-in | Explicit `fcgi`/`fastcgi` processor + suffix routing over TCP or Unix sockets; the app is externally supervised; bodies buffered. → |

| CGI execution, uWSGI | unsupported | Design contracts exist; nothing is routable. A `cgi` handler without an explicit FastCGI processor fails closed (never serves source). → |

| Rewrites & `.htaccess` | partial | Common rewrite, access, auth, header (`set`/`append`/`add`/`merge`/`unset`/`setifempty`), expiry (`ExpiresActive`/`ExpiresDefault`/`ExpiresByType`), cache and env directives. `Header edit` and `RequestHeader` are ignored. Run `check --strict`. → |

| Compression | supported | Dynamic gzip/brotli/zstd + precompressed siblings. Gzip *request* decoding on by default; brotli/zstd request decoding opt-in and bounded. → |

| Origin page cache | supported opt-in | Public/private tiers, vary (including per-URL cookie vary), purge tags, stale policies, single flight, admission, RAM/file tiers, dictionaries, restart scan, generation-scoped keys. A first-class route-level *microcache policy* is specified, not implemented. → |

| Access controls | supported | Peer ACLs, trusted-proxy client IP, GeoIP/ASN CIDR rules, per-IP rate limit, body limits, Basic auth (bcrypt, APR1 `$apr1$`, MD5-crypt `$1$` and `{SHA}` htpasswd in constant time; bcrypt cost capped at 14, files confined to the docroot). → |

| WAF | external opt-in | Bounded request-inspection sidecar over Unix socket (peer-UID verified) or loopback TCP, fail-closed by default. No embedded ModSecurity/CRS engine. → |

| Logs and metrics | supported | Combined or JSON access logs, text or JSON error logs with redaction, syslog tap, Prometheus text metrics, request ids, telemetry TSV, PHP slow log. → |

| OpenTelemetry | optional | OTLP traces and metrics behind `--features otel` + `HTTPJET_OTEL=1`. Bounded queues; no payload export. → |

| Runtime APIs | opt-in | Loopback read-only status API; separately authenticated transactional config API. Boot-owned resources stay restart-required. → |

| Extensions | compile-time only | Trusted Rust crates register read-only pre-handlers and response transforms. No dynamic ABI, no in-process sandbox. → |

| Deployment | examples | Generic systemd units (socket activation, boot gate, PHP pool) and a hardened OCI example that still needs an io_uring-permitting runtime. → |

## Deliberately unsupported or deferred

- **Generic CGI process execution and uWSGI** are not routable; their fail-closed design gates are documented. FastCGI, LSAPI or HTTP proxying cover application paths.

- **HTTP/2 server push** is not implemented — use `Link` preload plus 103 Early Hints.

- **HTTP trailers** (inbound h2/h3 trailing HEADERS, chunked trailers) are discarded and not forwarded through gateways. LSAPI has no trailer concept.

- **h2c is prior-knowledge only**; the HTTP/1.1 `Upgrade: h2c` handshake was removed by RFC 9113 and is not implemented.

- **QUIC connection migration** is disabled: listener steering does not yet preserve connection ownership across an address change.

- **No epoll/tokio transport fallback**, no Windows/macOS. Linux io_uring is mandatory.

- **No native dynamic-module ABI.** Untrusted inspection belongs behind the bounded sidecar contract.

- **LiteSpeed anti-abuse elements** (`lsrecaptcha`, `censorshipControl`, permission masks, `cgiRlimit`) are parsed and warned about, never enforced.

- **Legacy crypt and plaintext htpasswd schemes** (traditional DES, `$5$`/`$6$` `crypt()`, and plaintext entries) verify *false* with a parse-time warning — use bcrypt (`htpasswd -B`), APR1 (`$apr1$`), MD5-crypt (`$1$`) or `{SHA}`.

- **Cross-node cache peers** (`--cache-peer`, peer fill/purge fan-out) were removed in August 2026; the loopback purge and readiness endpoints remain.

- **Multipath QUIC** was assessed and deferred (June 2026).

## Build-time feature gates

The default binary includes the serving engine, LSAPI, FastCGI, proxy, cache, logging, metrics, the WAF sidecar client and an empty extension registry. These features add dependencies and require an explicit build — and still nothing happens until the matching runtime switch is set:

| Cargo feature | Adds | Runtime opt-in |

| `acme` | `hj-acme`: HTTP-01 / DNS-01 issuance and renewal | `--acme-directory … --acme-domains … --acme-store … --acme-accept-terms` |

| `ocsp` | `hj-ocsp`: fetch, validate, staple (OpenSSL 3.x) | `--ocsp-responder URL` (+ `--ocsp-required`) |

| `otel` | OTLP HTTP/protobuf tracing and metrics exporters | `HTTPJET_OTEL=1` (+ `HTTPJET_OTEL_METRICS=1`) |

| `profiling` | Loopback pprof CPU profile endpoint | `--profile-token` policy; loopback only regardless |

| `ktls` | Kernel TLS on the io_uring TLS path | `--ktls=auto|on|off`; `auto` requires a physical NIC with `tls-hw-tx-offload` |

| `allocount` | Allocation-measurement harness | Diagnostic builds only |

## Operational bounds

Request limits come from the LiteSpeed ` ` block and per-context overrides; inspect the effective values with `check --strict` and `serve --help`. Fixed or separately configured bounds worth knowing:

| Bound | Value |

| Page-cache single object | 100 MiB — larger responses serve uncached |

| Page-cache budgets | Independent index (`--page-cache-mem`), file tier (`--page-cache-disk-mem`), hot tier (`--page-cache-hot-mem`), object TTL and stale-window caps; persistent files need an integrity key (`--page-cache-integrity-key`; loaded through a private-file validator — single link, owner root or the serving uid, no group/other bits — with `--page-cache-integrity-required` to refuse booting the file tier without one) |

| Bridge buffering | Bodies ≤ 256 KiB buffered, larger streamed (H1/H2/H3) |

| Request body budget | Process-wide byte budget with leases; usage, capacity and rejections exported as `httpjet_body_buffer_*` |

| Request decompression | 16 MiB decoded ceiling; 17 MiB codec workspace reservation for br/zstd; zstd window ≤ 2 24 |

| Multipart ranges | 8 ranges / 8 MiB of part bytes, else a full 200 |

| `.htaccess` chain depth | 64 directories, then a deny-all sentinel |

| sub_filter buffering | 4 MiB default (`subFilterMaxBody`); beyond it the stream passes through raw |

| WAF sidecar | Body ≤ 1 MiB inspected (`--waf-body-max`), total timeout ≤ 30 s, concurrency ≤ 4096, 4 KiB response head, 64 MiB process-wide serialization budget |

| Admin APIs | Read: 4 KiB/32 header fields, 4 connections, 5 s deadlines, 1 MiB response. Write: 8 KiB/32 fields, 1 MiB body, ≤128 vhosts, ≤64 XML nesting, 4 connections, one candidate build, 5 s lock / 10 s wait |

| Active health probes | Intervals/timeouts 1 s–1 h, rise/fall 1–100, process-wide cap of 16 concurrent probes |

| FastCGI | 65,535-byte records; separately bounded PARAMS aggregate, response head, STDERR, body buffering, pool size and deadlines |

| ACME | 1–100 identifiers, ≤128 live challenges, 1 MiB snapshots and CA bodies, 120 s per attempt |

| OCSP | ≤128 identities, ≤4 concurrent fetches, 64 KiB responses, 7-day staple validity cap |

| OpenTelemetry | 2048 queued spans + one 256-span batch, 1 s interval, 2 s export timeout, 3 s shutdown bound |

| Loopback-only endpoints | `/__hj_cache_purge`, `/__hj_cache_ready` (raw loopback peer), metrics `:9090`, admin listeners |

Defaults are starting points, not sizing recommendations. Worker count, open-file limit, body budget, cache caps, PHP/backend concurrency and health/WAF timeouts must be sized together for the deployment.

## Reload boundary (summary)

SIGHUP and the transactional API replace application state without dropping in-flight requests: vhost maps, rewrites, document roots, contexts, reloadable request settings, TLS material on an unchanged listener topology, and the trust policy of an already-enabled QUIC endpoint. Listener addresses/roles, QUIC enablement, Unix-listener topology, PHP topology, cache-store identity, process user/namespace policy and other boot-owned resources are **restart-required**; the write API says so instead of partially applying. Details: Admin API & reload .

## Reproducible checks

           **verify the tree** · what CI runs
```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --locked -p httpjet --bin httpjet
cargo run --locked -p httpjet -- --root "$PWD/examples/litespeed" check --strict
cargo test --locked --workspace
```

Protocol, cache, ACME, OCSP, OTel, FastCGI, WAF, admin and OCI pages carry their narrower acceptance commands. Every test uses synthetic configuration, temporary files and ephemeral loopback ports.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Protocol stacks (https://httpjet.net/docs/protocols)
SUMMARY: HTTP/1.1, native HTTP/2 with zero-allocation HPACK, HTTP/3 over QUIC, sendfile and kTLS egress, PROXY protocol, and Unix-socket listeners on one io_uring transport.
==============================================================================

# Protocol stacks

httpjet speaks **HTTP/1.1**, a **from-scratch native HTTP/2** stack, and **HTTP/3 over QUIC** through one unconditional **io_uring / monoio** transport. TCP and QUIC converge behind one rustls configuration, every protocol hands requests to the same pipeline, and file bodies leave over `sendfile(2)` where the kernel allows it.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## Overview

All serving lives in the binary's `uring/` module. HTTP/1.1 is a custom monoio + `httparse` codec; HTTP/2 and cleartext h2c use the native `hj-h2` stack through its monoio serve path; HTTP/3 is `uring/h3.rs`, a `quinn-proto` QUIC loop over io_uring UDP with `quinn-udp` socket metadata (GSO/GRO). Protocol selection happens at the connection boundary: ALPN over TLS, a non-destructive preface sniff in cleartext, and QUIC on the UDP listener.

> [Diagram: connection-lifecycle] A TCP connection's life. PROXY-protocol stripping (if the listener opts in) happens before the TLS handshake or the cleartext sniff, so every later stage sees the proxied client as the peer. ALPN picks the TLS stack; the 24-byte h2 preface picks the cleartext one. H2 connections drain with GOAWAY on shutdown.

           HTTP/1.1 · custom monoio codec
           HTTP/2 · native `hj-h2`
           h2c · prior-knowledge sniff
           HTTP/3 · `quinn-proto` on io_uring
           HPACK · RFC 7541, zero-alloc
           TLS · rustls / aws-lc-rs · optional kTLS

## Connection front doors

Two per-listener features sit before protocol detection. Both are httpjet-native — LiteSpeed has no listener-level equivalent — and both change *who httpjet thinks the client is*.

### PROXY protocol v2 / v1

A listener with ` 1 ` requires every connection to open with a PROXY header. The header is consumed and the claimed client address installed before the TLS handshake on secure listeners and before the H1/h2c discriminator on plain ones. Missing header → the connection is closed (fail-closed both ways). Since 2026-09-16 a header that claims a loopback or unspecified source is **refused at the parser**: those addresses feed the mTLS exemption and the loopback purge gate, so accepting them would let a proxy hop forge local trust.

        !   The listener opt-in is the trust decision
Unlike OpenLiteSpeed's server-level trusted-peer ACL, httpjet binds PROXY trust to the listener (nginx/HAProxy semantics). Enabling it on an internet-facing bind lets anyone forge their client address; `check` warns on wildcard or public binds. Point such a listener only at your load balancer or a local hop.

### HTTP over Unix sockets

A listener whose address is `unix:/path/sock` (or `uds:`), or the `--http-uds` flag, serves plain HTTP over a Unix-domain socket: H1 and h2c prior knowledge, one accept core (SO_REUSEPORT does not exist for AF_UNIX), socket mode 0600 group-writable, socket-activated fds adopted by path. A stale socket file is unlinked only after a `connect(2)` proves it dead, and cleanup is bound to the owned directory and socket identity. Peers have no address: ACLs, the per-IP throttle and `REMOTE_ADDR` see a fabricated loopback value and the access log renders `unix:`. TLS over UDS is unsupported and linted.

## HTTP/1.1 & h2c detection

The H1 codec parses with `httparse`, enforces strict framing (single `Content-Length`, conflicting-length rejection, bounded incomplete reads), supports keep-alive and pipelining, honors `maxKeepAliveReq` (0 or 1 disables keep-alive, matching OpenLiteSpeed), decodes chunked bodies, and streams large responses from the bridge without buffering. Request-body deadlines extend on forward progress up to an absolute ceiling, while response egress enforces a minimum send-progress rate. Since the 2026-10-06 review it also enforces the RFC 9112 request-target and Host rules at intake: only origin-form targets (plus `*` for OPTIONS) and http/https absolute-form (reduced to origin-form, its authority replacing `Host`); `CONNECT` answers **405**, authority-form and a raw `#` answer 400. HTTP/1.1 **requires `Host`**, and any Host must be UTF-8 and pass the same authority validation the h2/h3 `:authority` rule uses (HTTP/1.0 may omit it). A header line terminated by a bare LF is rejected 400 before the head is materialized, and refusals that leave request bytes unread perform a lingering close so the peer reads the error status cleanly.

Cleartext HTTP/2 by prior knowledge has no upgrade handshake — the client simply sends the connection preface. httpjet detects it *non-destructively*: the bytes already read are handed to whichever stack wins, so h1 and h2 both parse the connection as if no router sat in front.

            **uring** · ALPN + cleartext routing

```
// over TLS: ALPN decides the TCP stack
match alpn {
    b"h2"       => hj_h2::server::serve_local_with_prefix(io, prefix, service, cfg).await,
    _           => handle_h1_bridged(io, prefix, service).await,   // http/1.1 or none
}

// cleartext: sniff the 24-byte preface, pass the observed bytes along
match sniff_cleartext(&mut stream).await? {
    Proto::Http2(prefix) => hj_h2::server::serve_local_with_prefix(stream, prefix, service, cfg).await,
    Proto::Http1(prefix) => handle_h1_bridged(stream, prefix, service).await,
}
```

Beyond framing, the H1 path implements the newer semantics end to end:

- **103 Early Hints** — the same preload/preconnect `Link` matcher the h2 stack uses emits an interim `103` on h1 (batched into the same write as the final head when both are ready); `101` upgrades bypass it; canonical/alternate links are excluded.

- **Ranges, single and multipart** — RFC 9110 multi-range sets are parsed, clamped, coalesced and framed as `multipart/byteranges`, capped at 8 ranges / 8 MiB of part bytes with a full-200 fallback. An invalid component poisons the whole header (→ 200); an unsatisfiable set is 416.

- **Request decompression** — gzip bodies decode by default; brotli/zstd opt in with `--request-decompression-extra`. Bounded and buffered; see Compression .

- **Bandwidth pacing** — a per-connection token bucket (burst 2× rate) paces `Body::Full` as 64 KiB slices and streams per chunk when `bandwidthLimit` is set; a matched context overrides the server-wide rate.

- **Explicit `CONNECT` rejection** (405) and stalled-sendfile backoff with a 60 s zero-progress bound.

## Native HTTP/2

`hj-h2` is httpjet's own HTTP/2 server. Every h2 connection — ALPN `h2` over TLS and cleartext h2c — lands here through the monoio local serve path. The design targets the CDN→origin shape: few long-lived connections, many concurrent streams, so it optimizes one connection's multiplexing rather than spreading work across many.

- TLS conn ALPN h2 / h2c ONE connection task FuturesUnordered⟨stream⟩ stream 1 · handler stream 2 · handler … stream N HPACK enc / dec send flow control · deadlines one vectored writev / wake wire zero-copy Bytes bridge dispatch → shared pipeline → monoio writes One connection task multiplexes every stream and emits a single vectored write per wake. Handlers cross the bridge into the shared pipeline; framing stays on the monoio core. **One task per connection.** All streams multiplex through `FuturesUnordered`; a 100-stream connection costs one task.

- **Send-side flow control** honors per-stream and connection windows; **frame, header-block and body deadlines** are enforced on the monoio loop, and a stalled response stream waiting on withheld flow-control credit that delivers under 16 KiB per `connTimeout` window is reset with `RST_STREAM(CANCEL)`.

- **Streaming bodies** — LSAPI, proxy, SSE and async file bodies stream without buffering; the response-completion hook keeps spans open through the final flush.

- **One vectored write per wake**; large bodies are zero-copy from page-cache `Bytes`. The vendored `monoio-rustls` fork adds a real `writev`, flushes all queued TLS records in one socket write, and pools per-record buffers per core so records do not page-fault.

- **Inbound RFC 9113 validation** with graceful GOAWAY drain; `CONTINUATION` without an open header block and stream-id reuse are connection errors; over-cap decoded header blocks become a **stream error** (`RST_STREAM(REFUSED_STREAM)`, decoding the block with emission suppressed so the HPACK dynamic table stays in sync on pooled CDN connections); the time-refilled rapid-reset budget (`httpjet_h2_rapid_reset_drops_total`), HTTP/2 Bomb pattern (CVE-2026-49975) and no-forward-progress cases are bounded.

- **Egress pacing** is per connection at the OutQueue flush with the server-wide rate (a per-response override is ill-defined under multiplexing). HTTP/3 is not paced.

        ⎁   Measured
The native stack passes **146 of 146** h2spec 2.6.0 cases over TLS (three consecutive runs is the gate). h2c is informative-only: generic §3.5/2 is structurally unsatisfiable on a port that also sniffs HTTP/1.1, so it records 145/146 with that one documented exception.
 scripts/h2spec_check.sh · scripts/ci-h2spec.py

## HPACK

Header compression is RFC 7541 HPACK, implemented as the `hpack` submodule of `hj-h2` (once a standalone crate, folded in so the codec and the connection state evolve together). It is **zero-allocation** — fields are decoded and encoded by slicing frame bytes in place — and pure safe Rust with `#![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]`. Both the decoder and the round-trip are fuzz targets ( Conformance ).

## HTTP/3 & QUIC

HTTP/3 is `uring/h3.rs`: `quinn-proto` for QUIC state, `quinn-udp` for socket metadata (with a live GSO segment cap and QUIC DATAGRAM disabled), UDP driven from monoio/io_uring, incremental request-stream parsing, QPACK encode/decode (charging decoded head bytes to both `total_req_bytes` and the global body budget), and the same bridge into the pipeline. Small, cached and sub-threshold bodies are buffered and sent whole; large, SSE and proxy bodies stream — HEADERS goes out immediately and DATA follows as the backend produces it, with backpressured writeback and send-stall stream resets (`httpjet_h3_send_stall_resets_total`). Retained response memory is bounded per connection (2026-09-06). The process-wide connection budget (shared with TCP accepts) is charged at `Connected` — after address validation — so spoofed Initials cannot hold budget for the idle timeout; until then a connection costs only one of 256 per-core handshake slots, and once 64 connections on a core are handshaking an unvalidated Initial receives a stateless **Retry** (token-bearing Initials are still accepted). A full budget closes with `H3_EXCESSIVE_LOAD`; handshakes are closed after 10 s.

Discovery is via **Alt-Svc** on TLS responses (the last response transform), so an h2 client learns it can upgrade to QUIC. Connection migration is disabled because listener steering does not yet preserve ownership across an address change. Each connection pins its trust generation and mTLS requirement at acceptance; a trust reload replaces quinn's server configuration only for future handshakes while the bound UDP workers and established connection IDs survive.

> [Diagram: h3-admission] HTTP/3 UDP intake, anti-amplification and stream admission. Unvalidated Initial packets pass through per-core handshake slot caps (256 max, stateless Retry above 64 concurrent handshakes) before charging the process-wide maxConnections budget at Connected. Decoded QPACK headers charge both total_req_bytes and BodyBufferBudget.

        !   Publish UDP too
The same numeric HTTPS port must be reachable over TCP (h1/h2) *and* UDP (h3). Publishing `8443/tcp` alone means no HTTP/3, and the Alt-Svc header will advertise a port clients cannot reach.

## File egress: sendfile & kTLS

An uncached `Body::File` keeps its pinned inode and byte range across the tokio→monoio bridge. On **plain TCP HTTP/1** it is sent with bounded nonblocking `sendfile(2)`; unsupported descriptor/filesystem combinations resume at the exact offset with positional io_uring reads, and short files or client aborts close the connection rather than completing an incorrect `Content-Length`. A stalled sendfile backs off exponentially and gives up after 60 s of zero progress.

A `--features ktls` build extends this to **TLS 1.3 H1**: after the rustls handshake the socket is upgraded to kernel TLS, so the same sendfile writer feeds ciphertext without a userspace AEAD copy. A peer KeyUpdate queued during a transfer is applied before the next response writes, fencing TX rekey from sendfile. Policy is `--ktls=auto|on|off`: `auto` (default in feature builds) resolves the IPv4 default-route interface, reads its driver and features via ethtool ioctls, refuses known virtual NICs, and enables kTLS only when `tls-hw-tx-offload` is active — otherwise it logs one reason and stays on rustls. TLS 1.2, H2, H3 and UDS keep their userspace paths.

        ⎁   Measured
Plaintext sendfile: 5,000 × 1 MiB at c=50 → **4,852 req/s**, 10.08 ms mean, zero failures. Software kTLS on a virtual GVE NIC (offload `off [fixed]`): **2,999.7 req/s off vs 2,944.9 on** — the expected-negative result that is why `auto` refuses virtual NICs.
 loopback · 2026-09-09 · `bench-results/httpjet-sendfile-*.csv`, `httpjet-ktls-sendfile-*.csv`

## TLS in one paragraph

`hj-tls` builds **one** `rustls::ServerConfig` for TCP and QUIC with aws-lc-rs as the crypto provider. SNI maps directly to configured chains (no cert-name-match, like OLS), with dual ECDSA+RSA chains per name; client verification is optional mTLS against the *listener* CA with CRL enforcement; TLS 1.3 offers exactly `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`; resumption uses single-use tickets with 0-RTT off. Certificates, ACME and OCSP have their own page: TLS, ACME & OCSP .

==============================================================================
PAGE: TLS, ACME & OCSP (https://httpjet.net/docs/certificates)
SUMMARY: Certificate selection, mutual TLS with CRLs, resumption policy, opt-in ACME HTTP-01 and DNS-01 issuance, and opt-in OCSP stapling.
==============================================================================

# TLS, ACME & OCSP

How httpjet selects certificates, verifies clients, and resumes sessions — plus the two opt-in certificate services: **ACME** issuance and renewal (HTTP-01 and DNS-01, `--features acme`) and **OCSP stapling** (`--features ocsp`). Both are default-off at build *and* runtime, and both publish into the same generation-bound resolver slots that file-based certificates and SIGHUP use.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## TLS configuration

`hj-tls` builds **one** `rustls::ServerConfig` for TCP *and* QUIC via `build_server_config_alpn(cfg, listener, alpn)`, on the aws-lc-rs provider. A certificate rotation, verifier change or CRL update therefore lands on both transports at once.

| Listener XML | Meaning |

| `secure`, `keyFile`, `certFile` | The listener's default identity (PEM). `certChain=1` appends `CACertFile` as the served chain. |

| per-vhost ` ` | The SNI identity for that vhost's domains — server *chain* material, never a client-verify root. Configure an ECDSA and an RSA pair for the same names to serve modern clients the smaller chain (ECDSA is chosen when the client offers ECDSA signature algorithms). |

| `clientVerify` 0–3, `CACertFile`, `verifyDepth` | Mutual TLS: 0 none · 1 optional · 2 required · 3 optional without CA check. The verifier is built from the **listener** CA only. Positive chain verdicts are memoized off the hot path. |

| `crlFile` httpjet | PEM CRL or bundle enforced by the webpki verifier. Absent = no revocation checking. Loaded at config build; rotating means a reload of the trust generation. |

| `enableStapling` | Parsed for compatibility; OCSP fetching needs the `ocsp` feature and `--ocsp-responder` (see below). `check` says so. |

### Handshake posture

- **SNI without cert-name-match** — the SNI name maps directly to configured material, mirroring OpenLiteSpeed; there is no re-validation that the leaf's SANs match the SNI. Managed ACME identities are exact-SNI overlays and do not replace the no-SNI listener fallback.

- **TLS 1.3 offers exactly `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`** (the RFC 8446 mandatory suite); TLS 1.2 keeps its full set. rustls negotiates by client order, and without this pin OpenSSL-family clients pick slower suites; the transcript moves to hardware SHA-NI.

- **Resumption & certified-peer idle window** — single-use TLS 1.3 tickets, 0-RTT off, including on client-cert-verifying listeners. Cloudflare does not re-offer origin tickets, so `httpjet_tls_handshakes_resumed_total` stays low behind it. Ticket volume is tunable with `--tls-session-tickets` (rustls default 2); production mints **0** — each ticket was two extra handshake records plus a cached copy of CF's client-cert chain for a resumption that never comes. Instead, `--trusted-proxy-idle-secs` extends the idle window for connections that presented a verified client certificate (reducing full handshakes per request by 28% on x86 and 78% on ARM in production). Resumption is *disabled* whenever OCSP is enabled (status must be enforced per handshake).

- **mTLS trust boundary** — on a listener with `clientVerify=2`, a plaintext request for an mTLS-protected vhost is refused from the request head unless it arrives from loopback; `--no-mtls` relaxes the requirement for local testing only.

- **Reload** — file-based certificates reload through `CertReloadHandle` on SIGHUP or via the write API ; a failed reload keeps the certificates whose reload failed. kTLS templates apply to new handshakes only.

        !   Two CAs, two roles
A per-vhost `CACertFile` is chain material sent *to* clients. The listener `CACertFile` is the root that verifies *client* certificates. Treating the vhost chain CA as a client-verify root would silently widen the mTLS trust boundary; httpjet keeps them distinct.

## ACME certificate automation --features acme

Build with `cargo build --locked -p httpjet --features acme`. The manager is *native CLI*, not pretend LiteSpeed XML: nothing happens unless all four required flags are present. One manager, account and identifier set is supported per process; its domain and TLS/HTTP vhost mappings are boot-frozen.

          HTTP-01  DNS-01 / wildcard  Local test CA

               **serve** · HTTP-01
```
httpjet --root /abs/root serve … \
  --acme-directory https://YOUR-CA/directory \
  --acme-domains example.test,www.example.test \
  --acme-store /abs/private/acme \      # pre-created, mode 0700, owned by the service uid
  --acme-accept-terms \
  --acme-bootstrap                      # only for first issuance without a configured certificate
```

Requires public TCP port 80 and an enabled TLS listener. The raw challenge route `/.well-known/acme-challenge/ ` runs before URI normalization, redirects, rewrites, auth, cache and backends; only plaintext GET on the validated authority answers (404 for unknown tokens, 405 otherwise, always `Cache-Control: no-store`); tokens are redacted in the access log. No exemption is granted for forwarded-scheme headers, and the historical path-prefix bypass (#259) stays closed.

               **serve** · DNS-01
```
httpjet --root /abs/root serve … \
  --acme-directory https://YOUR-CA/directory \
  --acme-domains 'example.test,*.example.test' \   # quote the wildcard
  --acme-store /abs/private/acme --acme-accept-terms \
  --acme-dns-webhook https://YOUR-CONTROLLER/acme \
  --acme-dns-zones example.test \
  --acme-dns-token-file /abs/private/dns-controller.token   # regular file, 0600, 16..4096 printable chars
```

No port 80 requirement and no HTTP challenge exemption. There is **no built-in Cloudflare or provider integration**: you run a controller that implements the webhook contract below with a credential scoped to the listed zones. A managed wildcard matches exactly one leftmost label — request the apex separately.

               **controller contract** · POST, Bearer token, application/json
```
{"version":1,"operation":"present","name":"_acme-challenge.example.test","value":" "}
{"version":1,"operation":"ready",  "name":"…","value":"…"}   → {"ok":true,"ready":true|false}
{"version":1,"operation":"cleanup","name":"…","value":"…"}   → {"ok":true}
```

Operations must be idempotent: `present` adds the exact value without replacing the RRset; `cleanup` removes only that value and succeeds if it is already absent (apex and wildcard share one owner name). Replies over 16 KiB, redirects, non-2xx and unexpected fields are rejected; each call has a 5 s deadline; a `ready:true` returned without real DNS visibility is not a valid production implementation.

`--acme-test-mode` permits literal-loopback HTTP directories and alternate HTTP ports and requires loopback serving addresses. `--acme-test-ca-root` and `--acme-test-issuer-root` replace trust roots without disabling verification; `--acme-dns-test-root` does the same for the DNS controller. These are for the Pebble fixture only:

               **acceptance** · Pebble v2.10.1
```
cargo test --locked -p hj-acme
cargo build --locked -p httpjet --features acme
python3 -B scripts/acme-pebble-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet \
  --pebble /path/to/pebble --dns /path/to/pebble-challtestsrv \
  --pebble-source /path/to/pebble-v2.10.1 --bootstrap [--dns01]
```

### Issuance, recovery and activation

> [Diagram: acme-http01] HTTP-01 issuance. Every durable step precedes the network step that depends on it: the account key before registration, the certificate key and CSR before finalize, and the issued pair in the same atomic snapshot as account/order state. Only a fully validated pair is published to the TLS resolvers.

- **Durable before network.** A lost `newOrder` response is intrinsically ambiguous, so a marker stops automatic reissuance: recover the order URL from the CA's account records and restart once with `--acme-reconcile-order `. Never delete the store as a generic retry.

- **Bounded CA traffic.** Only GET/HEAD/POST at the directory's origin, no redirects, no environment proxies, 1 MiB bodies, 5 s connect / 10 s request, 120 s per attempt, persisted exponential backoff with account jitter plus `Retry-After`.

- **Private store.** An operator-provisioned 0700 directory owned by the effective uid; every ancestor is checked with pinned no-follow descriptors; an exclusive lock prevents two managers sharing a store; snapshots are 0600 single-link regular files written pending→fsync→rename→dirsync, capped at 1 MiB; an unfinished pending file is discarded on reopen, never promoted.

- **Activation.** The validated `CertifiedKey` is published to the TCP, kTLS and QUIC resolver overlays as an exact-SNI identity. File-based SIGHUP updates a separate slot and cannot erase or mix managed generations. Boot revalidates the persisted pair; an expired one is rejected and needs operator recovery.

- **Bootstrap.** With `--acme-bootstrap` the default TLS identity starts *absent*: handshakes for hosts without a configured certificate fail until issuance succeeds. No self-signed placeholder is generated; client-auth policy is unchanged.

- **Renewal** is scheduled with one third of the remaining lifetime in reserve plus jitter.

> [Diagram: acme-dns01] DNS-01 with durable cleanup. The exact owner/value cleanup intent is journaled before any DNS mutation, so a failed, cancelled or timed-out presentation is always recoverable; cleanup replays after attempts, at shutdown and at startup, and blocks new issuance until it succeeds. Snapshots bind cleanup to the provider endpoint and sorted zone scope — changing those while reusing the store fails closed.

Scope today: DNS identifiers only (ASCII A-labels), one account/group per process, same-origin ACME endpoints, no EAB, contact management or ARI. Production at windowsforum.com still renews through certbot; the manager is an adoption path, not a forced replacement.

## OCSP stapling --features ocsp

Build with `--features ocsp` (OpenSSL 3.x development headers and pkg-config at build time, the shared libraries at runtime). Pass `--ocsp-responder https://ocsp.example.net/status` to `serve`, optionally with `--ocsp-required`. The explicit CLI opt-in applies to every certificate on the process's TLS listeners regardless of the XML `enableStapling` boolean, and the one responder must serve every enabled issuer (per-issuer routing is not implemented).

        !   Not for Let's Encrypt
Let's Encrypt retired its OCSP service on 2025-08-06 and publishes CRLs instead. There is no responder to fetch from — do not enable this manager for current Let's Encrypt certificates. It exists for other CAs.

> [Diagram: ocsp-policy] Status lifecycle. Fetching never happens during a handshake. A verified GOOD response fills a generation-bound staple slot and is refreshed before expiry with jitter; a verified REVOKED result suppresses that leaf's handshakes even across a same-leaf reload; malformed or transient failures preserve a still-valid staple and otherwise fall to the optional/required policy.

- **Trust.** Each managed leaf must include its immediate issuer in the configured chain; responses must be signed by that issuer or a responder it directly authorizes for OCSP signing. Arbitrary trusted-root responders, unsigned responses, AIA fetching, redirects, encoded bodies and verification-bypass flags are all refused. SHA-256 CertIDs; RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 and ECDSA signatures with SHA-256/384/512.

- **Freshness.** `thisUpdate`, `producedAt` and `nextUpdate` are required; a staple is never valid past seven days from `thisUpdate` or the leaf/issuer/responder validity; expiry uses wall *and* monotonic time so a clock step back cannot extend a staple.

- **Transport.** Percent-encoded GET when the full URL is ≤ 255 bytes, else binary POST; DNS pinned per fetch; private destinations rejected except literal loopback under `--ocsp-test-mode`.

- **Policy.** Optional (default): cold or expired status serves without a staple unless the certificate has Must-Staple. Required: new handshakes are rejected until a valid response arrives — including at startup and for new certificate generations, so plan availability. Status is memory-only and resets on restart.

           **acceptance** · real-server fixtures on isolated listeners
```
cargo test --locked -p hj-ocsp
cargo test --locked -p hj-tls --features ocsp ocsp
cargo build --locked -p httpjet --features acme,ocsp
python3 -B scripts/ocsp-runtime-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet            # required policy
python3 -B scripts/ocsp-runtime-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet --optional
python3 -B scripts/ocsp-runtime-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet --optional --must-staple
```

## Kernel TLS

The staged `--ktls` path (feature `ktls`) upgrades a completed TLS 1.3 rustls handshake to kernel TLS so H1 file bodies leave through `sendfile(2)`. It is hardware-aware and off on virtual NICs by default; see Protocol stacks → File egress for the policy and the measured (negative-on-GVE) receipt.

==============================================================================
PAGE: LSAPI & PHP (https://httpjet.net/docs/lsapi)
SUMMARY: The native LSAPI wire codec, the lsphp supervisor, the zero-downtime external pool with generation tracking, the CGI environment, and the fail-closed jail.
==============================================================================

# LSAPI & PHP

httpjet speaks the **native LSAPI wire protocol** to an operator-configured `lsphp` executable — no FastCGI shim, no translation layer. `hj-lsapi` holds the wire codec, a generation-aware UDS client pool, the `lsphp` supervisor, the CGI environment builder, and a fail-closed jail. The production shape is a **persistent external pool** so the web tier restarts without cold-starting PHP.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## Overview

When suffix routing maps a request to a PHP handler (` ` or an `lsapi` `extProcessor` bound by a `scriptHandler`, or a `.htaccess` `SetHandler application/x-httpd-php`), httpjet talks LSAPI directly to `lsphp`. PHP is optional: static, proxy and FastCGI deployments need no LSAPI executable.

- client HTTP/1·2·3 HTTP httpjet LSAPI handler · CGI env LSAPI · UDS lsphp pool — capped by --php-children / maxConns php #1 php #2 … php #N streamed response · php-slow log · lsapi_ttfb histogram Native LSAPI over a Unix socket. The pool may be owned by the web process (spawn mode) or run as a separate `httpjet lsphp` process (external mode, the production shape). Native LSAPI · vendored `lsapidef.h` Operator-supplied `lsphp` Generation-tracked UDS pool Candidate-first zero-downtime reload Fail-closed jail ## The LSAPI wire codec `proto/{frame,builder}` implement the protocol straight from the vendored php-src `lsapidef.h` constants (BSD-3-Clause), so frames match byte-for-byte what `lsphp` reads. One sharp edge deserves stating precisely: every env key/value and known header value is length-prefixed with a big-endian `u16` that **includes the trailing NUL**, so the largest safe field is `u16::MAX − 1` bytes. A longer field would wrap the prefix and desync `lsphp`'s parser for every subsequent frame; the builder rejects it. **proto** · the NUL-inclusive length prefix ``` // each env/header field: [u16 BE = byte_len + 1] [bytes…] [0x00] const MAX_FIELD: usize = (u16::MAX as usize) - 1; // 65534 ``` The response-header parser is one of the eight fuzz targets (`lsapi_resp_header`). Request bodies are scanned before transmission and refused if they embed an `lsphp` `BEGIN_REQUEST` frame signature, negative env counts are rejected at the builder, and the repository ships a verified `packaging/lsphp/lsapilib-hardening.patch` for upstream `lsapilib.c`. If a worker dies before emitting an `LSAPI_RESP_END` packet, the response body is aborted rather than silently truncated. Inbound tracing context reaches PHP as `HTTP_TRACEPARENT` in the unknown-header table when OpenTelemetry is on. ## The UDS connection pool Requests reach `lsphp` over a Unix-domain socket fronted by a pool that carries a **generation epoch**. In owned mode the epoch is process-local; in external mode it is the 16-byte generation file below, mapped read-only. A bodyless idempotent request whose pooled connection dies before the send gets one transparent retry on a *fresh* dial, bounded by the processor's `retryTimeout`. A fresh-dial `EAGAIN` under backlog pressure is retried and counted (`httpjet_lsapi_eagain_*`). Accepted connections keep TCP keepalive so a vanished client cannot pin pool permits. Attribution is what makes generation retirement safe: for every connection the pool identifies the accepting worker through `UNIX_DIAG` peer-inode lookup plus `/proc`, pins it with a pidfd, and — after the response completes — retires a stale-generation worker through that pidfd rather than by pid (workers call `setsid()` and are not reliably in the master's tree). Failures to attribute are counted, never guessed. Metric Meaning `httpjet_lsapi_generation_advances_total` Epoch advances this web process observed. `httpjet_lsapi_stale_idle_drops_total` / `_stale_checked_out_drops_total` Idle sockets discarded / checked-out sockets refused re-pooling after an advance. `httpjet_lsapi_stale_worker_retire_signals_total` / `_failures_total` Old-generation workers retired via pinned pidfd after their response completed / signals that failed. `httpjet_lsapi_worker_attribution_failures_total` Connections whose worker could not be pinned. `httpjet_lsapi_acquire_seconds` · `_dispatch_seconds` · `_ttfb_seconds` Pool contention · backend call time · request-committed-to-first-byte (worker pickup + render start). ## The lsphp supervisor In spawn mode (`serve` without `--lsphp-external`) `hj-lsapi` spawns and supervises `lsphp` itself: the listen socket is passed on **fd 0**, inherited socket-activation listeners are kept out of PHP children via `FD_CLOEXEC` and `close_range(..., CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC)`, `setsid()` detaches the pool from any controlling terminal, `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` ties a worker's life to its parent, and the `pre_exec` closure between fork and exec calls only async-signal-safe syscalls. The process is a subreaper (reaping all adopted PHP orphan zombies) and tracks each generation family by an injected `LSAPI_Z_HTTPJET_GENERATION_MARKER` plus pidfds. The config's `LSAPI_CHILDREN` env is stripped so `--php-children` / `maxConns` is the only cap (values below 2 normalize to 2). Two refusals are unconditional (2026-09-16): the supervisor **never runs workers as root** (resolve_credentials rejects uid/gid 0 even if suEXEC would compute it) and **refuses to spawn a setuid `lsphp` binary**. `--php-max-process-time-ms` sets a total per-request deadline: exceeded → 504. In spawn mode the monitor also kills and restarts the worker; under `--lsphp-external` there is no monitor in the web process, so only the 504 applies and a wedged worker is not auto-reclaimed here — keep the value conservative. ! Packaging boundary httpjet ships no PHP runtime. The executable, its extensions, `php.ini`, opcache settings and writable application paths are operator-managed. For the pool unit's sandboxing the repository ships a **validated hardening runbook** (`systemd/httpjet-lsphp.service.d/hardening.conf`: a bounded capability set, the standard Protect*/Restrict* family, and `MemoryDenyWriteExecute=no` because opcache JIT needs RWX, with the opcache helper steps run via `+`-prefixed ExecStartPre/Reload) — validated against a live pool, but not applied by any unit by default; adopting it is the operator's call. ## Zero-downtime deploys: the external pool Spawn mode couples PHP's lifetime to the web process — a binary deploy cold-starts opcache. The `httpjet lsphp` subcommand instead runs a **persistent pool as its own systemd unit** (`httpjet-lsphp.service`, `Type=notify`, socket-activated through `httpjet-lsphp.socket`); the web tier dials it with `serve --lsphp-external --lsphp-generation-file ` and never spawns workers itself. Both halves then deploy independently: #### Web tier deploy `systemctl restart httpjet`
- systemd holds the :80/:443 fds — no RST for new or queued connections
- PHP workers and opcache stay warm

#### PHP recycle

- `systemctl reload httpjet-lsphp` → `httpjet lsphp-reload`
- candidate-first: a new family must answer a real, marker-attributed LSAPI request before promotion
- the systemd-owned listener is never closed; queued dials survive

> [Diagram: lsphp-reload] Candidate-first generation reload. The supervisor promotes a new family only after a marker-attributed response, then advances the shared 16-byte epoch. Web pools observe the epoch, drop idle sockets, and retire each in-flight stale worker only after its response completes, through a pidfd pinned before the epoch moved. The old family is drained with bounded forced cleanup.

           external pool wiring (see  Operations  for the units)
```
# the PHP half — its own unit, its own identity
httpjet --root /abs/root lsphp --php-socket /run/httpjet/php.sock --php-children 256 \
  --control-socket /run/httpjet/lsphp-control.sock \
  --generation-file /run/httpjet/lsphp.generation

# the serving half — dial, never spawn; restart freely
httpjet --root /abs/root serve … --lsphp-external /run/httpjet/php.sock \
  --lsphp-generation-file /run/httpjet/lsphp.generation

# opcache/PHP recycle without dropping the listener
httpjet lsphp-reload --control-socket /run/httpjet/lsphp-control.sock --timeout-secs 90
```

        !   The generation file is the trust anchor
The 16-byte file (epoch + promoted-family marker fingerprint) is how a web tier tells *its* pool from a foreign one. Supplying `--lsphp-generation-file` is fail-closed: startup aborts if it is missing or malformed. Its parent directory must not be group/other-writable. Test pools default their control and generation files *beside their own socket* so they can never advance the production epoch — which would drop the live web tier's pooled connections and retire its workers against a foreign marker.

        !   Never restart the socket unit during a reload
`httpjet-lsphp.socket` is the continuity boundary: keeping it open preserves the listener inode and its 8192-deep accept queue. Replace the supervisor by restarting only `httpjet-lsphp.service`; it reapplies the XML backlog to the inherited fd with `listen(2)`. Verify with `stat` of the socket inode before/after, a 16-byte generation file, and `ss -xln` Send-Q = 8192; `LIVE=1 scripts/lsphp-reload-test.sh` is the live gate.

## The CGI environment

The env builder assembles the CGI/LSAPI environment per request. The load-bearing split is *what was requested* vs *what runs*: the `LsapiScript` request extension pins a resolved `SCRIPT_FILENAME` while the **original** `REQUEST_URI` is kept, with `SCRIPT_NAME`/`QUERY_STRING` pushed into `ctx.env` and upserted over the builder's defaults. That is what makes front-controller routing (every page → `/index.php`) correct.

| Variable | What it holds |

| `REQUEST_URI` | The original request URI, preserved through rewrites. |

| `SCRIPT_FILENAME` / `SCRIPT_NAME` | The resolved on-disk script and its URI-space name. |

| `REMOTE_ADDR`, `SERVER_NAME`, `HTTPS`, `CONTENT_LENGTH`, `HTTP_AUTHORIZATION`, `PHP_VALUE`, `PHP_ADMIN_VALUE`, … | Server-computed or special-env only. Since 2026-09-16 a `.htaccess` `[E=…]`/`SetEnv` or processor `env` entry that names one of these is **denied** (shared deny-list with FastCGI) — a directory cannot override the server's view of the client or inject PHP ini overrides through the regular environment. |

| `HTTP_*` | Request headers after name/value validation, under one forwarding rule (2026-10-06, applied identically to the CGI env table, the LSAPI wire header block and FastCGI params): the `Proxy` header and underscore-named headers never pass, and forwarding-authority names (`CF-Connecting-IP`, `X-Forwarded-*`, `X-Real-IP`, `True-Client-IP`, `Forwarded`) pass only from a peer that is *both* a trusted proxy and — on a client-cert listener — presented one. `HTTP_TRACEPARENT` when OTel is enabled. |

| `REMOTE_USER` | Set by a successful Basic auth realm. |

| special-env section | `php_value` / `php_admin_value` / `php_flag` / `php_admin_flag` from `.htaccess`, carried on the LSAPI special-env wire path with the right permission level — plain `lsphp` ignores a regular CGI `PHP_VALUE`. |

## The jail

PHP execution is fenced by a config-gated jail — suEXEC (` ` with `uidMin`/`gidMin` floors), chroot (`chrootMode` 0–2, per-vhost `chrootPath`) and optional Linux namespaces (`mount`, `net`, `uts`, `ipc`; `pid` is accepted but deliberately not honored). Resolution has two outcomes and no third:

- suEXEC off, non-root process, or no per-vhost isolation → the **all-None** case: the default `"php"` pool, single-pool behavior preserved byte-for-byte.

- A configured jail that turns out unsafe — uid 0, a uid below the floor, a bad chroot, an out-of-range `setUIDMode`/`chrootMode` (hard error since 2026-09-16), or a chroot without credentials to run inside it (hard error since 0.0.5) → httpjet **disables PHP for that vhost and returns 503**. It never runs unjailed, and it never falls through to the static handler.

        !   Source-disclosure guard
A script that resolves to a PHP handler is identified as PHP even when no pool can serve it. Falling through to static would hand back the raw `.php` source, so an unavailable pool is a 503, always. Operators sharing one pool across vhosts should read the "shared PHP trust boundary" note in the repository's security docs: workers in one pool share credentials, so per-vhost isolation is a suEXEC decision, not a default.

## Request bodies

LSAPI needs a concrete `m_reqBodyLen` before the body is sent, so chunked / no-`Content-Length` uploads are collected first. `collect_to_cap` enforces the effective `maxReqBodySize` *as frames arrive* — the instant the accumulated size would exceed the cap it returns `PayloadTooLarge` (413) — and every buffered byte is charged to the process-wide body budget through an owned lease that is released on completion or on connection teardown (H2/H3 teardown leaks were closed in the 2026-09-06 review).

        ⎁   Measured
PHP/LSAPI over HTTP/1.1: **~44.8k req/s vs LiteSpeed's ~38.5k at c=40** on the same hardware (LiteSpeed's best, ~41.2k, needed c=60). In production the render inside PHP is ~90% of request wall time; pool acquire is p99.9  loopback · PGO · 2026-06 · production telemetry 2026-08-30

==============================================================================
PAGE: Proxy & gateways (https://httpjet.net/docs/gateways)
SUMMARY: Reverse proxy over h1/h2/h2s, weighted upstream groups with active health checks, WebSocket and SSE relay, and the opt-in FastCGI gateway.
==============================================================================
