# Proxy & gateways

Everything that hands a request to another process: the **reverse proxy** (HTTP/1, `h2://`, `h2s://`) with **weighted upstream groups and active health checks**, **WebSocket** and **SSE** relay, and the opt-in **FastCGI** gateway. LSAPI/PHP has its own page . Generic CGI execution and uWSGI are specified but deliberately not routable.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## How a request reaches a backend

Three routes select a gateway, in dispatch order: a **WebSocket map** (` `) when the request carries an upgrade, a **proxy ``** whose URI prefix matches and whose `handler` names a `proxy` extProcessor, and a **rewrite `[P]`** target (deferred so it can still participate in the page cache). Script suffixes (`scriptHandler`) route to LSAPI or FastCGI. A proxy context that cannot resolve its processor falls through to static; a script handler that cannot resolve its pool hard-fails 503.

| Target form | Protocol to the backend |

| `host:port`, `ip:port`, `uds:///path`, `http://…` | HTTP/1.1 with keep-alive pools |

| `https://…` | HTTP/1.1 over TLS; backend certificate verified; optional client cert (`clientCertFile`/`clientKeyFile`) |

| `h2://host:port` httpjet | HTTP/2 prior knowledge (cleartext); multiplexes requests on one backend connection |

| `h2s://host[:443]` httpjet | HTTP/2 over TLS, ALPN fail-closed |

Pool keys are scheme-scoped, so an h1 and an h2 target at the same address never share a connection. Forwarded requests to h2 upstreams are re-absolutized (the h2 client derives `:scheme`/`:authority` from the URI). Proxied *responses* may not assert `X-LiteSpeed-Purge`/`-Cache-Control`/`-Vary` — those are stripped so a remote backend cannot inject cache policy. Named upstreams receive a W3C `traceparent` when tracing is on.

        !   [P] targets are screened
Since 2026-09-16 a rewrite `[P]` URL that resolves (after DNS — `/etc/hosts` pins cannot bypass the screen, and concurrent DNS lookups are bounded so slow resolvers fail fast) to loopback, link-local or a Unix socket is refused unless it matches an operator-configured extProcessor address. Forwarding to a foreign `[P]` origin also withholds client `Authorization` and `Cookie` headers. This closes the class where a `.htaccess` author reaches the local trust plane (metrics, admin, purge endpoints) or leaks origin credentials through the server.

## Upstream groups & selection

An `extProcessor` with several ` ` children is a group. Without the options below it keeps **ordered primary/failover** behavior with a passive circuit breaker (3 consecutive dial failures mark a peer bad; one successful dial clears it — nginx `max_fails` semantics). With them it becomes a load-balanced group:

           **httpd_config.xml** · a weighted group with active probes
```

   application
   proxy
   127.0.0.1:9001
   127.0.0.1:9002
   weighted-round-robin

   2,1

     GET

/ready application.internal 10 2 2 3 200 ``` > [Diagram: proxy-selection] Selection. Eligibility is the intersection of active health and the passive breaker; the policy then picks among eligible peers. A pre-head dial failure marks the peer and moves to the next eligible one; nothing replays a request body that has already been sent. > [Diagram: upstream-health] Peer states. A health-enabled peer starts cold (ineligible) until rise consecutive successes; fall failures take it down; probe success restores it without user traffic. Passive breaker state is independent. All-ineligible → 503. - **Policies:** `primary-first` (default), `weighted-round-robin` (smooth WRR), `weighted-least-active` (active ÷ weight, smooth-WRR tie-break). These options on non-proxy processors, unknown policies and invalid health settings fail config loading rather than silently falling back. - **Probes:** `connect` tests transport only; `GET`/`HEAD` use the configured protocol, validate TLS, bound the response head, compare the status exactly, follow no redirects, consume no body, and carry no cookies, authorization or body. Dedicated connections, a process-wide cap of 16 concurrent probes, skipped missed ticks; they never consume application pool permits. - **All peers in a group share a protocol**; do not put credentials, paths or queries in group authorities. A `Host` override does not override TLS identity. - **Reloads:** candidate generations start no probe tasks; publication starts the new scheduler and retires the old one. Unchanged identities keep their group state; changed endpoints, weights, policies or TLS identities start fresh. Server- and vhost-scoped processors are distinct. - **Reservations** survive the response head: streaming bodies and WebSocket relays release the peer's active count on completion, error or drop. Per-peer metrics carry scope, group name and ordinal labels (never URLs or credentials): `httpjet_proxy_peer_{healthy,probes_total,health_transitions_total,active_requests,selections_total,prehead_failures_total}`, plus `httpjet_proxy_failover_total` and the `httpjet_phase_upstream_seconds` latency histogram. The read-only status API exposes the same peer health.

## Streaming, SSE and timeouts

Upstream responses are **never buffered** (`respBuffer` is parsed but always streams — `check` warns). Server-sent events therefore stay real-time through compression (the per-chunk `CompressStream`) and through H1, H2 and H3 alike. A backend connect timeout is `initTimeout`; the response-head deadline is the processor's default or a context's `responseTimeout` override; a backend timeout is a 504. Request bodies stream to h1/h2 upstreams; a context `maxReqBodySize` is enforced before dispatch.

## WebSocket relay

A ` ` map (`uri` → `address`) or an upgrade request on a proxy context performs the HTTP/1 handshake with the backend and then relays raw frames both ways. The relay supports **plain TCP HTTP/1 upstreams only** — not TLS, H2 or Unix-socket targets. Maps carry a stable `websocket: ` target identity scoped to their vhost, so named-target trace propagation applies; the client span covers the handshake, not the potentially unbounded relay. TCP keepalive keeps a vanished peer from pinning fds and permits forever.

## FastCGI gateway opt-in

An external processor declared ` fcgi ` or `fastcgi` is an `ExtKind::FastCgi` — never silently converted into an HTTP proxy or an LSAPI worker. Only an explicit `cgi` script handler whose named processor is FastCGI dispatches through the gateway; a `cgi` mapping with a missing or different processor **fails closed** and is never served as static source. httpjet does not spawn the application: it connects to the configured TCP or Unix endpoint of an independently supervised process.

           **vhost XML** · FastCGI suffix routing
```

   my_fcgi
   fcgi
   uds:///run/my-app/fcgi.sock
   32
   5

30 fcgi cgi my_fcgi ``` > [Diagram: fastcgi-flow] One request through hj-fastcgi. The pipeline hands over an already-validated script target; the gateway never derives an executable path from the URI. Connections are poisoned by default and only a clean, exact END_REQUEST makes one reusable. Multiplexing request ids on one connection is disabled. - **Wire bounds:** FastCGI version 1, nonzero request id, known record types, the protocol's 65,535-byte record limit; PARAMS lengths are rejected before allocation when either the field bound or the configured aggregate cap would be exceeded. - **Pool:** caps all sockets including idle and in-progress dials under one acquisition deadline; poison/drop releases capacity immediately; clean idle sockets expire oldest-first. - **CGI variables** are server-derived; request headers become `HTTP_*` after validation; processor `env` cannot override protected identity/routing variables (`SCRIPT_FILENAME`, `DOCUMENT_ROOT`, `REMOTE_ADDR`, `SERVER_NAME`, `CONTENT_LENGTH`, `HTTP_AUTHORIZATION`, …). The same deny-list applies to `.htaccess` `[E=]` for LSAPI. - **Bodies** are buffered under the shared budget so the exact STDIN length is known; declared underflow/overflow, framing errors and cancellation poison the connection. - **Responses:** strict CRLF head, repeated end-to-end headers preserved, one valid `Status`, CGI `Location` default, folding rejected, app hop-by-hop headers and origin cache-control headers (`X-LiteSpeed-*`) stripped, and streams that end without an `END_REQUEST` frame abort the body; STDERR is byte-capped and control-escaped into the error log, never the client. Known follow-ups: explicit CGI context-directory routing (today: script-handler suffix mappings only), a codec fragmentation corpus, and a maintained real-application interoperability fixture.

## Conventional CGI and uWSGI not routable

Both remain disabled by design until a demonstrated workload exists. Existing `type=cgi`, `rails`, `appserver` and unknown processor types never activate either; `check --strict` keeps warning for configured CGI contexts. The design contracts are strict on purpose: CGI would require an absolute execution root distinct from the docroot, a fixed non-root identity, wall/CPU/memory/process/output limits, an executable allowlist, direct `execve` with no shell or PATH lookup, inode pinning, and bounded pipes with process-group termination; uWSGI would be a separate crate over an explicit endpoint with modifier-0 packets only, no multiplexing, and no connection reuse until a maintained responder proves the response boundary. Proposed identities are `type=cgi-exec` and `type=uwsgi`.

## Reproducible checks

           **tests** · loopback fixtures only
```
cargo test --locked -p hj-config -p hj-proxy
cargo test --locked -p hj-proxy --test upstream_groups     # h1/h2 weighted distribution, cold start, down/recovery, all-down 503
cargo test -p hj-fastcgi                                    # synthetic loopback responder + clean-connection reuse
cargo test -p httpjet --bin httpjet
```

To return a group to legacy selection, remove `loadBalancePolicy`, `addressWeights` and `healthCheck` and reload; removing only the health check keeps the configured policy.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Rewrite & .htaccess (https://httpjet.net/docs/rewrite)
SUMMARY: The Apache mod_rewrite engine: per-directory loading, the dense-DFA prefilter, directives and flags, access control, Basic auth, header operations, and the fast-path memo.
==============================================================================

# Rewrite engine & .htaccess

`hj-rewrite` is httpjet's Apache **mod_rewrite** / `.htaccess` engine — depending only on `hj-compress` so `.htaccess` and XML expiry directives share one `A/M` time grammar. It prefers a linear-time regex engine and falls back to **`fancy-regex`** only for the lookaround and backreferences real `.htaccess` files use. The same crate enforces per-directory access control, scoped Basic auth, header operations, expiry rules and the LSCache directives.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## Overview

The rewrite stage runs the vhost's inline ` ` rules first, then the `.htaccess` chain for the resolved directory — OpenLiteSpeed's order. One entry point, `evaluate()`, returns exactly one outcome per pass: `Rewritten`, `Redirect`, `Proxy`, `Forbidden`, `Gone` or `Unchanged`.

> [Diagram: rewrite-eval] One evaluation pass. A rewrite that crosses into another directory reloads the destination chain and evaluates again; a terminal flag stops the walk; an exhausted chain returns Unchanged and dispatch falls through to suffix routing.

## Per-directory loading

An `HtaccessCache` loads each directory's file (name from `accessFileName`, default `.htaccess`; bare file names only — `/` and `..` are rejected) with **mtime invalidation**, so an edit takes effect on the next request without a reload. The parsed form holds the directive list, compiled regexes, scoping blocks, a per-file memo of which access rules match, the auth realm map and the memo-eligibility verdict. The chain from docroot to the request's directory is bounded at **64** levels; past that a deny-all sentinel applies. Since 2026-09-16 an **unreadable or non-UTF-8 `.htaccess` also fails closed** to that sentinel rather than being skipped.

Vhost-level switches: ` 0` disables the whole chain (even with `autoLoadHtaccess`), while `autoLoadHtaccess` alone loads files without enabling general overrides. Candidate configuration generations own their own htaccess, rewrite-outcome and UA caches, so a reload never reintroduces stale results.

## The dense-DFA prefilter

Rather than test every rule's regex per request, the eligible patterns compile once into **one fully-determinized dense DFA** (`regex_automata::dfa::dense`) searched a single time to learn *which* rules could match. Only those run for real. A dense DFA holds no lazy transition state, so the search is **cacheless**: no per-search cache allocation and no cross-thread pool lock — one mutex fewer on the request path at high concurrency.

           **hot path** · prefilter, then evaluate
```
let hits = prefilter.search(path);          // which rules *could* match — one DFA pass
for rule in hits {
    if let Some(m) = rule.regex.find(path) { return rule.apply(m); }   // substitute + flags
}
Outcome::Unchanged
```

## Linear vs backtracking matching

A flagged rule runs through a `CompiledRegex` that prefers `regex_automata::meta::Regex` with an explicit thread-local cache keyed per pattern, and falls back to `fancy-regex` only for constructs the linear engine cannot express. The split is exact, not approximate: a pattern the linear engine accepts has identical match semantics under both, so the choice is invisible.

| Pattern shape | Engine | Why |

| Anchors, classes, alternation, repetition | `regex_automata::meta` | Linear time; per-pattern thread-local cache, no shared lock. |

| Lookahead `(?=…)` / `(?!…)`, lookbehind | `fancy-regex` | Not expressible as a finite automaton. |

| In-pattern backreference `\1` | `fancy-regex` | Requires backtracking. |

A regex that errors at match time **fails closed toward the rule's polarity**: a deny that cannot evaluate counts as matched; an allow that cannot evaluate is withheld (hardened 2026-09-06 alongside the spoofing checks).

## Rewrite-outcome cache & UA classification

For chains whose inputs are *path-cacheable*, the whole rewrite decision is memoized for `--rewrite-outcome-ttl-ms` (default 1000 ms — which also bounds `-f`/`-d` filesystem staleness and lets `.htaccess` edits land within a second; 0 disables). The key is vhost/scheme/method/host/path/query plus any keyable header variables the chain reads. Counters: `httpjet_rewrite_outcome_{hits,misses,uncacheable}_total`.

`--rewrite-ua-classify` (default off, a deploy-time decision) keys User-Agent-reading chains by the *bitmap of matching UA RewriteConds* instead of the raw UA string, when parse-time analysis proves the outcome depends on the UA only through those matches. Real-world UA diversity collapses onto a handful of entries (`httpjet_rewrite_ua_classify_entries`). Since 2026-09-06 header-dependency collection continues past the UA classification so a chain that also reads Origin or Accept keys correctly.

## The fast-path memo and chain eligibility

The on-core **finished-response memo** (default on; `--no-fast-memo` / `HJ_FAST_MEMO=0`) serves repeat cookieless static GETs without running the pipeline at all — per thread, 1 s TTL, 64 MiB/worker, only for 200 full bodies without `Set-Cookie`, and only after each distinct key has passed the full pipeline once. Whether a docroot's chain is eligible is a **parse-time verdict** (`MemoClass`, fail-closed) that `httpjet check` prints per vhost.

> [Diagram: memo-eligibility] Memo eligibility. A chain that reads anything the memo key cannot carry — client/server addresses, protocol, IP/env/host access operands, REDIRECT_STATUS, %{HTTP_COOKIE}, %{TIME*} — is ineligible and pays the full pipeline every time. Eligible chains memoize with a VARY-SET of every header the chain reads (raw Origin, UA bitmap …), so an 800-line forum chain still memoizes.

        ⎁   Measured
Same-binary A/B on the forum's 806-line docroot chain (`/robots.txt`, c=100): **h2 137k → 248k req/s (+81%)**, **h1 107k → 153k (+43%)**. The byte-identity gate `scripts/fast_memo_parity_test.sh` diffs a UA × Origin × Accept-Encoding × scheme matrix memo-on vs memo-off (192 cells, zero differences at the last three review rounds).
 PGO · 2026-08-28 · parity re-run 2026-09-16

Interactive · `.htaccess` & `fast_memo` readiness inspector

         Paste or edit an `.htaccess` snippet to inspect `MemoClass` eligibility, `VARY-SET` headers, regex engine split, and directive support:
           RewriteEngine On
SetEnvIfNoCase User-Agent "SemrushBot|AhrefsBot|MJ12bot" bad_bot=1
RewriteCond %{ENV:bad_bot} =1
RewriteRule ^ - [F,L]

Header always set Access-Control-Allow-Origin "https://windowsforum.com" env=CORS_OK
RewriteCond %{HTTP:Origin} ^https://(www\.)?windowsforum\.com$ [NC]
RewriteRule ^ - [E=CORS_OK:1]

RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} -f [OR]
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} -d
RewriteRule ^ - [L]
RewriteRule ^ index.php [L]

Mirrors the parse-time `MemoClass` analysis printed by `httpjet --root /usr/local/lsws check`.

## SetEnvIf & lazy headers

`SetEnvIf` / `SetEnvIfNoCase` evaluate with **lazy header access**: the engine hands each rule a callback that materializes headers only if the rule references one, and the attribute compare is case-insensitive without allocating a lowercased copy. A request matching no rule pays nothing. Since 2026-09-16, `SetEnvIf`/`[E=]` cannot set server-computed CGI names (`REMOTE_ADDR`, `HTTPS`, `CONTENT_LENGTH`, …) — those writes are denied.

           **.htaccess** · SetEnvIf
```
SetEnvIfNoCase User-Agent "bot|crawler" is_bot=1
SetEnvIf Request_URI "\.(?:png|jpg|css|js)$" is_asset=1
RewriteCond %{ENV:is_bot} =1
RewriteRule ^/expensive/ - [E=no-cache:1]      # [E=no-cache] also bypasses the page cache
```

## Front-controller routing

XenForo, WordPress and most PHP frameworks rewrite *every* URL to `/index.php`. The engine keeps the **original `REQUEST_URI`** and pins the resolved script separately (`SCRIPT_FILENAME` via the `LsapiScript` extension, `SCRIPT_NAME`/`QUERY_STRING` into the env). PHP sees the front controller; everything downstream still sees the URL the visitor asked for — which is why the page cache keys by the original URI .

## Access control

` ` / ` ` / ` ` / ` ` / ` ` scoping carries `Order` / `Allow from` / `Deny from` and `Require`, ANDed across every enclosing block. A ` ` deny applies to the directory **and everything beneath it**. `Require all granted` grants; `Require all denied` and every other predicate (`ip`, `host`, `env`, `expr`, `method`, …) **fails closed to deny** rather than being approximated — a shipped auth file that httpjet cannot honor 403s rather than opening up. Directory patterns accept mapped filesystem paths as well as the docroot-relative convention.

## HTTP Basic auth

`AuthType Basic` + `AuthName` + `AuthUserFile` + `Require valid-user | user …` protect a subtree. Since the 2026-09-06 review the model separates parsed policy from the effective realm: requirements resolve in order across scopes, a metadata-only section cannot erase an inherited requirement, an explicit `Require` replaces it, exact usernames are preserved, and the realm is enforced against the original, rewritten, index, script/PATH_INFO and canonical filesystem targets **before cache lookup**, with a served-target backstop. Unsupported or incomplete active auth fails closed. Valid credentials set `REMOTE_USER`; failures return 401 with the challenge.

           **.htaccess** · a protected subtree
```
AuthType Basic
AuthName "Staging"
AuthUserFile /srv/example.test/conf/htpasswd
Require valid-user
```

htpasswd hashes: **bcrypt** (`$2y$`/`$2b$`/`$2a$`, `htpasswd -B`, cost capped at 14 — a higher cost is refused before hashing), **APR1-MD5** (`$apr1$`), **MD5-crypt** (`$1$`) and `{SHA}`, verified in constant time; an unknown user pays dummy bcrypt/MD5 work at the file's recorded cost, so user enumeration costs nothing, and Basic-auth attempts are charged per client before hashing (repeated `Authorization` headers are refused). Plaintext entries and traditional DES / `$5$` / `$6$` `crypt()` hashes verify *false* with a parse-time warning. The `AuthUserFile` must resolve **inside the vhost docroot** — or a directory listed in `--auth-user-file-roots` — checked on the opened descriptor's real path (symlinks followed, `.`/`..` rejected in relative paths, read capped at 1 MiB, a planted FIFO cannot block the open); an unreadable or out-of-root file is a 500 with an error-log entry, never a silent 401, and `check` warns about out-of-root paths. Authenticated static responses get `Cache-Control: private, no-store` from automatic expiry when no explicit policy exists (#414).

## Directives reference

| Directive | Status | Notes |

| RewriteEngine · RewriteBase | supported | Toggle and base-path resolution. |

| RewriteCond · RewriteRule | supported | Flags: `L END R R=code F G P PT E= N NC QSA QSD NE C S=n`, `OR` on conditions; `-f -d -l -s -x` file tests. Variables: `REQUEST_URI REQUEST_FILENAME REQUEST_METHOD REQUEST_SCHEME QUERY_STRING THE_REQUEST HTTPS HTTP_HOST HTTP_USER_AGENT HTTP_COOKIE HTTP_REFERER HTTP_ACCEPT REMOTE_ADDR REMOTE_PORT SERVER_ADDR SERVER_NAME SERVER_PORT SERVER_PROTOCOL DOCUMENT_ROOT SCRIPT_FILENAME`, `%{HTTP:Name}`, `%{ENV:NAME}`, `%{LA-U:…}`/`%{LA-F:…}`. `%{TIME*}` and map lookups yield the empty string. Unknown flags are ignored, as Apache does. |

| SetEnvIf · SetEnvIfNoCase | supported | Lazy header access; server-computed CGI names are protected. |

| Order · Allow from · Deny from | supported | Apache accumulation per scope; `env=`, host and CIDR operands (host/env/IP operands make the chain memo-ineligible). |

| Require | partial | `all granted`, `valid-user`, `user …`. Everything else fails closed to deny. |

| AuthType · AuthName · AuthUserFile | supported | Basic only; bcrypt, APR1 (`$apr1$`), MD5-crypt (`$1$`) and `{SHA}` hashes. |

| Header set / add / append / merge / unset / setifempty | supported | `always`/`onsuccess`, case-insensitive `env=`/`env=!` guards, `%{NAME}e` interpolation, ` `/` `/` ` scopes (merged in Apache order: directory-level across the chain, then ` ` against the resolved target file, then ` `). `merge` deduplicates trimmed comma-separated values. Applied in `finalize`, before cache storage and compression. CR/LF rejected. |

| Header echo | partial | Parses without error; emits nothing. |

| Header edit / edit* / note · RequestHeader * | ignored | Line ignored. See the header-directive compatibility inventory in the source tree (`docs/header-directive-compatibility.md`) for the exact boundary and the executable fixtures. |

| Header condition expr= / value expr= | partial | Only a conjunction of `%{REQUEST_URI} =~ / !~` is evaluated; other expressions are not. Value expressions are not implemented. |

| ErrorDocument | supported | Path, inline and external forms; never clobbers an application's own JSON error body. |

| DirectoryIndex | supported | Including the `Disabled` form. |

| SetHandler · AddHandler · AddType · ForceType · RemoveHandler · RemoveType | supported | `application/x-httpd-php` forces PHP handling / records the mapping; other handlers and `Remove*` record a non-PHP reset; `AddType`/`ForceType` override response `Content-Type`. |

| CacheLookup · CacheEnable · CacheDisable · CacheKeyModify | supported | The LSCache directives driving the page cache ; `CacheKeyModify` strips query parameters from the key. |

| php_value · php_admin_value · php_flag · php_admin_flag | supported | Per-request PHP ini overrides on the LSAPI special-env path. |

|             | partial | Common scopes honored; ` ` only for the modeled REQUEST_URI shape; ` ` bodies are evaluated. |

| FileETag · H2EarlyHints · esi · AddOutputFilterByType · AllowOverride · Options | no-op | Recognized and dropped. |

| ExpiresActive · ExpiresDefault · ExpiresByType | supported | Scoped across directory, ` ` and ` ` blocks; shares `hj-compress`'s `A/M` time grammar and overrides the vhost XML ` ` defaults when active. |

Unrecognized directives are ignored leniently so vendor `.htaccess` files remain loadable. The planned first step for the header family is making unsupported forms visible in `check --strict` before adding more mutation behavior.

## Per-context overrides & sub_filter

Alongside the per-directory chain, XML contexts rewrite *responses* and override limits for a URI prefix (reference: Configuration → Contexts ):

- **`subFilter`** — literal `SEARCH => REPLACEMENT` substitution between the expires and compress stages, 200 responses only, un-encoded bodies of matching `subFilterTypes` (default `text/html`). Buffered bodies and streams both cap filtered output at `subFilterMaxBody` (4 MiB default); a stream past the cap passes through raw, never half-filtered. `Content-Length` is recomputed, ETag dropped, Last-Modified off unless kept. sub_filter paths bypass the page cache (whose hits re-enter transforms), while eligible static responses may use the fast-path memo (which stores and replays finalized bytes without re-filtering).

- **`maxReqBodySize`** — per-context body cap enforced at dispatch for all terminals (413).

- **`responseTimeout`** (proxy paths) and **`bandwidthLimit`** — override the backend deadline and the server-wide egress rate.

## Reproducible checks

           **tests**
```
cargo test -p hj-rewrite                                   # parser, evaluator, access, auth, cache directives
cargo test -p hj-rewrite --test header_compat              # characterization fixtures for the Header boundary
cargo test -p hj-rewrite --test redirect_repro
bash scripts/fast_memo_parity_test.sh                      # memo-on vs memo-off byte identity on a real chain
```

==============================================================================
PAGE: Security & access control (https://httpjet.net/docs/security)
SUMMARY: Client identity, network ACLs, throttling, GeoIP/ASN rules, PROXY protocol trust, request decompression limits, the body budget, the WAF sidecar, and the PHP jail.
==============================================================================

# Security & access control

Everything that decides **who the client is** and **who may ask**: the trusted-proxy identity model, network ACLs, the opt-in per-IP throttle, GeoIP/ASN rules from an offline source, PROXY-protocol trust, the mTLS boundary, request-body and decompression budgets, the WAF sidecar seam, and the fail-closed PHP jail. The recurring rule is **fail closed**: a control that cannot evaluate acts restrictive, never permissive.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## Client identity

Every decision that depends on "the client's IP" starts from one resolved value, produced at connection admission and stored in `ReqCtx.client_ip`:

> [Diagram: client-ip] From socket peer to client identity. Forwarded headers are evidence, not identity: they count only from a peer an allow rule marks T; from anyone else they are attacker-controlled data and ignored. Every later gate — ACL, geo, throttle, mTLS exemption, logs, the cache key — reads the resolved value.

| `useIpInProxyHeader` | Forwarded headers are believed… |

| 0 | never |

| 1 / 4 | always (only safe when nothing but your proxy can reach the listener) |

| 2 (default) | only from trusted peers (`allow … T`); `CF-Connecting-IP` recognized on that path |

| 3 | as 2, for IP purposes only |

The admin write API classifies `useIpInProxyHeader` and the whole ` ` block as **restart-required**: trust must not change under a running generation without a listener transaction.

## Network ACLs

` ` evaluates `allow`/`deny` CIDR lists most-specific-wins; a trailing `T` on an *allow* rule marks a trusted proxy. ` ` globs are never served, and a malformed glob is a hard start/reload error rather than a warn-and-skip. ` ` mode `2` (owner-restricted) fails closed to never-follow. Static opens use `openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH)` — plus `RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS` when policy denies symlinks — and refuse non-regular files so a planted FIFO cannot park an executor thread; a kernel without `openat2` fails closed to 404.

## Per-client-IP throttle

` ` (or `--per-ip-rate`) caps requests per client IP per fixed window (`perIpRateWindowSecs`, default 1 s); excess requests get 429. The implementation is a sharded fixed-window counter — 64 shards, 4096 tracked IPs per shard — counted exactly once per request at the fast-path serve points and at dispatch.

        !   Off by default, and fail-open
Default 0 (disabled): a shared NAT egress aggregates many real visitors behind one address, so limits are strictly opt-in. Under internal state pressure (a distinct-IP flood) the throttle evicts expired windows and then *admits untracked* — degrading fairness, never availability. `httpjet_throttle_{allowed,rejected}_total` show what it does.

## GeoIP / ASN rules

Country and network membership come from `hj-geo`, which has no runtime network access: point ` ` at a CidrList text file and refresh it on your own schedule. Ranges load into sorted, merged interval sets queried by binary search; IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses are judged in v4 space.

           **geo source** · CidrList format
```
# country
country US 203.0.113.0/24 198.51.100.0/24
country DE 2001:db8::/32
# asn
asn 13335 203.0.113.0/24
```

`geoAllow`/`geoDeny` (ISO-2 labels) and `asnAllow`/`asnDeny` resolve to CIDR sets at state build: **deny first**; an allow list with no deny list is a **fail-closed whitelist**; an unknown label or a missing database is a hard build error, not a silent no-op; `check` warns on geo lists without a database. Both funnels (on-core and bridged) judge the *resolved* client IP, so CDN-fronted visitors are evaluated by their real address.

## PROXY protocol trust

A listener with `proxyProtocol=1` requires a PROXY v2/v1 header on every connection, consumed before TLS or the h1/h2c sniff. The listener opt-in *is* the trust decision — never enable it on a public bind (`check` warns). Headers claiming a loopback or unspecified source are refused at the parser (2026-09-16), because those addresses would otherwise unlock the mTLS exemption and the loopback purge/ready endpoints. Details: Protocol stacks .

## TLS & mTLS

- **mTLS** — `clientVerify` 1–3 attaches a webpki verifier to the *listener* CA; level 2 requires a client certificate (e.g. Cloudflare Authenticated Origin Pulls). A plaintext request for an mTLS vhost is refused unless from loopback. `--no-mtls` is for local testing only — always confirm the live flags with `systemctl show -p ExecStart` before reasoning about the boundary.

- **Revocation** — `crlFile` adds PEM CRL enforcement; absent means none, stated plainly.

- **Cipher and resumption discipline** — one TLS 1.3 suite, single-use tickets, 0-RTT off; resumption disabled when OCSP is on. TLS stream splitting was made memory-safe in the 2026-09-06 round.

- **One config, two transports** — a certificate, verifier or CRL change cannot land on TCP and miss QUIC. See TLS, ACME & OCSP .

## Request limits & resource fences

| Fence | Enforcement |

| Header and URL size, connection counts, timeouts | From ` `: `maxReqURLLen`, `maxReqHeaderSize`, `maxConnections`, `connTimeout`, `keepAliveTimeout`, `maxKeepAliveReq`. Incomplete request reads are bounded (2026-09-06); h2 frame/body deadlines apply on both loops. |

| Body size | `maxReqBodySize` server-wide, per-context override; 413 on every terminal. Chunked/decoded growth is reserved before allocation. |

| Body budget | A process-wide byte budget with owned leases attached to the allocation (including cloned/sliced `Bytes`), released on completion or connection teardown. `httpjet_body_buffer_{bytes,capacity_bytes,rejected_total}`. |

| Request decompression | Gzip by default; br/zstd opt-in. Decoded ceiling 16 MiB, 17 MiB codec workspace reservation, zstd window ≤ 2 24 , one coding only; 503 when the reservation fails, 413 past `maxReqBodySize`. → |

| Egress bandwidth | Per-connection token bucket (`bandwidthLimit`, context override); H2 paces per connection; H3 unpaced. |

| Ranges · sub_filter · `.htaccess` depth | 8 ranges / 8 MiB; 4 MiB buffer then raw pass-through; 64 levels then deny-all. |

| H2 / H3 memory | Stream and connection limits, HTTP/2 Bomb mitigation, bounded H3 retained response memory, body-reservation leases released on reset/EOF/error. |

| Page cache | 100 MiB object cap; index/file/hot budgets; identity guard; integrity-keyed persistent containers (key loaded through the same private-file validator as the admin/profiling tokens — `O_NOFOLLOW`, single link, owner root or the serving uid, no group/other bits, checked on the opened descriptor; `httpjet_pagecache_integrity_active` on :9090, and `--page-cache-integrity-required` makes an uninstallable key a boot failure); purge endpoint loopback-only and POST-only (other methods get 405 + `Allow`). |

| Reload safety | A broken config on SIGHUP keeps the old generation; out-of-range isolation modes are hard errors; the write API rejects rather than partially applies. |

| Worker pinning | Core indices clamped to `CPU_SETSIZE`. |

## WAF inspection seam

httpjet embeds no rules engine. `--waf-sidecar-addr` enables a bounded HTTP inspection call over a Unix socket (`unix:/path`, peer UID verified via `SO_PEERCRED` against `--waf-sidecar-uid`) or loopback TCP (`ip:port`) that runs after URI normalization and body limits but **before** rewrite, cache lookup, WebSocket/proxy dispatch, LSAPI, FastCGI and static serving — so a warm cache hit is still inspected. The default failure policy is **closed** (503); `--waf-fail-open` must be chosen explicitly and logs every bypass (an explicit 403 from the sidecar always blocks). The full contract is on Extending httpjet .

## The PHP jail

suEXEC (` `, off by default, `uidMin`/`gidMin` floors; uid 0 always rejected), chroot (`chrootMode` 0–2) and optional namespaces (`pid` accepted but not honored). A configured jail that turns out unsafe disables PHP for that vhost with a 503 — never unjailed, never falling through to static. Workers never run as root and a setuid `lsphp` is refused. See LSAPI & PHP .

## Control surfaces

| Surface | Guard |

| `/__hj_cache_purge`, `/__hj_cache_ready` (main listeners) | Raw TCP peer must be loopback — no shared secret; CDN-relayed or LAN peers get 404. The purge endpoint answers POST only (405 + `Allow` otherwise) and honors every `X-LiteSpeed-Purge` header line; the ready probe answers GET/HEAD. PROXY headers cannot claim loopback; a `unix:` listener opens these endpoints to any local process (`check` warns — the socket mode is the boundary). |

| `--metrics-addr` (`/metrics`, `/cache-entries`, `/__mimalloc-stats`, `/__alloc-count`, `/debug/pprof/profile`) | Loopback-only by default; `/metrics` is open on loopback, while `/cache-entries`, `/__mimalloc-stats`, `/__alloc-count` and profiling require `Authorization: Bearer ` matching `--profile-token-file` (returning 403 when unset or mismatched). Do not reverse-proxy it. |

| `--admin-addr` (read-only `/v1/status`) | Loopback TCP only (argument parsing rejects anything else); Host must be a loopback authority; Origin headers and bodies rejected; no secrets in the schema. |

| `--admin-write-addr` (`/v1/revision`, `/v1/config[/validate]`) | Loopback + bearer token from a 0400/0600 single-link file (constant-time compare) + exact `If-Match` revision + explicit resource roots for any filesystem reference. |

| LSAPI control and generation files | Root-only control socket; generation file mmap'd read-only by web pools; non-group-writable parent directory required. |

| ACME store · DNS token · integrity key · admin token | Owner and mode checks on the descriptor, no symlink following, bounded reads. |

## Audit posture

Seven whole-codebase review rounds plus the sixteen-round October bug-bash campaign have landed on top of the August hardening pass: **2026-08-30** (issues #362–#368: no exploitable High, five low/informational fixes), **2026-09-06** (five confirmed medium/low findings: H2/H3 body-reservation leaks, retained-body and gzip-expansion accounting, scoped Basic-auth merging, public caching of authenticated static responses, UA-classification memo dependencies), **2026-09-16** (twelve fixes: h2 monoio deadlines, sendfile stall bounds, unreadable `.htaccess` fail-closed, PROXY loopback claims, `[P]` target screening, CGI-var deny-list, never-root and setuid refusal, isolation-mode hard errors, restart-required trust fields, seccomp ptrace gating, Origin-varied cache entries, CPU_SETSIZE clamp and single Content-Length), **2026-10-06** (issues #560–#575, released as 0.0.4: the H3 connection budget is charged at `Connected` with stateless Retry under handshake pressure, RFC 9112 request-target/Host enforcement at the H1 intake, one rule for which client headers reach PHP, `AuthUserFile` confined to the docroot with constant-cost verification and a bcrypt cost cap, POST-only purge + validated integrity keys + bounded control surfaces, quinn GHSA-53rm-773f-4q8c, new `qpack_decode`/`proxy_protocol_parse`/`lscache_control` fuzz targets, and a daily RustSec dependency-advisory CI job), **0.0.5** (15 findings #579–#593), **0.0.6** (2026-10-13 audit #594–#611: truncated LSAPI/FastCGI response aborts, HPACK over-cap converted to a stream error so dynamic tables stay in sync on pooled CDN connections, H3 streaming backpressure, OCSP responder TLS SAN verification), and **0.0.7–0.1.5** (2026-10-14..24 bug-bash rounds 1–16 and audit #1138: OLS XML wildcard/routing parity, APR1/MD5-crypt htpasswd + per-client auth rate limit, `.htaccess` `Expires*` + `Header merge`, per-URL cookie vary, SHA-256 vary hashing, Unix-socket WAF peer-UID verification, Bearer token gating on `/cache-entries` and `/__mimalloc-stats`, `lsapilib-hardening.patch` + `BEGIN_REQUEST` body scan, time-refilled H2 rapid-reset budget and send-stall resets, rustls 0.23.46 and webpki emSign distrust). Each round's regressions are in the tree; gates re-run after each: full workspace suite (3,019 tests), fast-memo parity, cache xurl/scheme/xhost, h2spec 146/146.

        i   Reporting
Security issues: use private responsible disclosure per `SECURITY.md` in the repository, not a public issue. Findings are reconciled against source and regression tests; none of this is evidence of production exploitation or a proof of absence of other vulnerabilities.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Page cache (https://httpjet.net/docs/page-cache)
SUMMARY: The opt-in LSCache-protocol origin page cache: keys, tiers, admission, purge, the file tier, dictionaries, stale policies, capsules, and generation-scoped namespaces.
==============================================================================

# The origin page cache

An opt-in full-response origin cache speaking the LiteSpeed cache protocol — `X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control`, `X-LiteSpeed-Tag`, `X-LiteSpeed-Vary`, `X-LiteSpeed-Purge` — so a site already tuned for LSCache needs no application change. A **hit** returns the stored response without touching the backend; everything else is engineered so the cache can never serve the wrong page.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## Overview

Two crates split the work. `hj-pagecache` is the transport-agnostic store: a sharded byte-weighted LRU index built on `hj-cache`, W-TinyLFU admission, key + vary + tag indexes, TTL and stale windows, the LSCache header classifier, and the HJPC file tier. The binary's `lscache/` module is the request-aware glue: `cache_lookup` runs after rewrite and access control but before any backend; `cache_store` runs after each terminal's `finalize_response`. Both are inert and near-zero-cost without `--page-cache`.

           Off by default · app opt-in per response
           Keyed by the ORIGINAL URI · identity-guarded
           Public · private · shared-path tiers
           RAM index · hot tier · tmpfs file tier
           Tag purge · stale-while-revalidate · stale-if-error · single flight
           Per-vhost dictionaries · survives restarts

        i   Not the fast-path memo
Static files have a separate, default-on per-worker finished-response memo (1 s TTL) that sits even earlier on the on-core path — see Rewrite → fast-path memo . It never serves page-cache entries.

## Opt-in by the app

The cache never guesses. A response is stored only when the application says so. Per-vhost ` ` (and the six LSWS gates on a context's `cachePolicy`), the `.htaccess` `CacheLookup` directive, and the `[E=no-cache]` env all gate lookups; the response header gates storage.

           **app → httpjet** · the cache protocol headers
```
X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: public,max-age=3600            # public entry, one hour
X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: private,max-age=120            # per-session entry (needs --page-cache-private; TTL capped 300 s)
X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: public,max-age=60,stale-while-revalidate=600,stale-if-error=3600
X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: no-cache                       # never store this response
X-LiteSpeed-Tag: T1234,forum7                             # purge tags
X-LiteSpeed-Vary: cookie=xf_style_id                      # vary the public entry on a declared cookie value
X-LiteSpeed-Purge: tag=T1234                              # drop every entry carrying this tag (also: * for all)
```

**Standards mode.** `--page-cache-standard-vhosts a.example,b.example` puts listed vhosts into OpenLiteSpeed's `checkPublicCache` shape: a plain `Cache-Control: public, max-age=N` is an opt-in, a default public policy applies when no ` ` block exists, and `CacheLookup` defaults on. It is an allowlist, so a status/admin vhost cannot start caching because it merely marked something public. All other guards still apply.

        !   Backends cannot self-purge
Proxied upstream responses may not assert `X-LiteSpeed-*`; those headers are stripped so a remote backend cannot inject policy or invalidate entries. Only LSAPI/PHP responses and loopback callers of the purge endpoint shape cache behavior.

## The lookup path

> [Diagram: cache-lookup] Lookup, tier routing and freshness. Member-cookie requests route to the private tier (or, for allow-listed visitor-invariant endpoints, to the shared public tier); the key is derived from the original URI; a found entry serves only if its stored identity matches; stale entries within their windows serve immediately with a background refresh; concurrent misses collapse onto one render.

## Keys, tiers and the identity guard

key & tier explorer — change the request and the app's header

           method  GET  HEAD  POST
           scheme  https  http
           host
           path
           query
           vary cookie xf_style_id

             request carries the member cookie (xf_user)
             --page-cache-private on
             path matches --page-cache-shared-paths
             the .htaccess chain reads Origin

          X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control on the response

Illustrative composition, not the byte layout. The real key is a compact id plus the stored identity; the guard makes any id collision a miss.

        !   Invariant 1 · key by the original URI
The key uses `orig_path`/`orig_query`, never the rewrite-resolved path. XenForo's front controller rewrites *every* page to `/index.php`; keying by the resolved path once collapsed the whole site onto one entry and served the wrong page to everyone. The incident is documented in the crate itself.

        !   Invariant 2 · the identity guard
Every entry records the host + raw request path it was built for; a lookup serves only if both match. A key collision degrades to a miss (`httpjet_pagecache_key_id_collisions_total`), never to wrong content.

Three more dimensions were added later and are part of the key today: **per-URL cookie vary** (`X-LiteSpeed-Vary: cookie=NAME` per URL in addition to the vhost-wide `--page-cache-vary-cookies` list, with request-header vary dimensions hashed with SHA-256), **Origin** when the vhost's `.htaccess` chain reads it (2026-09-16 — a reflected `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` no longer replays the first storer's CORS verdict; an absent Origin keeps the historic base key so persisted entries survive), and the **epoch + generation** namespace introduced by the first API publication so an old in-flight render can never overwrite a new generation's entry. Only the canonical Host spelling may read or populate a vhost's entry.

| Tier | Routed when | Keyed by | Notes |

| **Public** | No member cookie | vhost · scheme · host · original path?query · declared vary-cookie values (· Origin) | `Set-Cookie` and `X-LiteSpeed-*` stripped from the stored copy; a response that sets a private cookie is never stored. |

| **Private** | Member marker present (`xf_user`, or a bare `xf_session` with no `xf_user` — session-only logins leave the public tier, 2026-10-04) and `--page-cache-private` | public key + session-cookie value | Never reads or writes public entries in either direction. TTL capped at 300 s. Member POSTs typically emit a tag purge so their own reply is never hidden. |

| **Shared paths** | Member cookie, path matches `--page-cache-shared-paths` (`PATH?PARAM` exact or `PATH` prefix), within the sticky canary % | public key | Only for visitor-invariant, HMAC-gated image endpoints — never HTML. Malformed specs abort startup; empty = inert. |

| **Bypass** | Non-GET/HEAD, `[E=no-cache]`, no accepted header, member without private tier | — | Counted as `httpjet_cache_bypass`. |

## The store path and admission

> [Diagram: cache-store] Store gates. After the app opts in, the response still has to pass the status list, the private-cookie guard, the proxied-header strip, the self-redirect guard, the purge-race check and the object cap, and then earn admission. Only then is the stored copy written — into RAM, or at birth into an immutable tmpfs file.

### W-TinyLFU admission

> [Diagram: admission] A fixed-memory frequency sketch rejects one-hit wonders: at the default threshold of 2 a URL is stored on its second sighting. One request is ONE sighting — the on-core fast path probes uncounted and records only a hit it serves. Size weighting adds +1 per 256 KiB. With dictionaries making storage cheap, --page-cache-admit-threshold 1 caches on first sight. Tune by httpjet_cache_hit_ratio_real and httpjet_cache_admit_ratio.

The **self-redirect guard** declines an app-marked-cacheable 3xx whose `Location` is the request's own URL (hosts normalized without port, because an h2 `Host` carries `:443` and a generated absolute Location may not); it is re-checked at serve time, and the XF add-on refuses at a third layer. A cacheable origin *redirect* is also de-cached from the CDN's perspective via the deny-CDN-cache transform, so a canonical loop cannot pin itself at the edge.

## Storage tiers & the file tier

> [Diagram: cache-tiers] Dual-cap tier model. The RAM index describes every entry; with a file tier, bodies live as immutable HJPC files and are charged metadata-only against --page-cache-mem while their footprint counts against --page-cache-disk-mem. A small hot tier fronts the files. Every teardown path (evict, expire, purge, replace) is synchronous under the shard lock; only the unlink(2) syscall is deferred to just after the lock is released.

By default the cache is in-RAM only and flushes on restart. `--page-cache-store-path /dev/shm/jetcache` (or `default`/`jetcache`) makes it **tmpfs-primary** in the LiteSpeed Enterprise style: `PageStore::store` offloads every body to a file at birth in identity form, off the process heap; one immutable file per body version; self-describing HJPC containers authenticated with the `--page-cache-integrity-key`. The LiteSpeed `cacheStorePath` is parsed but deliberately unused so httpjet never collides with a resurrected LiteSpeed.

- **Survives restarts.** A background boot scan (up to 8 threads over the fan-out dirs) rebuilds the index from the files — ~300k entries in seconds. `/__hj_cache_ready` returns 503 while scanning and 200 + `x-hj-cache-ready: 1` + `x-hj-cache-loaded: N` when done; probing a URL mid-scan re-primes it and unlinks the persisted copy, so wait for readiness.

- **Reclaim invariant.** Live entries resolve to live bodies; a missing file fails closed to a miss and counts `disk_read_err`. Orphan reconciliation reclaims superseded files it can prove are safe to delete and defers the rest.

- **Durable purges.** Purges unlink eagerly and retain a purge-all stamp, so old data cannot be resurrected on restart.

- **Dictionaries compress at store.** The birth copy is identity; a bounded background task then dict-recompresses it in place against the vhost's own zstd dictionary (~3.5–9× smaller) at store time — never inline on a response, and never triggered by a first hit. An admission filter rejects one-hit public content before it reaches this work, and incompressible Content-Types are never encoded. Judge by `httpjet_pagecache_dict_recompress_{total,skipped_total{reason}}`; the served bytes stay standard zstd/br/gzip either way.

budget calculator — how many pages fit?

           --page-cache-mem (MiB)
           --page-cache-disk-mem (MiB)
           --page-cache-hot-mem (MiB)
           typical page (KB, identity)
           dictionary ratio ×

Rules of thumb only (≈6 KB of metadata per entry, ratio 3.5–9× measured on forum HTML). tmpfs *is* RAM — size the disk cap against the box's headroom. Production runs disk-mem 6 GiB, hot-mem 384 MiB.

| Flag | Default | Bounds |

| `--page-cache-mem` | 128 MiB | RAM index: metadata, variants, any in-RAM body. With a file tier, persisted bodies are charged metadata-only here. |

| `--page-cache-disk-mem` | 2 GiB | tmpfs footprint (actual blocks when available); a per-shard disk LRU evicts the least-recently-*served* entry. 0 ⇒ fall back to `--page-cache-mem`. |

| `--page-cache-hot-mem` | 192 MiB | In-RAM hot bodies in front of the files: zero-syscall serves; cold hits pay one ~µs tmpfs read + decode. |

| `--page-cache-store-path` | *none* | Enables the file tier. Requires the integrity key; deploy scripts gate it behind `ALLOW_PAGE_CACHE_FILE_TIER=1`. |

| `--page-cache-dict-vhost` / `--page-cache-dict` / `--page-cache-dict-level` | — | Per-vhost zstd dictionaries (train one per site with `scripts/train-pagecache-dict.sh`) / global fallback / per-vhost internal zstd level (1–19, default 12). Rotation needs a restart; old-generation entries become safe misses (each body records its `dict_gen`). |

| `--page-cache-vary-default` | *empty* | `name=value` pairs: a vary cookie carrying the default value (e.g. `xf_style_id=50`) is keyed as if absent. |

| `--page-cache-opt-in-status` / `--page-cache-303-prefixes` | *empty* | Opt-in caching of 303/404/410 — only on an explicit `X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: public`, TTL capped 300 s, no stale windows; a 303 only under a listed prefix. Default: only 200/301 are cached. |

| `--page-cache-stream-fill-vhosts` | *empty* | Vhosts whose cacheable public 200 misses without a Content-Length stream to the client frame by frame and store when the backend finishes (~ms earlier first byte on progressive template output). Errors/short bodies/over-cap serve but never store. |

        !   Dictionaries can retain content
Train only on public, logged-out pages of one vhost; a dictionary trained on another site's boilerplate does little, and one trained on private pages can leak fragments. Served bytes are never dictionary-encoded — a missing compatible dictionary is a miss, never undecodable output.

## Variants, compression and egress

The store keeps identity bytes plus **one best precompressed variant** chosen by the request's `Accept-Encoding` under the server priority zstd > br > gzip (when `--cf-send-zstd` is active, background refreshes fill only the zstd variant); a client whose accepted set differs gets a per-serve compress of the identity form. Egress is therefore always standard zstd/brotli/gzip/identity, and a hit re-negotiates encoding — stored responses are never tied to the first client. Hits from the hot tier are zero-copy `Bytes` on h2. See Compression .

## Purge

Invalidation is tag-based. The app emits `X-LiteSpeed-Purge: tag=T1234` (or `*`) on a response — every such header line is honored (0.0.5) — or a local process POSTs the loopback endpoint on the main listener. The endpoint answers **POST only** (2026-10-07); a loopback GET or other method gets 405 + `Allow`, and the ready probe takes GET/HEAD. A store that started before a relevant purge and finished after it is rejected (`httpjet_pagecache_store_purge_rejections_total`), so a stale render cannot win a race against the purge.

           **purge** · loopback-only endpoint
```
curl -s -X POST -H 'x-litespeed-purge: tag=T1234' -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1/__hj_cache_purge   # 204
curl -s -X POST -H 'x-litespeed-purge: *' http://127.0.0.1/__hj_cache_purge                                          # everything
```

The endpoint is gated by the **raw TCP source being loopback** — no shared secret, no per-URL purge, and a CDN-relayed or LAN request gets 404. The former `--cache-peer` fan-out and `--cache-purge-secret-file` are gone. A purge with the file tier unlinks eagerly; a restart cannot resurrect purged entries.

## Stale policies & single flight

| Mechanism | Flags | Behavior |

| stale-while-revalidate LSCache-authoritative: an `X-LiteSpeed` opt-in does not merge in the standard `Cache-Control`'s `stale-while-revalidate`/`stale-if-error` (2026-10-04); `s-maxage` still implies proxy-revalidate and suppresses these defaults | `--page-cache-stale-default-secs` (0), `--page-cache-stale-max-secs` (86400) | Within the window a stale entry serves immediately and a background refresh (`httpjet_pagecache_refresh_inflight`) re-renders through the same dispatch (so WAF and gates apply). |

| stale-if-error | `--page-cache-stale-if-error-default-secs` (0), `--page-cache-stale-if-error-max-secs` (86400) | A backend 5xx (including an lsphp-down 503) on a cacheable public GET serves the retained entry as `X-LiteSpeed-Cache: hit,stale-if-error` with a short `public,max-age=30` egress, Age reset, CDN-CC stripped — the CDN coalesces a 30 s burst but never pins it. Production sets 30 s. Gate: `scripts/cache_sie_test.sh`. |

| single flight | built in | Concurrent misses of one key collapse onto one leader via a `Notify`; followers wait rather than each rendering. Registering on the leader's Notify *before* the pre-wait lookup closed a lost-wakeup that once serialized misses. |

## XenForo public-shell capsules application-specific

A second, XenForo-shaped tier behind `--xf-capsule` (requires `--page-cache`): a public HTML *shell* for member requests, with the member-specific bits filled client-side by the SessionValidator/CacheOptimizer add-on. It is fail-closed by allow-list — `--xf-capsule-vhosts` empty disables it for every vhost — with route coverage by `--xf-capsule-paths` prefixes or the `all-get-classified` conservative classifier, deterministic canaries for guests and members, and its own stale window (`--xf-capsule-stale-secs`, production 3600 so a missed purge self-heals within an hour). Since 2026-10-04 members are served from the shell-capable *public* entry — `--xf-capsule-dedicated-store` (default off) restores the second dedicated copy. The capsule purge gate (`scripts/cache_capsule_purge_test.sh`) proves a tag purge invalidates the member-served shell. Metrics: `httpjet_xf_capsule_*`.

> [Diagram: xf-capsule] Guest vs logged-in member routing across the four cache surfaces. Guests use the public tier directly; logged-in members route visitor-invariant HMAC image paths (--page-cache-shared-paths) to the public tier, eligible forum routes (--xf-capsule) to the anonymized public HTML shell, and remaining opt-in pages to the per-session --page-cache-private tier.

## Generation-scoped namespaces

The first successful API publication introduces a response-cache *epoch* derived from the process-bound revision; every later generation (including SIGHUP) keys public, private and capsule entries by epoch + generation while preserving request identity and purge labels. Old in-flight renders finish in their own namespace; restart returns to the on-disk configuration's namespace, and volatile API entries cannot replay there. Obsolete entries age out under the ordinary budgets. The finished-response memo is generation-keyed for the same reason.

## Microcaching today, and what is missing

Short TTLs already work: a backend that sends `X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: public,max-age=2` gets every guard above and a two-second hit window (`scripts/microcache_policy_example.sh` proves miss→hit→expiry→fresh render, distinct-query isolation and `no-store` respect on an isolated instance). What does not exist yet is a **first-class route-level policy**: named profiles with deterministic precedence, route TTL floors/ceilings, per-profile eligibility, bypass matchers, declarative key dimensions, profile budgets, and bounded collapse/refresh controls. The proposed ` ` contract is specified in the source tree (`docs/microcache-policy.md`) and the parser intentionally rejects it until implemented.

## Observing the cache

           **observe** · headers, entries, metrics
```
$ curl -sI -H 'Host: example.test' http://127.0.0.1:8080/ | grep -i x-litespeed-cache
x-litespeed-cache: miss            # ran the backend; stored if admitted
$ curl -sI -H 'Host: example.test' http://127.0.0.1:8080/ | grep -i x-litespeed-cache
x-litespeed-cache: hit             # served from cache (also: hit,stale-if-error)

$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /etc/httpjet/profile.token)" http://127.0.0.1:9090/cache-entries   # totals, per-URL-class counts, top-N by size, ram/disk line, health line
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9090/metrics | grep -E '^httpjet_(pagecache|cache)_'
$ curl -sk https://127.0.0.1/__hj_cache_ready -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'   # 200 once the boot scan finished
```

Judge health by `httpjet_cache_hit_ratio_real` (non-loopback lookups), `httpjet_pagecache_{hits,misses,stores,purges,evictions}_total`, the per-vhost `httpjet_cache_{hits,misses}_by_vhost{vhost}` split (2026-10-04), `disk_{read,write,full}_errors_total`, `missing_file_invalidations_total`, `poisoned_locks_total` (nonzero = indexes may be inconsistent), and direct content checks — never by a transient raw file count. The full metric list is on Observability .

## Deploy gates

These scripts must pass before `--page-cache` ships anywhere; they run against a loopback instance and each catches a class of bug that has actually happened:

- **`cache_xurl_test.sh`** Three distinct URLs keep their own content — the front-controller poisoning class.

- **`cache_scheme_test.sh`** An HTTP-origin canonical 301 must not poison the HTTPS entry — the "Too Many Redirects" loop.

- **`cache_xhost_test.sh`** Foreign-host isolation.

- **`cache_private_test.sh`** Private-tier session isolation, plus the shared-paths case when configured.

- **`cache_persist_test.sh`** With a file tier: waits on `/__hj_cache_ready` and asserts the boot scan restored entries. It restarts the service — run once (five restarts a minute trip systemd's start limit).

- **`cache_sie_test.sh` · `cache_capsule_purge_test.sh`** Stale-if-error (kills its own lsphp mid-test) and the capsule purge invariant.

        !   A cache bug outlives a rollback
A wrong response cached at the CDN edge stays there for its edge TTL. If bad content shipped: confirm the origin is correct on loopback, then purge the CDN zone — a binary rollback does not remove objects already stored upstream.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Compression (https://httpjet.net/docs/compression)
SUMMARY: Response compression with gzip, brotli and zstd, server-priority negotiation, streaming encoders, precompressed siblings, and bounded request decompression.
==============================================================================

# Compression

`hj-compress` encodes responses with **gzip**, **brotli** and **zstd**, chosen by server priority but always bounded by the client's `Accept-Encoding`. Buffered bodies encode in one shot; streamed bodies stay streaming; precompressed static siblings skip the work entirely; and a trusted proxy can be handed forced zstd. The reverse direction — **request** decompression — is bounded and mostly opt-in.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## Codecs and negotiation

| Codec | Backend | Default level | XML switches |

| zstd | `zstd` | 3 (1–22) | `enableZstdCompress`, `enableDynZstdCompress`, `zstdCompressLevel` |

| brotli | `brotli` | 5 (0–11) | `enableBrCompress`, `enableDynBrCompress`, `brCompressLevel` |

| gzip | `flate2` | 6 | `enableGzipCompress`, `enableDynGzipCompress` |

> [Diagram: compression-negotiation] Choosing an encoder. Bodies of 200 bytes or fewer are never compressed (OpenLiteSpeed parity), the compressible-type set matches LiteSpeed's compressibleTypes, already-encoded and 206 responses are skipped, and every encoded response carries Vary: Accept-Encoding.

zstd encoding uses a per-thread `ZSTD_CCTX` pool and pooled transient output buffers (`hj_core::recycle::BODY_BUFS`) so neither contexts nor output buffers page-fault per response. Streamed bodies (`Body::Stream` — LSAPI, proxy, SSE) wrap in a lazy per-chunk `CompressStream`: each inbound chunk is encoded as it arrives, so SSE stays real-time and a slow backend never holds the first byte hostage.

## Trusted-proxy zstd egress

`--cf-send-zstd` (or `CF_SEND_ZSTD=1`) forces zstd to a *trusted-proxy* peer regardless of the forwarded `Accept-Encoding`. Cloudflare asks the origin for br/gzip but decodes an origin `Content-Encoding: zstd` and re-encodes per browser at its edge, so this hands the CDN the cheapest-to-produce form (zstd ≪ brotli to compress) without changing what browsers receive. Off by default, officially unsupported CDN↔origin, enabled in production; it never applies to untrusted or direct clients.

## Precompressed siblings

If a `.br` or `.gz` sibling of a static file exists in the same directory, httpjet serves it directly with the matching `Content-Encoding` and `Vary: Accept-Encoding` — `gzip_static`/`brotli_static` behavior, brotli preferred. Ranged requests skip the swap so byte ranges stay exact; same-directory placement keeps `accessDenyDir` and symlink verdicts unchanged; a missing sibling falls back to on-the-fly compression at the cost of one stat.

## Interaction with the page cache

The page cache keeps identity bytes plus one best precompressed variant chosen under the same priority; a client whose acceptable set differs is re-encoded per serve. Internal dictionary compression is a storage optimization only — dictionaries never reach the wire, and a hit decodes to identity before standard client compression is selected.

## Request decompression

httpjet decodes a single supported `Content-Encoding` after the transport has fully framed the request body and before rewrite, cache, WAF, proxy or application dispatch — the same decoder for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, h2c and HTTP/3. Gzip is on by default for compatibility; brotli and zstd are opt-in:

           **serve** · opt-in codings
```
httpjet --root /abs/root serve … --request-decompression-extra br,zstd     # accepts br, brotli, zstd; "gzip" is rejected as redundant
```

> [Diagram: request-decompression] Bounded, buffered, fail-safe. Only exactly one coding is decoded; malformed streams and the 16 MiB ceiling forward the original representation unchanged (the destination applies its own policy); the codec workspace and both body forms are charged to the shared budget first.

- A successful decode removes `Content-Encoding` and replaces `Content-Length` with the decoded length before any handler sees the request.

- Decoded output may not exceed the effective `maxReqBodySize` (413). The absolute decoder ceiling is 16 MiB — at it, httpjet forwards the encoded body rather than exposing a truncated one.

- Brotli large-window extensions are disabled; zstd frames are limited to a 2 24 -byte window; `deflate` is not decoded.

- Brotli/zstd reserve 17 MiB for decoder tables before constructing the codec; if that plus both body forms cannot be reserved, the request gets 503.

           **tests**
```
cargo test --locked -p httpjet uring::request_body --no-fail-fast     # all three codecs, bombs, malformed input, stacked encodings, workspace exhaustion
```

## Decode safety

Response-side decoding (page-cache variants, dictionary frames) caps `windowLogMax` and bounds decoded output size; a hostile or corrupt frame fails the decode rather than ballooning memory. Compression cost depends on body size, codec, cache state and backend latency — compare representative hits and misses before trading CPU for bytes. In production the origin's compression phase is sampled as `httpjet_phase_compress_seconds`.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Configuration (https://httpjet.net/docs/configuration)
SUMMARY: The LiteSpeed-compatible XML reference: server, tuning, security, listeners, external processors, upstream groups, virtual hosts, contexts, and httpjet-native extensions.
==============================================================================

# Configuration reference

httpjet is configured by a **LiteSpeed-compatible XML tree** selected with `--root`: `conf/httpd_config.xml`, the per-vhost files it references, and `conf/mime.properties`. An existing LiteSpeed or OpenLiteSpeed tree works as-is. On that base httpjet layers its own opt-in directives — marked httpjet — which LiteSpeed ignores. Operational overrides live on the command line , not in the XML.

## The configuration tree

With no `--root`, httpjet uses `/usr/local/lsws`. The parser (`hj-config`) applies LiteSpeed value semantics faithfully:

- Variables `$SERVER_ROOT`, `$HOSTNAME`, `$VH_ROOT`, `$VH_NAME` substitute in `$VAR` and `${VAR}` forms.

- Sizes accept `K`/`M`/`G`/`B` suffixes; times are bare seconds.

- Bounded integers use OLS semantics: absent, unparsable *or out-of-range* values fall back to the default (never clamped). The isolation modes `setUIDMode`/`chrootMode` are the exception: out-of-range is a hard error (2026-09-16).

- Booleans are `1`, `2` or `true` (case-insensitive); `followSymbolLink`/`allowSymbolLink` treat `2` (owner-restricted) as fail-closed never-follow.

- Unknown elements are ignored so real trees load; `check --strict` reports the ones that would silently do nothing.

           **layout** · a server root
```
/usr/local/lsws/
├── conf/
│   ├── httpd_config.xml          # server, tuning, security, listeners, extProcessors, vhost declarations
│   ├── mime.properties           # mime/type = ext1, ext2   (best-effort)
│   └── vhosts/example.test.xml   #  : docroot, contexts, rewrite, vhssl, cache, logging
└── logs/
```

> [Diagram: config-inheritance] Configuration cascade and parse-time memo classification. Server-wide defaults in httpd_config.xml cascade into each  , then into longest-prefix   overrides and the per-directory .htaccess chain, where static analysis computes the MemoClass eligibility verdict reported by httpjet check.

## Server and tuning

| Directive | Default | Meaning |

| `serverName` | `$HOSTNAME` | Server identity (else `localhost`). |

| `user` / `group` | `nobody` | Run-as credentials (the systemd unit usually sets these). |

| `indexFiles` | `index.html` | Directory-index candidates (vhost may override). |

| `useIpInProxyHeader` | `2` | Client-IP trust: 0 never · 1 always · 2 trusted peers only (+ `CF-Connecting-IP`) · 3 as 2 for IP purposes · 4 always. Restart-required through the write API. |

| ` ` | `0` | HTTP/3 master switch; also drives `Alt-Svc`. Needs the UDP port published. |

| ` maxConnections` | `65000` | Connection cap. |

| `connTimeout` / `keepAliveTimeout` | `60` / `5` s | Idle / keep-alive timeouts. |

| `maxKeepAliveReq` | `1000` | Requests per keep-alive connection (0 or 1 disables keep-alive, matching OpenLiteSpeed). |

| `maxReqURLLen` / `maxReqHeaderSize` | `8192` / `16380` | URL and header-block caps. |

| `maxReqBodySize` | `100M` | Server-wide request-body cap (413); per-context override below. |

| `perIpRate` · `perIpRateWindowSecs` httpjet | `0` · `1` | Per-client-IP request throttle (0 = off) and its fixed window. 429 on exceed; fail-open under state pressure. |

| `bandwidthLimit` httpjet | `0` | Per-connection egress throttle, bytes/s (0 = unlimited). H2 paces per connection; H3 unpaced. |

| `maxCachedFileSize` / `totalInMemCacheSize` | `4M` / `4G` | Small-file in-memory promotion threshold and budget (`CacheCaps`). |

| `maxMMapFileSize` / `totalMMapCacheSize` | `256K` / `2G` | Parsed for compatibility; the mmap file cache was removed. |

| `fileETag` | `28` | ETag bitmask (INODE|MTIME|SIZE → `"size-mtime-inode;;;"`); 0 = no ETag. |

| `enable{Gzip,Br,Zstd}Compress` (+`Dyn`) | on | Static/dynamic compression per codec; `zstdCompressLevel` 3, `brCompressLevel` 5. |

| ` enableExpires`, `expiresByType` | off | `image/*=A604800, text/css=M86400` (A = access, M = modify). Also honored in `.htaccess` via `ExpiresActive` / `ExpiresDefault` / `ExpiresByType` (sharing the same grammar). Authenticated responses get `private, no-store` when no explicit policy exists. |

| ` expireInSeconds` · `privateExpireInSeconds` · `cacheStatusCode` · `enablePostCache` | `900` · `0` · `200,301` · off | Default public/private TTLs and cacheable statuses. `cacheStorePath` is parsed but deliberately unused (see `--page-cache-store-path`). |

## Security directives

| Directive | Default | Meaning |

| ` ` `allow`/`deny` | — | `ALL` or CIDR lists, most-specific wins. A trailing `T` on an allow rule marks a trusted proxy. |

| ` ` | — | Globs never served; a malformed glob is a hard start/reload error. |

| ` followSymbolLink` | off | Folded into each vhost's effective `allowSymbolLink`; `2` fails closed. |

| `geoipDBFile` · `geoAllow`/`geoDeny` · `asnAllow`/`asnDeny` httpjet | none | Offline CidrList source and label lists; deny-first, allow-only = whitelist, unknown label = build error. → |

| ` enable` · `uidMin` · `gidMin` | `0` · `100` · `100` | suEXEC master gate and floors; uid/gid 0 always rejected. |

| ` ` `enable`, `mount`, `pid`, `net`, `uts`, `ipc` | off | Namespace isolation for PHP workers; `pid` is accepted but not honored. |

| ` ` `CPUSoftLimit`/`CPUHardLimit` | — | Parsed for compatibility; ignored on persistent `lsphp` workers (`check` warns). |

| `lsrecaptcha`, `censorshipControl`, permission masks | — | not enforced — `check` warns. |

## Listeners and TLS

| Directive | Default | Meaning |

| `name`, `address` | `*:80` | `ip:port` / `host:port`. httpjet also `unix:/path` or `uds:/path` for an HTTP-over-Unix-socket listener (TLS over UDS is rejected). Listener names are the stable identity across reloads. |

| `secure`, `keyFile`, `certFile`, `certChain` | off | TLS material; `certChain=1` appends `CACertFile` to the served chain. |

| `CACertFile` · `clientVerify` · `verifyDepth` | none · `0` · `1` | Client-certificate verification (0 none · 1 optional · 2 required · 3 optional without CA) against the listener CA. |

| `crlFile` httpjet | none | PEM CRL/bundle enforced by the client verifier. |

| `enableStapling` | `0` | Compatibility only; OCSP needs `--features ocsp` + `--ocsp-responder`. |

| `proxyProtocol` httpjet | `0` | PROXY v2/v1 required on *this* listener; fail-closed; never on a public bind. |

| `vhostMapList/vhostMap` `vhost`, `domain` | — | Host→vhost; domains lowercased; exact matches take precedence over longest-match leading (`*.example.com`) or suffix (`example.*`) wildcards, then the bare `*` catch-all. |

           **httpd_config.xml** · a TLS listener with h3
```
  1

     https
     *:443
     1
     /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.test/privkey.pem
     /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.test/fullchain.pem
     0
       example.test  example.test,www.example.test

```

## External processors

An ` ` (server-level ` ` or per-vhost) is a reverse-proxy upstream (`proxy`), an LSAPI app (`lsapi`), or httpjet a FastCGI app (`fcgi`/`fastcgi`). ` ` configures the default PHP handler with the same pool knobs. Unknown legacy types (`rails`, `appserver`, …) keep proxy behavior; `cgi` contexts are not executed.

| Directive | Default | Meaning |

| `name`, `type` | required | `proxy` · `lsapi` · `fcgi`/`fastcgi` httpjet . |

| `address` (repeatable) | required | `ip:port`, `host:port`, `uds:///path`, `http://`, `https://`, and httpjet `h2://` (prior knowledge) / `h2s://` (TLS, ALPN fail-closed). Additional addresses form a group: ordered failover by default, load-balanced with the options below. |

| `loadBalancePolicy` httpjet | `primary-first` | `weighted-round-robin` · `weighted-least-active`. Invalid on non-proxy processors. |

| `addressWeights` httpjet | all 1 | One integer 1–1000 per address. |

| ` ` `mode` · `path` · `host` · `interval` · `timeout` · `rise` · `fall` · `expectedStatus` httpjet | `connect` · `/` · — · 10 · 2 · 2 · 3 · 200 | Active probes; intervals 1–3600 s, timeout ≤ interval, thresholds 1–100, status 200–599. → |

| `maxConns` | `100` | Pool cap (LSAPI: worker count source unless `--php-children` overrides). |

| `initTimeout` / `retryTimeout` / `pcKeepAliveTimeout` | `60` / `0` / `60` s | Connect timeout / bad-mark cooldown (retry dials fresh; a backend timeout is 504) / idle recycle. |

| `respBuffer` | `0` | Parsed; responses always stream (`check` warns if set). |

| `clientCertFile` / `clientKeyFile` httpjet | none | Upstream mTLS client identity for `https://`/`h2s://` targets; must lie within an admin resource root when submitted via the API. |

| `env` (repeatable) | — | `K=V` worker environment. Server-computed CGI names are protected. |

| `path`, `backlog`, `instances`, `autoStart`, `runOnStartUp` | — / `100` / `1` / `0` / `0` | LSAPI worker binary and supervision (`instances>1` warns: one fixed upstream). |

| *`phpConfig` additionally:* `phpHandler` (`command`, `suffixes`), `memSoftLimit`/`memHardLimit`, `maxProcessTime` (0 = unlimited; `--php-max-process-time-ms` overrides), `procSoftLimit`/`procHardLimit`, `extMaxIdleTime`, `backlog` default 1024, `detachedMode`. |

## Virtual hosts

Declarations live in `httpd_config.xml` (`name`, `vhRoot`, `configFile`, `allowSymbolLink`, `enableScript`, `restrained`); behavior lives in the referenced ` `. `allowSymbolLink` is a tri-state override (file > declaration > server); `restrained` confines the vhost to `vhRoot` and forces symlinks off; `enableScript=0` disables script handlers for the vhost.

| Vhost directive | Meaning |

| `docRoot`, `indexFiles`, `enableExpires`/`expiresByType` | Root and per-vhost overrides of the server settings. |

| ` ` `enable`, `autoLoadHtaccess`, `base`, `rules` | Inline rules run before the `.htaccess` chain. |

| ` ` `allowOverride`, `accessFileName` | `allowOverride 0` kills the whole chain; the access file name defaults to `.htaccess`. |

| ` ` `keyFile`, `certFile`, `certChain`, `CACertFile` | The SNI identity for this vhost's domains (chain material, not a client-verify root). |

| ` ` `enableCache`, `enablePublicCache`, `enablePrivateCache` | Per-vhost page-cache gates (with `--page-cache-standard-vhosts` a missing block gets a default public policy). |

| ` ` `suffix`, `type`, `handler` | Suffix routing to `lsapi`/`php` handlers or a `cgi` handler bound to a FastCGI processor. |

| ` ` `uri`, `address` | WebSocket relay maps (plain TCP HTTP/1 upstreams). |

| ` ` `accessLog`/`errorLog` with `useServer=0`, `fileName`, `rollingSize`, `keepDays`, `logHeaders` httpjet | Per-vhost log files (default roll 50 MB, keep 30 days; `logHeaders` 7 = combined). Log paths are boot-owned. |

| `setUIDMode` (0/1/2), `chrootMode` (0/1/2), `chrootPath`, `suexecUser`/`suexecGroup`, ` ` | Per-vhost PHP isolation (needs the server ` ` gate). Out-of-range modes are hard errors. → |

| ` ` | Vhost-scoped processors (distinct scope from server-level ones). |

## Contexts

Contexts map URI prefixes to terminals (`static`, `proxy`, `redirect`, `php`/`lsapi` via `handler`) and carry per-context overrides:

| Context directive | Default | Meaning |

| `type`, `uri`, `location`, `handler`, `enabled` | — | Kind, prefix, on-disk location (static), processor name (proxy/lsapi). |

| `extraHeaders` | — | Additional response headers for the context. |

| `addDefaultCharset` / `addDefaultCharsetCustomized` | off | Charset appended to text types. |

| `cachePolicy/*` | on | `checkPublicCache`, `checkPrivateCache`, `respectCacheable`, `enableCache`, `enablePrivateCache`, `enablePostCache` — the six LSWS gates, enforced on both cache tiers. |

| `maxReqBodySize` httpjet | inherit | Per-context body cap (413) on every terminal. |

| `responseTimeout` httpjet | inherit | Upstream response-head deadline, seconds (proxy paths). |

| `bandwidthLimit` httpjet | `0` | Egress throttle overriding the server-wide rate. |

| `subFilter` (repeatable) · `subFilterOnce` · `subFilterTypes` · `subFilterMaxBody` httpjet | — · `0` · `text/html` · `4M` | `SEARCH => REPLACEMENT` literal body substitution. The `=>` separator is mandatory — a rule missing it disables the whole context's sub_filter with a warning. → |

           **vhost XML** · a proxied API prefix with overrides
```

     proxy
     /api/
     application
     2M
     15
     http://internal.example => https://example.test
     text/html,application/json

```

## Checking a configuration

           **check**
```
httpjet --root /abs/root check            # summary: listeners, vhost map, fast-memo verdicts, warnings
httpjet --root /abs/root check --strict   # + topology lint, missing docroots, vhost-map-fingerprint; non-zero on findings
```

Run the check under the intended service identity as well as as root: readable-by-root is not proof the runtime user can read certificates or write logs and sockets. The same normalization runs for the write API 's in-memory bundle (`parse_bundle`), which additionally refuses DTDs, more than 64 nesting levels, more than 128 vhosts, and 1 MiB of XML. A config file read from disk is capped at 16 MiB per file (`ConfigError::TooLarge`, 2026-10-06) — a bound on all readers, `check` included.

## Environment variables

The full list, with the flags they pair with, is on the CLI reference . The ones most often set in a unit drop-in: `HTTPJET_ACCESS_LOG_FORMAT=json`, `HTTPJET_ERROR_LOG_FORMAT=json`, `HTTPJET_SYSLOG_TARGET`, `CF_SEND_ZSTD=1`, `HJ_FAST_MEMO=0`, `HTTPJET_OTEL=1`, `RUST_LOG`.

==============================================================================
PAGE: CLI reference (https://httpjet.net/docs/cli)
SUMMARY: Every httpjet subcommand and serve flag, grouped and filterable, plus the environment variables the binary reads.
==============================================================================

# CLI reference

One binary, four subcommands. `--root` is the only global option. Persistent policy lives in the XML; **everything on the command line is an operational override** — addresses, workers, PHP wiring, cache budgets, feature opt-ins. This page is generated from `httpjet serve --help` of v0.1.5 plus the feature-gated flags.

## Subcommands

           **httpjet** [--root DIR] <subcommand>
```
