httpjet --root /abs/root check [--strict]     # parse + summary; --strict lints topology and exits non-zero on findings (deploy gate)
httpjet --root /abs/root serve [flags…]       # bind the configured listeners and serve
httpjet --root /abs/root lsphp [flags…]       # run a standalone persistent lsphp pool (the PHP half of a zero-downtime deploy)
httpjet lsphp-reload [flags…]                 # ask a running pool to replace its worker generation without closing the listener
httpjet --version                             # httpjet 0.1.5
```

| Subcommand · flag | Default | Meaning |

| `--root ` (global) | `/usr/local/lsws` | Server root containing `conf/httpd_config.xml`. Use an absolute path. |

| `check --strict` | off | Hard-error on shared docroots, missing docroots, vhosts without an exact `vhostMap` domain; warn on apex-without-www, TLS over UDS, PROXY protocol on public binds, geo lists without a db, inert LiteSpeed elements, generic CGI contexts, unsupported auth forms; print `vhost-map-fingerprint` and fast-memo verdicts. |

| `lsphp --php-socket` | `/tmp/php8-httpjet.sock` | Socket lsphp listens on — the path `serve --lsphp-external` dials. A systemd-activated fd at the same path is adopted. |

| `lsphp --php-children` | `0` | 0 = honor the XML `PHP_LSAPI_CHILDREN`/`maxConns`; >0 overrides; values below 2 normalize to 2. |

| `lsphp --control-socket` | ` .control` | Root-only control socket used by `lsphp-reload`. Defaults beside the pool socket so a test pool can never answer the production control path. |

| `lsphp --generation-file` | ` .generation` | The 16-byte epoch + marker file external web pools map. Defaults beside the pool socket so a test pool can never advance the production epoch. |

| `lsphp-reload --control-socket` | `/run/httpjet/lsphp-control.sock` | Control socket of the running supervisor. |

| `lsphp-reload --timeout-secs` | `90` | Maximum wait for candidate readiness and old-generation drain. |

## serve flags

Type to filter; click a group to narrow. Defaults are the binary's; *(empty)* means an empty string disables the feature.

| Flag | Default | Meaning |

| Listeners & transport |

| --http-addr   | 127.0.0.1:8080 | Address for the plain-HTTP listener |

| --https-addr   | 127.0.0.1:4443 | Address for the TLS listener. Empty to disable |

| --workers   | — | Number of accept-loop workers (SO_REUSEPORT sockets). Defaults to CPUs |

| --no-core-pinning | off | Do not pin the per-core io_uring transport threads to their CPU cores. Pinning is automatic (and only) when the worker count equals the machine's CPU count; this flag is the kill switch if pinned placement worsens tail latency |

| --uring-ring   | legacy | io_uring ring setup for the per-core transport runtimes. `legacy` (default) = flagless rings — the A/B measured `coop` (COOP_TASKRUN + SUBMIT_ALL) as noise and `defer` (+SINGLE_ISSUER + DEFER_TASKRUN) as a consistent ~-2% on this virtualized guest; both stay available for other hardware. Ring size always stays default — ring memory is memlock-charged and bigger rings under the prod unit's LimitMEMLOCK bankrupt late runtimes (2026-08-27 crash-loop). Unsupported flags fall back to plain rings per-thread with a warning Values: `legacy, coop, defer`. |

| --no-multishot-accept | off | Disable multishot accept: submit one accept SQE per connection (the pre-multishot behavior) instead of one armed SQE per listener |

| --http-uds   | — | Additionally serve plain HTTP on this unix domain socket (H1 + h2c prior knowledge, one accept core). Peers have no address: ACLs and logs see fabricated loopback and the access log renders `unix:` — the socket file's mode/owner is the real access boundary. A socket-activated fd at the same path (socket unit) is adopted for zero-downtime restarts |

| --ktls [ ] | auto | Kernel-TLS on the io_uring TLS path: after the rustls handshake, upgrade the socket to kTLS so H1/H2 serve plaintext over the raw fd (kernel encrypt/decrypt), removing the userspace AEAD copy on large-body egress. Runs only on the io_uring TLS path (the default transport). `auto` (default) requires a `--features ktls` build, a physical default-route NIC, and active `tls-hw-tx-offload`; otherwise it logs one reason and stays on rustls. `on` forces kTLS for isolated benchmarking and fails when the feature is absent; `off` never enables it. A bare `--ktls` remains an alias for `--ktls=on`. TLS 1.3 only (1.2 falls back to userspace); peer KeyUpdate is handled (RX rekey + reply). STAGED — validate on an alt port before production Print help Values: `auto, on, off`. |

| Security & limits |

| --no-mtls | off | Local testing / explicit rollback only: drop the mandatory Cloudflare client-cert requirement so TLS content can be tested locally without a Cloudflare-issued client cert. Without this flag, clientVerify=2 validates every presented certificate during TLS. A peer that presents none completes the handshake, then the request pipeline rejects it before dispatch (except the loopback exemption) |

| --per-ip-rate   | — | Per-client-IP request throttle: max requests per client IP per second. 0 (default) = disabled — overrides the ` ` tuning field when set. Protects the origin from single-source floods; a shared NAT egress aggregates many visitors, so size accordingly |

| --request-decompression-extra   | (empty) | Additional request Content-Encoding values to decode before dispatch. Gzip remains enabled for compatibility; Brotli and zstd are opt-in. Accepted comma-separated values: br,zstd |

| --trusted-proxy-idle-secs   | 0 | Idle window in seconds for connections whose peer presented a VERIFIED client certificate (in prod, only Cloudflare's authenticated-origin-pull cert). CF never resumes TLS to the origin, so closing a connection it would have reused costs a full TCP + TLS + mTLS handshake. 0 keeps the normal 90 s floor for everyone; uncertified peers always keep it |

| --trusted-proxy-idle-max-conns   | 6000 | Above this many open connections, certified connections fall back to the normal idle floor (bounds idle state during a connection surge) |

| --tls-session-tickets   | 2 | TLS 1.3 session tickets issued per full handshake (rustls default 2). 0 stops minting them and shrinks the session cache to TLS 1.2 session IDs: Cloudflare's origin pull never resumes (`httpjet_tls_handshakes_resumed_total` stays 0), so the tickets only cost two records per handshake plus a cached copy of its client-cert chain |

| --auth-user-file-roots   | (empty) | Extra directories (comma-separated) where a `.htaccess` AuthUserFile may live, besides the vhost docroot |

| PHP / LSAPI |

| --no-php | off | Do not spawn lsphp; PHP requests fall back to static serving |

| --php-children   | 0 | LSAPI worker children for the lsphp pool. 0 (default) = honor the lsws config's `PHP_LSAPI_CHILDREN` / `maxConns` (true drop-in). A value > 0 is an explicit override (e.g. to cap concurrency on a shared box); values below 2 are normalized to 2 for persistent supervision |

| --php-socket   | /tmp/php8-httpjet.sock | Socket path for httpjet's OWN lsphp pool — deliberately separate from the production php8.sock so the two never contend |

| --lsphp-external   | — | EXTERNAL lsphp: connect to an lsphp master already listening on this socket (run by a separate `httpjet lsphp` process) instead of spawning one. Lets the web tier restart for a zero-downtime binary deploy without cold- starting PHP. Overrides --php-socket. Mutually exclusive with spawning |

| --lsphp-generation-file   | — | Shared lsphp generation epoch used to invalidate pooled external connections after a supervisor reload or restart. When supplied with --lsphp-external, startup fails if the 16-byte mapping cannot be opened |

| --php-max-process-time-ms   | — | Total request processing deadline in milliseconds. When exceeded, the handler closes the connection (504); in OWNED/spawn mode the monitor also kills+restarts the worker (Tier-2). Under --lsphp-external (prod) there is no monitor in this process, so only the Tier-1 504 applies — a wedged worker is NOT auto-reclaimed here. 0 = no deadline (matches the LiteSpeed XML `maxProcessTime` 0-means-unlimited convention). Absent ⇒ the XML value if present, else no deadline. Must be conservative: too low kills slow renders |

| Page cache |

| --page-cache | off | Enable the LSCache-equivalent origin full-page cache (OFF by default; opt-in / R&D). Per-vhost ` ` + `.htaccess CacheLookup` still gate each request, and the app must opt responses in via `X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control`. With this flag absent the cache is inert |

| --page-cache-mem   | 134217728 | RAM budget (bytes) for the in-process index: entry metadata + precompressed variants + any in-RAM body. With --page-cache-store-path, persisted (tmpfs) bodies do NOT count here — they are bounded by --page-cache-disk-mem instead — so this should be sized for metadata, not body bytes. Without a file tier it is the whole body budget, as before. Default 128 MiB |

| --page-cache-disk-mem   | 2147483648 | tmpfs file-tier footprint budget (bytes) for --page-cache-store-path: the disk LRU evicts the least-recently-served entry once charged file footprint under the store path exceeds this. tmpfs IS RAM, so size it against the box's headroom (with dict compression a 2 GiB cap holds the compressed equivalent of ~7–18 GiB of pages). 0 ⇒ fall back to --page-cache-mem. Ignored without a file tier. Default 2 GiB |

| --page-cache-store-path   | none | Directory for the PERSISTENT tmpfs file tier. The default is "none": bodies stay in the in-process RAM cache and flush on restart. Pass an explicit directory such as /dev/shm/jetcache to opt into the LiteSpeed-Enterprise-style store where bodies live as files and the cache survives restarts via a boot-time warm scan. The LiteSpeed config's cacheStorePath is intentionally NOT used |

| --page-cache-integrity-key   | /usr/local/httpjet/conf/.jetcache.key | Integrity key used for persistent cache containers |

| --page-cache-integrity-required | off | Refuse to start the file tier when the integrity key cannot be installed, instead of running with untagged containers |

| --page-cache-hot-mem   | 201326592 | Byte cap of the in-RAM hot tier in front of the file store (zero-syscall zero-copy serves for the hottest bodies). Only meaningful with --page-cache-store-path. Default 192 MiB |

| --page-cache-dict   | (empty) | Path to a shared zstd dictionary used to store cached bodies far smaller. CMS pages share ~60%+ of their bytes as position-shifted boilerplate that only a dictionary captures; with this set, `cache_store` dict-compresses the stored body (the SERVED bytes stay standard zstd/br/gzip — browsers/CF can't decode a private dict). Absent/empty/unreadable ⇒ bodies are stored as plain identity (today's behaviour). Build one from a reviewed local corpus with scripts/train-pagecache-dict-from-files.sh |

| --page-cache-dict-vhost   | (empty) | Comma-separated `vhost=path` pairs: a PER-VHOST zstd dictionary, trained on that vhost's own content (train one local corpus per vhost). A shared dictionary trained on one site's boilerplate does little for a differently templated site, so each vhost compresses against its own. A vhost not listed here falls back to --page-cache-dict if set, else stores identity (today's behaviour). Example: `forum.example=conf/pagecache-forum.dict,moon.example=conf/pagecache-moon.dict` |

| --page-cache-dict-level   | (empty) | Comma-separated `vhost=level` pairs overriding the internal zstd level (1-19, default 12) of that vhost's dictionary. A vhost whose compressed bodies round to the same 4 KiB tmpfs pages at a cheaper level gains nothing from 12 (one production vhost costs 5× less at level 3 with no footprint change). A malformed pair aborts startup |

| --page-cache-vary-default   | (empty) | Comma-separated `name=value` pairs: a vary cookie carrying this value is keyed like no cookie (the app treats the default the same way). E.g. `xf_style_id=50` |

| --page-cache-opt-in-status   | (empty) | Comma-separated extra statuses (from 303, 404, 410) cached only when the app sends an explicit `X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: public`, with the TTL capped at 300 s and no stale windows. Empty = off (only 200/301 are cached) |

| --page-cache-303-prefixes   | (empty) | Comma-separated request-path prefixes under which an opted-in 303 may be stored (e.g. `/whats-new/`). A 303 anywhere else is never stored |

| --page-cache-stream-fill-vhosts   | (empty) | Comma-separated vhost names whose cacheable page-cache misses WITHOUT a Content-Length (progressive template output) are sent to the client as the backend writes them and stored once the backend finishes, instead of being buffered whole first. Only identity-encoded public 200s; a body that errors, is cut short or grows past the object cap is served but never stored. Empty = off |

| --page-cache-admit-threshold   | 2 | (W-TinyLFU) Base admission bar: minimum frequency a cacheable response must show before it is STORED. One request counts as ONE sighting — the on-core fast path probes uncounted and records only a hit it serves. 2 = store on the 2nd sighting (miss-miss-hit; rejects the long-tail of one-hit-wonders — the default). 1 = store on the 1st sighting (miss-hit; cache everything — now cheap with --page-cache-dict, with the store's byte LRU protecting the hot set). Size-weighting adds +1 per 256 KiB on top. Watch httpjet_cache_hit_ratio_real to tune |

| --page-cache-vary-cookies   | xf_style_variation,xf_style_id,xf_language_id | Comma-separated public-vary cookie names: a cacheable public response may declare `X-LiteSpeed-Vary: cookie=NAME,...` and the entry is keyed by these cookies' values (shared, non-sensitive prefs). Default matches the XenForo style/language set |

| --page-cache-private-cookies   | xf_session,xf_user | Comma-separated cookie names that forbid public caching if a public response tries to Set-Cookie them (session guard). Default: XenForo |

| --page-cache-private | off | Enable the per-session PRIVATE cache tier: an `X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: private[,max-age=N]` response from a logged-in request is stored keyed by the session cookie and served only to that same session. OFF by default — without the flag a private opt-in bypasses exactly as before |

| --page-cache-private-session-cookie   | xf_session | Request cookie whose VALUE keys a private entry's owner (the session) |

| --page-cache-private-user-cookie   | xf_user | Request cookie whose PRESENCE routes a request to the private tier (the logged-in marker; XenForo's remember cookie) |

| --page-cache-shared-paths   | (empty) | Comma-separated matchers for visitor-invariant endpoints that MEMBER (logged-in) requests may still read/populate on the PUBLIC cache tier — sharing one entry across guests and every member session instead of duplicating per session and re-rendering each member's first view through PHP. Two matcher forms: `PATH?PARAM` (path equals PATH exactly AND the query carries `PARAM=`, e.g. `proxy.php?image`) and `PATH` (path prefix, e.g. `/wf-unfurl/image`); a missing leading `/` is normalized on. ONLY list endpoints whose bytes are identical for every visitor (HMAC-gated image proxies) — never HTML pages. Malformed specs abort startup. Empty/absent = feature inert (kill switch; members keep today's private routing). GLOBAL like the other --page-cache-private-* knobs — not per-vhost — but a matching request still passes every per-vhost public gate (`vhost` cache policy, `.htaccess` CacheLookup) and every public-store guard before it is served or stored |

| --page-cache-shared-paths-canary-percent   | 100 | Deterministic percentage (0-100) of member requests matching --page-cache-shared-paths that actually route to the public tier; the rest keep today's private-tier behavior. Sticky per member (bucketed by a hash of the user/session cookie value, exactly like --xf-capsule-member-canary-percent), so one member never flickers between tiers. 100 = all matching requests |

| --page-cache-standard-vhosts   | (empty) | Comma-separated vhost names put into "standards mode": they honor a standard `Cache-Control: public, max-age=N` as a cache opt-in (OpenLiteSpeed's `checkPublicCache` equivalent), get a default public cache policy when they declare no ` ` block, and default `CacheLookup` to on — so a non-LiteSpeed app (e.g. moon.example) caches like a standards-compliant shared cache. ALLOWLIST, not a global switch: a vhost not listed is unaffected (X-LiteSpeed opt-in only), so opting one content site in can't make an unrelated vhost (status/admin API) cache a response it merely marked public. All other guards (GET-only, Set-Cookie/private-cookie, vary, status, self-redirect) always apply |

| --page-cache-stale-default-secs   | 0 | Stale-while-revalidate window (seconds) applied when the app declares none. 0 = off (serve only fresh unless the app sets stale-while-revalidate / max-stale) |

| --page-cache-stale-max-secs   | 86400 | Hard cap (seconds) on the stale-while-revalidate window honored from the app |

| --page-cache-stale-if-error-max-secs   | 86400 | Hard cap (seconds) on the stale-if-error window honored from the app |

| --page-cache-stale-if-error-default-secs   | 0 | Stale-if-error window (seconds) applied when the app declares none: how long past freshness a public entry stays servable as a backend-5xx fallback (a brief lsphp/DB outage serves slightly-stale pages instead of error pages). 0 = off (the prior behavior: only an app-declared stale-if-error window arms the fallback) |

| XenForo capsules |

| --xf-capsule | off | Enable XenForo public-shell capsules. Requires --page-cache; otherwise inert |

| --xf-capsule-vhosts   | (empty) | Comma-separated resolved vhost names allowed to serve capsules. Empty DISABLES the capsule tier for every vhost (#239 fail-closed default) |

| --xf-capsule-paths   | /,/forums/,/threads/,/whats-new/,/help/ | Comma-separated request-path prefixes eligible for capsule lookup/store |

| --xf-capsule-safe-get-mode   | prefixes | Capsule route coverage. `prefixes` honors --xf-capsule-paths; `all-get-classified` uses a conservative unsafe-route classifier Values: `prefixes, all-get-classified`. |

| --xf-capsule-stale-secs   | 86400 | Stale-while-revalidate window for capsule shell entries. This is applied to public-shell capsule stores even if the app declares a smaller window |

| --xf-capsule-canary-percent   | 100 | Deterministic percentage of eligible requests that may be served a capsule hit |

| --xf-capsule-members | off | Allow explicitly-marked member-cookie requests to receive public-shell capsules |

| --xf-capsule-member-canary-percent   | 0 | Deterministic percentage of eligible member-cookie requests that may receive capsules |

| Performance knobs |

| --no-fast-memo | off | Disable the finished-response memo on the on-core static fast path (default ON; per-thread, 1 s TTL, byte-identity-gated — see `pipeline::fast_memo`). Env `HJ_FAST_MEMO=0` is equivalent |

| --cf-send-zstd | off | Compress responses to a trusted-proxy (Cloudflare) peer as zstd, ignoring the forwarded Accept-Encoding. CF asks the origin for br/gzip but decodes an origin `Content-Encoding: zstd` and re-encodes per browser at its edge — so this hands CF the cheapest-to-produce form (zstd ≪ brotli to compress) without changing what browsers receive. Officially unsupported CF↔origin; opt-in, default off. Never applies to untrusted (direct) clients. Off ⇒ byte-identical to today |

| --rewrite-outcome-ttl-ms   | 1000 | TTL in milliseconds for the rewrite-outcome cache (memoized rewrite decisions for `path_cacheable` chains, keyed by vhost/scheme/ method/host/path/query + any keyable header vars). 0 disables the cache entirely. The default (1000 ms) matches the historical hard-coded TTL — it bounds `-f`/`-d` filesystem staleness exactly like the StatCache and lets `.htaccess` edits take effect within ~1 s |

| --rewrite-ua-classify | off | Key UA-reading rewrite chains by the bitmap of matching User-Agent RewriteConds instead of the raw UA string, when parse-time analysis proves the outcome depends on the UA only through those match results. Collapses real-world UA diversity (near-zero hit rate on raw UAs) onto a handful of outcome-cache entries. Default OFF — enabling is a deploy-time decision |

| Memory |

| --mimalloc-trim-secs   | 120 | Interval (seconds) for the background mimalloc OS-trim that calls mi_collect(force) to hand retained/cold arena pages back to the OS (counters the swap retention seen in prod after a burst). 0 = disable |

| --mimalloc-trim-threshold-mib   | 768 | Only run the mimalloc trim (periodic and after a connection close) when process RSS+swap (read from /proc/self/status) is at least this many MiB; 0 = always. Lets a healthy process skip the collect entirely. Default 768: above a cache-less steady state (~360 MiB). Size it above the deployment's healthy peak (a large page cache holds 1-2 GiB) so only genuine post-burst arena retention trips the safety-net reclaim |

| Observability |

| --metrics-addr   | 127.0.0.1:9090 | Loopback-only Prometheus metrics endpoint address. Empty to disable. Exposes the page-cache hit/miss ratio (the key operational number once --page-cache is live) plus request/connection counters |

| --telemetry-file   | (empty) | Append a cumulative per-request telemetry snapshot row to this file every --telemetry-flush-secs: durability across restarts + a self-contained time-series for the two-node A/B. Empty = no disk flush (the in-RAM aggregates + the :9090 endpoint still work). e.g. logs/telemetry.tsv |

| --telemetry-flush-secs   | 30 | Snapshot flush interval in seconds (only used when --telemetry-file is set). Fixed RAM; ~1 MB/day on disk at the default |

| --php-slow-log   | (empty) | Per-request PHP render log: a TSV line for every LSAPI request whose render TTFB exceeds --php-slow-threshold-ms, plus a 1-in-128 sample of ALL PHP requests as the population baseline — the per-URL / user-class attribution behind the lsapi_ttfb histogram. Rolls at 64 MiB, gzip archives, 30-day prune. Empty = disabled. e.g. logs/php-slow.tsv |

| --php-slow-threshold-ms   | 50 | "Slow" threshold in milliseconds for --php-slow-log |

| --request-id-header | off | Echo the per-request correlation id (also in the access/error/php-slow logs) as an `X-Request-Id` response header, so a client/CDN can join a response to the server-side logs. Off by default |

| --profile-token   | (empty) | Bearer secret required for profiling and sensitive metrics diagnostics. Empty disables those routes; ordinary metrics scraping stays available. Visible in /proc/*/cmdline; prefer `--profile-token-file` |

| Admin API |

| --admin-addr   | — | Opt-in read-only operational JSON endpoint (loopback TCP only) |

| --admin-write-addr   | — | Authenticated application-config writes on a separate loopback listener |

| --admin-token-file   | — | Private file containing a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal bearer token |

| --admin-resource-root   | — | Allowed existing filesystem root for submitted resources; repeatable |

| WAF sidecar |

| --waf-sidecar-addr   | — | Opt-in HTTP request-inspection sidecar: `unix:/path` (its listener's uid is verified) or a loopback `ip:port` (unauthenticated). The sidecar must return 204 to allow or 403 to block; absent keeps the WAF seam inert |

| --waf-sidecar-uid   | — | The uid a `unix:` sidecar must run as. Default: root or this process's uid |

| --waf-sidecar-path   | /inspect |  |

| --waf-timeout-ms   | 100 |  |

| --waf-body-max   | 65536 |  |

| --waf-concurrency   | 128 |  |

| --waf-fail-open | off | Continue when the configured WAF sidecar is unavailable or malformed. Default is fail-closed (503); this weaker policy requires explicit opt-in |

| ACME (--features acme) |

| --acme-directory   | — | ACME directory URL (HTTPS). Requires --acme-domains, --acme-store and --acme-accept-terms; nothing runs without all four. |

| --acme-domains   | — | Comma-separated DNS identifiers (1–100, ASCII A-labels). Wildcards need DNS-01. Quote a wildcard in the shell. |

| --acme-store   | — | Pre-provisioned private directory, mode 0700, owned by the service uid; holds atomic account/order/certificate snapshots and the DNS cleanup journal. |

| --acme-accept-terms | off | Explicit agreement to the CA terms of service. |

| --acme-bootstrap | off | Start with no listener default certificate; TLS handshakes fail until issuance succeeds. No self-signed placeholder. |

| --acme-reconcile-order   | — | One-shot recovery of an ambiguous newOrder from the same account's CA records. |

| --acme-dns-webhook   | — | Provider-neutral DNS controller endpoint (selects DNS-01). Requires --acme-dns-zones. |

| --acme-dns-zones   | — | Zone allowlist for TXT operations. |

| --acme-dns-token-file   | — | Bearer token for the controller: regular single-link file, mode 0600, 16–4096 printable characters. |

| --acme-test-mode | off | Loopback CA HTTP and alternate loopback validation ports for fixtures only; serving addresses must be loopback. |

| --acme-test-ca-root · --acme-test-issuer-root · --acme-dns-test-root   | — | Replace trust roots for the test CA / issuance / DNS controller without disabling verification (test mode only). |

| OCSP (--features ocsp) |

| --ocsp-responder   | — | Explicit HTTP(S) responder for every enabled certificate issuer. Applies regardless of the XML enableStapling boolean; disables TLS resumption. |

| --ocsp-required | off | Refuse new TLS handshakes without a fresh authenticated GOOD response (also implied by Must-Staple). |

| --ocsp-test-mode | off | Permit a literal-loopback responder, with loopback serving addresses only. |

| --xf-capsule-dedicated-store | off | Also store every capsule-capable page under a DEDICATED (admission-exempt) key. Off by default since 2026-10-04: members are served from the shell-capable PUBLIC entry, which keeps one copy per page and lets the admission gate govern every store |

        !   Removed flags
`--cache-peer` / `--cache-peer-fill*` (cross-node cache peers) and `--cache-purge-secret-file` are gone; the purge endpoint is loopback-gated. `--io-uring` / `--io-uring-h3` never existed as opt-ins — the io_uring transport is unconditional.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Meaning |

| `HTTPJET_ACCESS_LOG_FORMAT` | combined | `json` selects JSON access lines (fixed field order: `ts, client_ip, remote_user, method, uri, protocol, status, bytes, referer, user_agent, reqid`). |

| `HTTPJET_ERROR_LOG_FORMAT` | text | `json` selects JSON error events (`schema_version 1`, credential redaction, bounded fields). Independent of the access format; does not change the stdout/journald tracing formatter. Restart to change; rotate first to avoid mixed files. |

| `HTTPJET_ACCESS_ROLLING_BYTES` / `HTTPJET_ACCESS_KEEP_DAYS` | 50 MB / 30 | Unified access-log rolling size and retention. |

| `HTTPJET_LOG_DIR` | unset | Redirect every opened log file (unified and per-vhost) into this directory so isolated test or PGO runs never touch production log paths. |

| `HTTPJET_URING_NO_IOWAIT` | unset | `1` sets `IORING_FEAT_NO_IOWAIT` on supported kernels so network-wait time on io_uring rings is not accounted as system iowait. |

| `HTTPJET_SYSLOG_TARGET` | unset | Mirror every rendered access line to syslog: `udp://host:514`, bare `host:port`, or a unix-dgram path such as `/run/systemd/journal/syslog`. Sent from the writer task; failures counted, never fatal. |

| `HTTPJET_SYSLOG_FACILITY` · `_SEVERITY` · `_RFC` · `_HOSTNAME` · `_APP_NAME` | `daemon` · `info` · `5424` · server name · `httpjet` | Syslog framing (`3164` for the BSD format). |

| `CF_SEND_ZSTD` | unset | `1` ≡ `--cf-send-zstd`. |

| `HJ_FAST_MEMO` | `1` | `0` ≡ `--no-fast-memo`. |

| `HTTPJET_OTEL` · `HTTPJET_OTEL_METRICS` | unset | `1` enables OTLP tracing / metrics (`--features otel`; startup fails if the feature is absent). |

| `HTTPJET_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO` | `0.01` | Root-span ratio sampler, 0–1. |

| `HTTPJET_OTEL_TRUSTED_PARENTS` | empty | Comma-separated exact gateway IPs (≤128) allowed to supply a W3C `traceparent`; everyone else starts a new root. |

| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` · `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT` (+ SDK header settings) | — | Complete collector URLs, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces`. |

| `RUST_LOG` | `info` | Tracing filter for the error log / journal, e.g. `RUST_LOG=debug,hj_rewrite=trace`. |

| `HJ_ROOT`, `HJ_URING_*`, `HJ_PEBBLE_*`, `HTTPJET_*_TEST_CHILD` | — | Test-harness variables only. |

## Exit behavior and signals

- **SIGHUP**: Reload configuration and certificates through the publication coordinator; a bad config keeps the current generation (see Admin API & reload ).

- **SIGTERM / SIGINT**: Graceful shutdown: stop accepting, GOAWAY h2, drain within the unit's `TimeoutStopSec`, close the admin coordinator, flush logs and telemetry, bounded OTel shutdown.

- **Argument validation**: Public admin binds, missing companion options (`--admin-token-file`, `--admin-resource-root`, ACME requirements), malformed `--page-cache-shared-paths` or `--page-cache-vary-default` / `--page-cache-dict-level` pairs, an unopenable generation file, or a rejected WAF configuration fail startup before any socket is bound; `--page-cache-integrity-required` additionally refuses to start the file tier when the integrity key cannot be installed.

- **Socket activation**: Inherited fds are adopted by address/path; their count must match `--workers` for TCP listeners.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Operations (https://httpjet.net/docs/operations)
SUMMARY: Systemd socket activation, the persistent PHP pool, safe changes, deploy gates, rollback, kill switches, and the hardened OCI example.
==============================================================================

# Operations & deployment

httpjet is designed for a conventional Linux service: a dedicated account, the LiteSpeed-compatible tree, **systemd socket activation** so a binary deploy never refuses a connection, and a **separate persistent PHP pool** so a web-tier restart never cold-starts opcache. The checked-in units are generic references; a hardened OCI example covers container adoption.

## Installation

No signed packages are published yet; build from source and install the binary at a stable path *outside* Cargo's `target/` so a later `cargo clean` cannot delete what a running unit depends on.

           source install
```
cargo build --locked --release -p httpjet
sudo useradd --system --home-dir /var/lib/httpjet --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin httpjet
sudo install -d /usr/local/httpjet/bin /usr/local/httpjet/conf /usr/local/httpjet/logs
sudo install -m0755 target/release/httpjet /usr/local/httpjet/bin/httpjet

# an existing LiteSpeed tree works as-is — validate it first, as root AND as the service user
sudo /usr/local/httpjet/bin/httpjet --root /usr/local/lsws check --strict
sudo -u httpjet /usr/local/httpjet/bin/httpjet --root /usr/local/lsws check --strict

# minimal loopback example unit (no TLS, no PHP, no cache)
sudo install -m0644 packaging/systemd/httpjet-example.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now httpjet-example
```

        !   Review before start
The example units bind loopback and use example document roots. Set listeners, domains, docroots, TLS material, writable paths and the service identity deliberately before enabling a public service. A permission-preparing `ExecStartPre` that runs as root and then drops to the unprivileged account is the reference shape.

## The systemd model

> [Diagram: systemd-units] Five units. The socket units own the listening fds; the boot gate keeps the public listeners closed until the PHP pool can answer; the web tier adopts the fds and dials the pool. Restarting the web tier or reloading the pool never closes a listener.

| Unit | Role |

| `httpjet.socket` | N× `:80` TCP, N× `:443` TCP, N× `:443` UDP with `ReusePort=yes`, `Backlog=8192`. The multiplicity reproduces the per-worker SO_REUSEPORT fan-out, so N must equal `serve --workers`. Static (not enabled under `sockets.target`); pulled in by the service after the gate to avoid a cold-boot ordering cycle. |

| `httpjet-boot-ready.service` | Boot-only oneshot gate, availability-first: the `Type=notify` LSAPI pool is the one hard dependency; databases/caches are ordered but not required — it waits up to 300 s, then proceeds with a loud warning so a cold boot with a slow database still serves static + warm cache + stale-if-error. Later backend maintenance cannot tear down the sockets. |

| `httpjet.service` | The web tier: `httpjet --root … serve --lsphp-external … --lsphp-generation-file …` under a dedicated user, `Restart=always`, `OOMScoreAdjust=-500`, `LimitNOFILE=1048576`, `TimeoutStopSec=20`, `Conflicts=lshttpd.service`. Effective flags come from drop-ins in `httpjet.service.d/` — check `systemctl show -p ExecStart --value httpjet.service` before reasoning about them. The repository ships a validated **hardening drop-in** (`systemd/httpjet.service.d/zz-hardening.conf`: `ProtectSystem=strict` with logs-only `ReadWritePaths`, `PrivateTmp/PrivateDevices`, `ProtectProc=invisible`, empty capability set, `MemoryDenyWriteExecute`, `RestrictAddressFamilies`, and a **log-only seccomp stage** that filters the dangerous syscall groups while logging — enforce `@system-service` only after a clean soak), measured `systemd-analyze security` 9.0 → 1.9; it is the reference copy, not applied by the checked-in unit. |

| `httpjet-lsphp.socket` | Owns the LSAPI Unix listener (mode 0600, backlog 8192, `RemoveOnStop`). Never restart it during a reload or supervisor deploy. |

| `httpjet-lsphp.service` | `httpjet lsphp …`, `Type=notify` (active only after a marker-attributed LSAPI response), `ExecReload=httpjet lsphp-reload …`, its own identity, `RuntimeDirectory=httpjet` for the control socket and generation file. |

| `httpjet-edge-firewall.service` | Optional oneshot edge firewall (`scripts/httpjet-edge-firewall.sh`) for origins without a cloud firewall: restricts new `:80`/`:443` connections to Cloudflare IPv4 + private ranges (keep its list in step with the XML `T` entries). |

        i   Scope of the zero-loss guarantee
Socket activation eliminates RSTs of *new and queued* connections across a deploy. Requests the old process has already accepted — h1/h2 mid-serve and especially h3/QUIC streams — still drain under `TimeoutStopSec`. "Never drops a connection" means never RSTs a new or queued one.

## The persistent PHP pool

Static and proxy deployments need no PHP. For LSAPI, run the pool as its own unit and point the web tier at it; the units above wire the socket, the root-only control socket and the 16-byte generation file. Routine opcache recycle is `systemctl reload httpjet-lsphp.service` — synchronous and candidate-first. Reserve a hard restart of the pool *service* for supervisor binary/unit changes; verify the listener inode is unchanged before and after. Reference: LSAPI & PHP .

           replace the supervisor without closing the listener
```
before=$(stat -Lc '%d:%i' /run/httpjet/php.sock)
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl restart httpjet-lsphp.service                 # the SERVICE only — never the .socket
test "$(stat -Lc '%d:%i' /run/httpjet/php.sock)" = "$before"
test "$(stat -Lc %s /run/httpjet/lsphp.generation)" = 16
ss -xlnH | awk '$5 == "/run/httpjet/php.sock" {print $4}'    # Send-Q should equal the XML backlog
```

## Safe change workflow

- **Edit in a reviewable change** Configuration tree or application content.

- **`check --strict`** The deploy gate. SIGHUP with a broken config keeps the old generation, but the check should catch it first.

- **Test in isolation** Alternate ports, a separate PHP socket, a separate cache store path, low worker/child counts. Kill test instances by exact PID; a leaked SO_REUSEPORT instance silently shares the port with independent cache and htaccess state.

- **Apply** `systemctl reload httpjet` (SIGHUP) for vhost/rewrite/access/expires/tuning/certificate changes; `systemctl restart httpjet` for the binary or boot-owned resources; the write API for validated in-memory replacement.

- **Verify on loopback, then watch** `curl -sk -H 'Host: …' https://127.0.0.1/…`, the journal, `httpjet_requests_total` and 5xx counters. Purge any outer cache if an incorrect cacheable response reached it.

## Binary deploy and rollback

> [Diagram: deploy-flow] The deploy gate chain. The repository's scripts/deploy-lscache.sh automates this for one deployment (strict check, co-listener guard, external-lsphp recurrence guard, health probe with automatic revert to the previous binary, capsule purge gate); the shape is what matters for any deployment.

- **Kill switch: cache**: Drop `--page-cache` from the unit (a drop-in override) and restart; the cache code is inert without the flag.

- **Kill switch: capsules**: Drop the `--xf-capsule*` flags and restart.

- **Kill switch: fast memo**: `--no-fast-memo` or `HJ_FAST_MEMO=0`.

- **Kill switch: WAF**: Remove `--waf-sidecar-addr` (the seam is completely inert without it).

- **Rollback**: Keep the previous binary beside the current one (`bin/httpjet.prev`); restore and restart. A rollback does not remove bad objects already stored in the origin cache (purge) or at the CDN edge (purge the zone).

- **Start limits**: `StartLimitBurst=5` per 60 s: more than five restarts a minute trips systemd and takes the service down until `systemctl reset-failed`. The persistence gate restarts the service — run it once.

The production build uses profile-guided optimization (`scripts/build-pgo.sh`: instrument → drive a representative loopback workload → rebuild). PGO scratch data is kept off tmpfs. Never benchmark a non-PGO binary against a PGO one.

## What SIGHUP reloads

Vhost maps, rewrites, document roots, contexts, access/expires/tuning settings, cache policy gates, and TLS certificates on an unchanged listener topology. Signal streams (`SIGHUP`, `SIGUSR1`, `SIGUSR2`) are registered immediately at runtime startup so a certbot or reload signal arriving during boot queues cleanly instead of terminating the process. A change that needs a restart (listener addresses, QUIC enablement, PHP topology, cache-store identity, privileges, log paths) is logged as "requires a restart — keeping current config" and nothing changes. A reload that would 404 a mapped vhost because its per-vhost file failed to load is refused. The dictionary registry is retained across SIGHUP (rotation needs a restart). Full semantics: Admin API & reload .

## Observability checklist

           the loopback-only surfaces
```
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9090/metrics | grep '^httpjet_'          # Prometheus text
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /etc/httpjet/profile.token)" http://127.0.0.1:9090/cache-entries   # cache totals, budgets, health line
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9091/v1/status | jq .                     # with --admin-addr: generation, fingerprint, upstream health
curl -sk https://127.0.0.1/__hj_cache_ready -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'
journalctl -u httpjet -n 100
```

Metric families, log formats, the request-id header, telemetry TSV, PHP slow log, OpenTelemetry and profiling are all on Observability . Pair the counters with a process monitor (the tree ships a `monit` check whose start timeout stays above the boot gate's worst case).

## Hardened OCI example

`packaging/oci/` is an adoption example, not a prescription. The image runs as numeric UID/GID `10001:10001`, binds unprivileged ports, needs no capabilities; the compose file adds a read-only root filesystem, drops every capability, sets `no-new-privileges`, and mounts a small `noexec,nosuid,nodev` `/tmp`. Because Moby's default seccomp allowlist omits io_uring, `seccomp-httpjet.json` is the pinned Moby default plus only `io_uring_setup`, `io_uring_enter` and `io_uring_register` (ptrace/`process_vm_*` gated on `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`).

| Path | Access | Purpose |

| `/run/httpjet-certs` | read-only | TLS certificate + key (no key ships in the image; generate one for `example.test`). |

| `/var/lib/httpjet` | read-write | Page-cache files and the integrity key. |

| `/etc/httpjet/litespeed/logs` | read-write | Access/error logs. |

| `/etc/httpjet/litespeed/{conf,example}` | image read-only | LiteSpeed XML and static content. |

| `/tmp` | bounded tmpfs | Temporary runtime files. |

           build, run, smoke
```
docker compose -f packaging/oci/compose.yaml up --build     # publishes 8080/tcp, 8443/tcp AND 8443/udp
docker run … --security-opt seccomp=/abs/path/seccomp-httpjet.json …   # a hand-written run must pass the profile explicitly
bash scripts/oci-smoke.sh                                    # read-only root, UID 10001, caps dropped, real HTTP/3 through the UDP port
```

A seccomp denial is a startup/test failure — do not work around it with `--privileged`, `--cap-add` or `seccomp=unconfined`; narrow the runtime policy or pick a supported host. Rootless engines may add memlock, UDP or io_uring restrictions of their own. The image health check calls `/__hj_cache_ready`, so readiness means the cache boot scan finished, not that a user URL was warmed.

## Release and upgrade discipline

A public release must provide portable x86_64 and aarch64 artifacts, checksums, signatures or attestations, an SBOM, the GPL-3.0 license text and a documented Linux/kernel/libc floor; architecture-tuned PGO helpers must not be uploaded as generic binaries (production builds and gathers PGO natively on each architecture). Upgrades preserve the tree, dictionaries and state; stage and validate the new binary before restart; keep a known-good binary. Dictionary rotation: write the new file atomically, validate, restart, expect old-generation cache entries to become safe misses. Dependency upgrades run through `scripts/update-deps.sh` and the full suite (the 0.1.x sweeps refreshed tokio 1.54, rustls 0.23.46, rustls-webpki 0.103.16 + webpki-roots 1.0.10, fancy-regex 0.20, parking_lot 0.13 and zstd 0.14.3; a daily dependency-advisory job fails the build on any RustSec finding).

==============================================================================
PAGE: Observability (https://httpjet.net/docs/observability)
SUMMARY: Prometheus metrics, the cache-entries report, access and error logs in text or JSON, syslog, request ids, telemetry, the PHP slow log, OpenTelemetry, and profiling.
==============================================================================

# Observability

Everything httpjet tells you about itself: **Prometheus metrics** on a loopback listener, the **cache-entries** report, access and error **logs** in text or JSON with an optional syslog tap, per-request **correlation ids**, the telemetry TSV and PHP slow log, opt-in **OpenTelemetry** traces and metrics, and the profiling endpoints. All control surfaces are loopback-only by design.

## Prometheus metrics

`--metrics-addr` (default `127.0.0.1:9090`; empty disables) serves `/metrics` in the Prometheus text format. Over 130 series today; the families that matter, grouped:

| Metric | Type | Meaning |

| Requests & connections |

| httpjet_requests_total · httpjet_active_requests · httpjet_active_connections | counter / gauge | Served requests, requests in the response-head phase, open connections. |

| httpjet_requests_by_vhost · httpjet_responses_by_vhost · httpjet_request_duration_by_vhost_seconds | labeled | Per-vhost volume, status class and handle() wall time. |

| httpjet_status_{2xx,3xx,4xx,5xx} · httpjet_status_{400,403,404,410,414,429,500,502,503,504} | counter | Status classes and the interesting exact codes. |

| httpjet_proto_{h1,h2,h3} · httpjet_served_{static,php,proxy} | counter | Wire protocol and terminal mix. |

| httpjet_request_duration_seconds · httpjet_phase_{rewrite,cache_lookup,compress,upstream}_seconds | histogram | Total handle() time and sampled per-stage costs (upstream = proxy checkout → response head). |

| httpjet_tls_handshakes_{full,resumed}_total · httpjet_conn_{idle,peer}_closes_total | counter | Full vs resumed TLS handshakes; connection closes by idle timeout vs peer FIN/RST. |

| httpjet_h2_rapid_reset_drops_total · httpjet_h3_send_stall_resets_total | counter | H2 connections dropped on rapid-reset budget exhaustion; H3 response streams reset on send stall. |

| httpjet_throttle_{allowed,rejected}_total | counter | Per-IP throttle decisions (0 when disabled). |

| httpjet_body_buffer_{bytes,capacity_bytes,rejected_total} | gauge / counter | The process-wide request-body budget. |

| Fast path & rewrite |

| httpjet_fast_memo_{hits,stores,ineligible}_total | counter | Finished-response memo activity; *ineligible* = the chain refused the store (see `httpjet check`). |

| httpjet_fast_cookie_{none,member_session,benign_only}_total · httpjet_fast_bridge_total{reason} | counter | Cookie shape of fast-path GET/HEADs and attribution of why a GET/HEAD fell off the on-core fast path into the tokio bridge. |

| httpjet_rewrite_outcome_{hits,misses,uncacheable}_total · httpjet_rewrite_ua_classify_entries | counter / gauge | Rewrite-outcome cache and UA-classification table size. |

| Page cache |

| httpjet_pagecache_{hits,misses,stores,purges,purges_received,store_purge_rejections,expired_misses}_total · httpjet_pagecache_hit_ratio · httpjet_cache_hit_ratio_real | counter / gauge | Core activity; `_real` excludes loopback probes; `httpjet_cache_{hits,misses}_by_vhost{vhost}` split it per vhost and `httpjet_pagecache_evictions_total` counts size/TTL teardowns. Telemetry twins `httpjet_cache_{hits,misses,bypass,stale_serves,sie_serves,admitted,rejected}` and `httpjet_disp_*` (why a response was or wasn't stored) plus `httpjet_cache_admit_ratio`. |

| httpjet_pagecache_entries · _memory_bytes · _hot_bytes · _decoded_entries · _meta_{raw,compressed}_bytes · _tag_{keys,memberships,index_bytes} · _tag_purge_{tombstones,floor_milliseconds} | gauge | Exact RAM accounting of the index and tag indexes. |

| httpjet_pagecache_disk_{bytes,max_bytes} · _disk_evictions_total · _disk_evict_age_{lt_1h,1h_6h,6h_24h,ge_24h}_total · _swept_expired_total | gauge / counter | File-tier footprint vs budget, LRU evictions by entry age, proactive expiry sweeps. |

| httpjet_pagecache_disk_{read,write,full}_errors_total · _missing_file_invalidations_total · _orphan_{reclaimed,deferred}_total · _meta_decode_errors_total · _key_id_collisions_total · _poisoned_locks_total | counter | Health: every one of these should be flat. Poisoned locks nonzero = indexes may be inconsistent. `httpjet_pagecache_integrity_active` = 1 once the file-tier integrity key is installed. |

| httpjet_pagecache_dict_recompress_total · _dict_recompress_bytes_total · httpjet_pagecache_refresh_inflight | counter / gauge | Store-time dictionary recompressions (bounded background pool); stale-while-revalidate refreshes in flight. |

| httpjet_pagecache_shared_path_{public_routes,canary_skipped}_total · _shared_paths_{matchers,canary_percent} | counter / gauge | Shared-paths routing. |

| httpjet_xf_capsule_{hits,misses,stale_hits,dedicated_stores,canary_filtered}_total · _hits_by_class_total · _shell_age_secs | counter / histogram | XenForo capsule tier. |

| httpjet_process_rss_bytes · httpjet_process_rss_anon_bytes · httpjet_pagecache_unaccounted_rss_anon_bytes | gauge | Process RSS and the part the cache accounting cannot explain. |

| LSAPI / PHP |

| httpjet_lsapi_{acquire,dispatch,ttfb}_seconds | histogram | Pool contention · backend call · request-committed-to-first-byte. |

| httpjet_lsapi_generation_advances_total · _stale_{idle,checked_out}_drops_total · _stale_worker_retire_{signals,failures}_total · _worker_attribution_failures_total · _eagain_{retries,terminal_exhaustions}_total | counter | External-pool generation lifecycle and backlog pressure. |

| Proxy |

| httpjet_proxy_peer_{healthy,probes_total,health_transitions_total,active_requests,selections_total,prehead_failures_total} · httpjet_proxy_failover_total | labeled | Per-peer (scope, group, ordinal) health and selection; failovers served by a non-primary peer. |

| Logging, OTel, debug |

| httpjet_log_{access,vhost}_dropped_lines_total | counter | Unified and per-vhost log lines shed by the bounded writer queues (65,536 lines / 64 MiB per logger). |

| httpjet_otel_spans_{queue,dropped_total,exported_total,export_failed_total} · httpjet_otel_http_{exports,export_failures}_total | gauge / counter | Span queue depth and loss; collector HTTP outcomes (observable even when the collector is down). |

| httpjet_debug_cache_entries_{renders,throttled}_total | counter | Renders of the `/cache-entries` report and locally throttled requests for it. |

## The cache-entries report

`GET /cache-entries` on the metrics listener (not the main port — there it hits the vhost and 301s) renders a throttled text report: total entries and bytes, per-URL-class counts, top-N by size, a `ram: entries=… disk: bytes=…/max evictions=… swept_expired=…` line (live index count vs charged tmpfs footprint), and a health line (hits/misses/stores/purges/disk_{read,write}_err/poisoned_locks). `/__mimalloc-stats` beside it prints allocator statistics; `/debug/pprof/profile` (build feature `profiling`) returns a CPU profile — the release binary keeps its symbol table and frame pointers for exactly this. Whereas `/metrics` is open on loopback, `/cache-entries`, `/__mimalloc-stats`, `/__alloc-count` and `/debug/pprof/profile` all require `Authorization: Bearer ` matching `--profile-token-file` (returning 403 when unset or mismatched).

## Logs

          Access log  Error log  Syslog tap  Per-vhost logs

The unified access log (path from the XML; combined format with a trailing `reqid=` token) writes from a dedicated non-blocking task with a bounded queue (65,536 lines and 64 MiB per logger; `httpjet_log_access_dropped_lines_total` counts sheds), opens and rotates without following symlinks (`O_NOFOLLOW`), rolls asynchronously at 50 MB and prunes after 30 days (`HTTPJET_ACCESS_ROLLING_BYTES`, `HTTPJET_ACCESS_KEEP_DAYS`). `HTTPJET_ACCESS_LOG_FORMAT=json` emits one object per line with a fixed field order:

               access · json
```
{"ts":"17/Sep/2026:11:02:09 +0000","client_ip":"203.0.113.9","remote_user":null,"method":"GET","uri":"/threads/hello.123/","protocol":"HTTP/2.0","status":200,"bytes":41211,"referer":null,"user_agent":"Mozilla/5.0 …","reqid":"3f9c2a7b81d04e55"}
```

Unix-socket peers render the literal host `unix:`. Cache disposition is in the response header (`x-litespeed-cache`), not the log line; join on `reqid`.

The rolling `httpjet_error.log` (and captured backend stderr) is text by default. `HTTPJET_ERROR_LOG_FORMAT=json` switches to JSON events with `schema_version 1`: `timestamp_unix_ms`, `level`, nullable `target`, `message`, and a `fields` object that keeps tracing WARN/ERROR fields named rather than flattened. JSON-only redaction replaces values of authorization/cookie/password/token/secret/key/credential-named fields and suppresses whole values that look like credential syntax or URL userinfo — a conservative heuristic, not a guarantee. Bounds: 32 fields, 1024-char values, 8192-char messages; inputs over 32 KiB become `[OVERSIZED]`. The stdout/journald tracing formatter (`RUST_LOG`) is unaffected.

`HTTPJET_SYSLOG_TARGET` mirrors every rendered access line as an RFC 5424 (or 3164) datagram from the writer task — request path untouched, file logging unaffected, send failures counted. The MSG part is the rendered line itself, so existing parsers keep working. Targets: `udp://host:514`, bare `host:port`, or a unix-dgram path like `/run/systemd/journal/syslog`. Facility/severity/hostname/app-name knobs are on the CLI page .

A vhost's ` ` block with `useServer=0` and a `fileName` gives it its own access and error files (rolling size and keep-days per file; `logHeaders` 7 = combined format with request headers). Log paths are boot-owned: they cannot be changed through the write API.

## Request ids

Every request gets a 64-bit correlation id (a per-process seed mixed into a lock-free counter — no syscall, no RNG on the hot path; a background stale-while-revalidate refresh inherits its parent's id) that appears in the access, error and PHP-slow logs. `--request-id-header` also echoes it as `X-Request-Id` so a client or CDN can join a response to the server-side records. Off by default.

## Telemetry TSV and the PHP slow log

- **`--telemetry-file logs/telemetry.tsv`**: Appends a cumulative snapshot row of the in-RAM aggregates every `--telemetry-flush-secs` (30): durability across restarts and a self-contained time series (~1 MB/day). The `:9090` endpoint works without it.

- **`--php-slow-log logs/php-slow.tsv`**: A TSV line for every LSAPI request whose render TTFB exceeds `--php-slow-threshold-ms` (50), plus a 1-in-128 sample of *all* PHP requests as the population baseline — the per-URL / user-class attribution behind `httpjet_lsapi_ttfb_seconds`. Rolls at 64 MiB, gzip archives, 30-day prune.

These two files are what produced the production attribution on the Performance page: mean request 9.99 ms, of which 8.96 ms is inside PHP.

## OpenTelemetry --features otel

Build with `--features otel`, then set `HTTPJET_OTEL=1`; without it no provider or exporter is created, and requesting it in a binary without the feature fails startup. The official Rust SDK exports OTLP HTTP/protobuf to `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` (complete URL). `HTTPJET_OTEL_METRICS=1` adds a 30-second periodic metrics reader to `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT`.

> [Diagram: otel-spans] What gets exported. One root span per request at the dispatch boundary, backend client spans, internal stage spans on sampled requests, and a loss-accounted batch exporter. Spans carry status and bounded internal attributes only — no headers, bodies, URLs or error text.

- **Sampling and trust.** `HTTPJET_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO` (default 0.01) ratio-samples roots; children follow. Inbound `traceparent`/`tracestate`/`baggage` are discarded by default — clients cannot dictate parentage or force sampling. `HTTPJET_OTEL_TRUSTED_PARENTS` lists exact gateway IPs (direct peers on a known non-PROXY listener) allowed to supply a single version-00 traceparent; a listed gateway controls parentage *and sampling*, so it must strip public trace headers first. Do not list a CDN merely because it forwards client IPs.

- **Propagation.** Named configured proxy targets and WebSocket maps receive the generated traceparent; LSAPI receives it as `HTTP_TRACEPARENT`; ad-hoc targets get nothing.

- **Completion.** H1 spans end when the transport's write returns (including sendfile bodies); H2 spans ride the `ResponseCompletion` extension through flow control and the final flush; H3 spans complete when QUIC accepts the FIN. `httpjet.body.outcome` is `complete`/`error`/`cancelled` (`upgraded` for WebSocket). This is local write completion, not peer receipt.

- **Bounds.** Dedicated export thread, 2048 queued spans + one 256-span batch, 1 s interval, 2 s request timeout, 64 KiB response cap, no redirects or environment proxies, 3 s provider shutdown. Saturation drops telemetry rather than blocking serving; drops are counted on both the OTLP and Prometheus sides.

- **Metrics instruments.** `httpjet.pipeline.requests.completed` and `httpjet.pipeline.response_head.duration` (seconds, bounded status labels), plus `httpjet.otel.http.exports`.

           enable
```
HTTPJET_OTEL=1 HTTPJET_OTEL_METRICS=1 HTTPJET_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO=0.05 \
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces \
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/metrics \
httpjet --root /abs/root serve …
```

## The read-only status API

`--admin-addr 127.0.0.1:9091` exposes `GET /v1/status`: generation, configuration fingerprint, listener names, vhost names, upstream peer health/active/selection counters and page-cache aggregates — never paths, credentials or cached URLs. Full contract on Admin API & reload .

## Debugging a request

           tracing filters
```
RUST_LOG=debug,hj_rewrite=trace httpjet --root /abs/root serve --http-addr 127.0.0.1:8080 …
# where to look: vhost resolution (hj-core router) → rewrite outcome (hj-rewrite eval) →
#   cache lookup (httpjet lscache) → terminal (pipeline dispatch) → response (handler)
```

Production units run `RUST_LOG=httpjet=info`; anything you must see in the journal should log at WARN or above.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Admin API & reload (https://httpjet.net/docs/admin-api)
SUMMARY: SIGHUP reload semantics, the read-only status API, the transactional configuration API, revisions, and the restart-required boundary.
==============================================================================

# Admin API & reload

Three ways to change or inspect a running httpjet: **SIGHUP**, the opt-in **read-only status API**, and the separately authenticated **transactional configuration API**. All writers — including SIGHUP — go through one publication coordinator, so a change is either fully published as a new generation or not applied at all, and anything the process cannot safely replace at runtime is reported as `restart_required` rather than half-done.

## SIGHUP

`systemctl reload httpjet` (or `kill -HUP`) re-parses the tree, builds application state *before* touching certificate resolvers, and publishes through `config_transaction::Coordinator`. Preserved from the command line: `--no-mtls` and `--per-ip-rate` overrides. Outcomes, in the journal:

- **published**: New generation serving; in-flight requests finish on the old one; certificate handles reloaded for the unchanged listener topology.

- **requires a restart — keeping current config**: The diff touched a boot-owned resource (hot reload covers vhost/rewrite/access/expires/tuning, cache policy gates and TLS material).

- **reload would 404 mapped vhost(s)**: A per-vhost file failed to load; the old generation is kept rather than serving 404s.

- **reload rejected**: Parse or build error — nothing changes.

- **certificate reload failed**: Application state published; certificates whose reload failed are retained.

## Read-only status API

Opt in with `serve --admin-addr 127.0.0.1:9091`. Non-loopback addresses are rejected at argument parsing; a bind failure aborts startup. It is a separate listener from metrics, changes nothing, and exposes no profiling, allocation or purge operations.

           **GET** /v1/status · schema_version 1
```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9091/v1/status | jq .
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "generation": 3,                       # process-local, starts at 1; rejected candidates stay invisible
  "config_fingerprint": "sha256:…",      # of the normalized model's Debug form — comparable within one binary version only
  "listeners": [{"name":"https","tls":true,"unix":false}],   # configured names + flags, NOT bound addresses
  "vhosts": ["example.test"],
  "upstreams": [{"scope":"server","group":"application","peers":[{"ordinal":0,"healthy":true,"active":2,"selections":1290}]}],
  "page_cache": {"entries": 41210, "memory_bytes": 60817408, "hits": 1904411, "misses": 88123},   # or null when off
  "truncated": false
}
```

No configuration values, paths, credentials, request headers, session keys or cached URLs are returned. Names are limited to 256 characters and each collection to 256 rows; the response is capped at 1 MiB (503 beyond). Only GET at the exact path (405/404 otherwise); Host must be a loopback socket authority or `localhost`; Origin headers and request bodies are rejected; `Cache-Control: no-store`; every connection closes; 4 KiB/32 header fields; four concurrent tasks with five-second deadlines. Local users are trusted — this is not an authentication boundary between users on the same host, and it must never be reverse-proxied.

## Transactional configuration API

Writable access is a separate, explicit opt-in that never becomes available merely because the read-only listener is on. Three options are required together:

           **serve** · enabling writes
```
httpjet --root /abs/root serve … \
  --admin-write-addr 127.0.0.1:9092 \
  --admin-token-file /operator/private/token \       # 64 lowercase hex chars (32 random bytes), mode 0400/0600, one hard link, root or service uid
  --admin-resource-root /operator/content \          # repeatable; up to 32 existing directories; "/" is refused
  --admin-resource-root /etc/letsencrypt/live
```

> [Diagram: reload-transaction] Validate, then publish with an exact precondition. Every write carries If-Match with the revision it read; a stale revision or an out-of-band publication (SIGHUP included) loses with a conflict rather than silently rebuilding against newer state. Publication is volatile: the on-disk XML is never rewritten and a restart returns to it.

### Endpoints and contract

| Request | Behavior |

| `GET /v1/revision` | The current revision: a random 128-bit process incarnation plus a monotonic generation, so a restart can never revive an earlier process's revision. |

| `POST /v1/config/validate` | Builds the candidate, returns a redacted verdict, publishes and persists nothing. |

| `PUT /v1/config` | Builds, rechecks the exact revision under the publication boundary, publishes, transfers health-check ownership, notifies bridge admission. Returns the next revision and `persistence: volatile`. An interrupted response after publication does not roll back — re-read the revision to reconcile. |

Framing: `Authorization: Bearer ` (missing/duplicate/malformed → 401 without reading the body; constant-time digest compare; nothing about the token in Debug, logs or responses), exact quoted `If-Match` (missing → 428; stale → conflict), `Content-Type: application/json`, one positive `Content-Length` ≤ 1 MiB, headers ≤ 8 KiB/32 fields, five-second combined deadline, Host equal to the bound loopback address or `localhost: `; transfer/content encodings, Origin, Expect, Upgrade and Trailer are rejected; one request per connection, never pipelined. At most four connections and one candidate build; writer-lock acquisition is bounded at 5 s and candidate waiting at 10 s — a timed-out build keeps its admission permit until it exits and can never publish after its caller stopped waiting.

           **body** · the in-memory bundle (exactly three fields)
```
{
  "server_xml": " … ",
  "vhosts": [ {"name": "example.test", "xml": " … "} ],
  "mime": "text/html = html, htm\n"
}
```

`hj-config::parse_bundle` normalizes the bundle without ever reading the submitted `configFile` paths: 1 MiB aggregate, ≤128 vhosts, one root element per document, no DTD, ≤64 nesting levels, missing/extra/duplicate declarations fatal, diagnostics suppressed, errors carry no submitted data. The server root always comes from startup.

### What a transaction may change

#### Reloadable (application)

- Listener→vhost mappings on the unchanged listener set
- Rewrites, document roots, contexts, static locations
- Reloadable request settings, cache policy gates, expires
- Proxy processors and groups (health schedulers restart cleanly)
- GeoIP database and upstream client-cert files — inside a resource root

#### Constrained trust (TCP transaction)

- Listener identity/routing, PROXY-protocol policy, TLS certificate/key/CA/CRL material — through prepared same-socket TCP successors
- An existing `--http-uds` endpoint is handed off
- An already-enabled QUIC endpoint adopts the new TLS/mTLS policy for future handshakes without rebinding UDP
- UDS ext-processor addresses authorized against resource roots

#### restart_required

- Listener addresses, count, order, secure/plain roles; QUIC enablement; UDS topology
- PHP topology and pools; non-proxy processors
- Cache-store identity and boot-time cache caps/policy
- User/group, namespace and isolation settings, per-vhost log resources
- `useIpInProxyHeader` and the whole ` ` block

**Resource policy.** Every filesystem reference in a candidate (vhost roots, docroots, static contexts, GeoIP file, upstream client certs, TCP certificate/key/CA/CRL paths) must resolve inside one of the operator's `--admin-resource-root` directories: parent traversal, relative paths, missing resources and symlinks resolving outside the roots are rejected at submission time. This is authorization, not a sandbox — roots and their symlinks stay operator-controlled. Failures return bounded categories, never configuration values.

**Cache namespaces.** The first successful publication introduces a response-cache epoch; every later generation keys page-cache and memo entries by epoch + generation, so a late render from an old generation cannot overwrite a new entry and a previous document root's memoized response cannot replay. See Page cache → generations .

**Shutdown.** Closing the coordinator precedes cancelling serving; a prepared candidate receives `Closed` and cannot reactivate probes; the write listener drops its connection tasks. Blocking candidate work cannot be forcibly stopped by tokio, so use responsive local resource files — the ten-second deadline bounds the caller's wait, not an uninterruptible filesystem call.

## The reload boundary in depth

Live state is a *resource generation*: application state plus references to listener generations, each with immutable bind, PROXY-protocol and TLS-verification policy, a resource identity, and separately owned accept/drain control. Connections pin their trust generation at acceptance (`CoreHandler` reads a trust-epoch-aware `ServingView`, pinned again at TCP/UDS accept and per QUIC connection). Compatible application reloads stay visible to existing connections; an incompatible trust change retires the old listener group — H2 gets GOAWAY, H1 closes after its current response, H3 stops admitting streams while preserving connection IDs through a bounded drain — rather than letting an old unauthenticated connection reach newly protected routes.

| Resource | Owner | Replacement rule |

| TCP addresses, worker count, inherited fds | listener plan + `uring` worker groups | Prepared successors on the same sockets behind an activation barrier; kernel socket identities verified; raced accepts transferred to the successor. |

| UDS path and permissions | listener adoption | Stage a distinct owned path; never unlink an inherited or unrelated socket; retain the old inode until retirement. |

| TLS acceptor, mTLS requirement, PROXY binding | per-core TLS bridge | Pinned to one listener generation per connection. |

| Certificates / SNI map | `CertReloadHandle` | Validated snapshots published as one trust-generation handle; multi-resource swaps are not advertised as atomic. |

| QUIC endpoint / UDP fds | process-persistent `QuicResources` | UDP ownership stable; a shared policy handle replaces quinn's server config for future handshakes; a stale policy rejects new handshakes once its epoch is no longer current. |

| kTLS template | TLS worker | New templates apply to new handshakes; existing key schedules are connection-owned. |

| ACME overlays, OCSP staple slots | feature runtimes | Certificate targets owned by resource generation; refresh leases retained through retirement. |

| PHP supervisor / external worker registry | startup | Restart-required. |

| Log writers, cache budgets, body budget, metrics, bridge admission | process-owned Arcs | Retained across reloads; outstanding reservations preserved. |

| User/group, privileges, namespaces, systemd topology | startup | Never acquired at runtime; rejected before any resource acquisition. |

Acquisition order for a TCP trust transaction: authenticate and check the revision → derive the resource diff with unchanged resources retained by identity → acquire candidate-only resources with every descriptor, thread and pending side effect owned on creation → start candidate workers behind an activation barrier (readiness proves adoption, not permission to serve) → validate the complete bundle (failure drops and joins everything) → recheck the revision under the coordinator's publication/close boundary and publish atomically — no fallible resource creation after that point → activate and stop old acceptors → retire old generations outside the publication lock, bounded.

## Reproducible checks

           **tests** · isolated loopback listeners and temporary trees
```
cargo test --locked -p httpjet admin
python3 -B scripts/admin-runtime-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet                       # served-file replacement, validate-only non-mutation, stale writes, SIGHUP restoration, restart incarnation
python3 -B scripts/admin-runtime-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet --memo-parity         # 48-cell memo parity across a publication
python3 -B scripts/admin-runtime-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet --persistent-cache    # authenticated on-disk containers, hits across publication, boot-scan restoration
```

==============================================================================
PAGE: Extending httpjet (https://httpjet.net/docs/extensions)
SUMMARY: Compile-time extension hooks, the bounded WAF sidecar contract, and why there is no dynamic plugin ABI.
==============================================================================

# Extending httpjet

Two extension points, each with a deliberately narrow contract: **compile-time extensions** — trusted Rust crates linked into a custom build that register read-only pre-handlers and response transforms — and the **WAF sidecar**, a bounded loopback HTTP inspection call for an independently deployed engine. There is no dynamic plugin ABI and no in-process sandbox, on purpose.

## Compile-time extensions

`hj-extension::ExtensionRegistry` is assembled at the binary's registration point, `crates/httpjet/src/extensions.rs`. The distributed binary registers nothing, so the facility is inert unless an operator maintains a custom build. It is a *source-level* compatibility contract over the frozen `hj-core` types, not a stable native ABI.

           **extensions.rs** · registration
```
pub(crate) fn compiled_registry() -> hj_extension::ExtensionRegistry {
    let mut registry = hj_extension::ExtensionRegistry::new();
    registry.register_pre_handler("company.request-policy", company_policy::hook()).expect("unique");
    registry.register_response_transform("company.headers", company_headers::transform()).expect("unique");
    registry
}
```

Registration order is execution order. Names are globally unique, 1–64 bytes of lowercase ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`. Registered extensions are logged once at boot; changing them means rebuilding and restarting, and SIGHUP carries the same linked registry into the next generation. Extension settings belong to the extension crate — the registry does not reinterpret LiteSpeed XML and exposes no runtime loader.

> [Diagram: extension-hooks] Where hooks run. Pre-handlers run after trust and access resolution but before everything that could serve a byte; response transforms run after dispatch (and after page-cache storage) but before httpjet's own transforms, so an extension changes egress, not the canonical cached object, and is re-applied on hits.

### Pre-handler contract

A `PreHandler` receives an immutable `ReqCtx` and a `RequestView` exposing only method, URI and headers — no body, no mutable parts. It returns `Continue` (next hook, then built-in dispatch), `Respond(response)` (skip remaining hooks and dispatch; normal transforms, metrics, request-id handling and access logging still run), or `Err(HandlerError)` (fail closed to that status and log the named failure). Pre-handlers never see reserved operational routes intercepted before vhost dispatch (ACME challenges, loopback cache endpoints) or requests rejected before the hook boundary. **Any registered pre-handler disables the on-core memo/cache/static fast path**, because that synchronous path cannot run async hooks; response-only extensions keep it.

### Response-transform contract

Registered `ResponseTransform`s run in order on every full-pipeline response and every on-core cache/static response, before the host's static promotion, expires, sub_filter, compression, redirect-cache guard and Alt-Svc transforms — so an extension sees the origin representation before compression and cannot bypass the final transport-header policy by ordering. There is no error return: keep work bounded and express fallible initialization at registration.

        !   In-process means full authority
Extension code runs with httpjet's memory and filesystem authority. A panic, deadlock, unbounded allocation or blocking call affects the server. Only trusted, reviewed crates belong in the registry.

## WAF sidecar

httpjet embeds no rules engine and the ignored LiteSpeed `lsrecaptcha`/`censorshipControl` elements stay inactive. Instead, `--waf-sidecar-addr` turns on a bounded inspection call to a local HTTP service over a Unix socket (`unix:/path`, peer UID verified via `SO_PEERCRED` against `--waf-sidecar-uid`) or loopback TCP (`ip:port`) — the integration point for an existing maintained engine such as a Coraza/OWASP CRS adapter. httpjet does not claim CRS compatibility; the adapter owns the translation from the stable inspection document to its engine's model.

           **serve** · sidecar flags
```
--waf-sidecar-addr unix:/run/waf/inspect.sock   # or loopback 127.0.0.1:19090; absent = seam inert
--waf-sidecar-uid 0                   # uid a unix: sidecar must run as (default: root or serving uid)
--waf-sidecar-path /inspect           # absolute, no control characters
--waf-timeout-ms 100                  # total deadline: admission + allowance + connect + write + parse (≤ 30 s)
--waf-body-max 65536                  # bodies at or below this are sent as body_hex (≤ 1 MiB)
--waf-concurrency 128                 # ≤ 4096
--waf-fail-open                       # weaker policy: continue on sidecar failure (every bypass is logged; 403 still blocks)
```

> [Diagram: waf-sidecar] One inspection per request. Inspection runs after URI decoding/normalization and body-limit enforcement but before rewrite, cache lookup and any backend — background cache refreshes go through the same dispatch and are inspected too. Only two replies are valid; everything else is a sidecar failure.

- **Document.** `version: 1`, method, normalized path, query, resolved vhost, resolved client IP, protocol, effective TLS state, all request headers. Header values and the body are lowercase hexadecimal so raw bytes are lossless and cannot inject log or protocol controls; adapters must reject unsupported versions.

- **Bodies.** ≤ `--waf-body-max` → `body_hex`, restored byte-identically for downstream processing; larger → `body_omitted: true` and the sidecar must decide that shape explicitly. The global request limit stays authoritative.

- **Memory.** Beyond the concurrency cap, all generations share a 64 MiB serialization budget; each inspection reserves a byte-weighted allowance before creating hex/JSON copies, so stalled inspections cannot multiply temporary heap up to the concurrency limit. Waiting for the allowance is inside the deadline and follows the fail policy.

- **Transport.** One close-delimited HTTP/1.1 POST per inspection, never reused (no response-boundary ambiguity); response head ≤ 4 KiB; duplicate/nonzero Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, malformed status, EOF and any status other than 204/403 are failures.

           **tests**
```
cargo test -p httpjet --bin httpjet pipeline::e2e::waf_runs_before_static_cache_and_can_block_a_previously_allowed_path
cargo test -p httpjet --bin httpjet pipeline::e2e::waf_sidecar_failure_policy_is_closed_unless_explicitly_opened
cargo test -p hj-extension
```

## Why there is no dynamic or sandboxed plugin ABI

httpjet does not `dlopen` third-party trait objects: Rust promises no stable trait-object ABI across independently built shared libraries, and a native module would share allocator, signal, thread and process authority with the server. There is no current requirement to execute untrusted third-party code, so a WASM runtime and its dependency and attack surface are not included. Untrusted or independently deployed inspection belongs behind the bounded sidecar contract above. If an untrusted-plugin workload appears, it must first define capabilities, memory and fuel limits, deadline and cancellation behavior, body access, state and network permissions, version negotiation, and fail-open/closed semantics — only then would an isolation mechanism be selected.
